  • Warranty Policy
  • Shipping and Delivery Policy
  • Vendor Code of Conduct
  • Customer Grievance Redressal Policy

title: Warranty Policy
html:
DRAFT — LEGAL REVIEW REQUIRED. This document is an operational or legal draft and must be reviewed and approved by authorized management and, where required, qualified legal counsel before becoming effective.

Purpose

This policy states what warranty cover exists for goods sold by PlantAtHome, a brand of Silvestrix Green LLP, and how a customer claims it. PlantAtHome sells across categories that carry very different cover: a powered sprayer arrives with a manufacturer warranty card, a terracotta pot has none, and a living plant cannot carry one at all because its survival depends on care after delivery. The policy prevents agents from promising cover that does not exist and gives customers a single place to see what applies to what they bought.

Scope

Applies to all goods sold through PlantAtHome web and app channels and delivered in India, whether fulfilled from PlantAtHome inventory or by an approved nursery vendor, and to all support, operations and vendor management staff handling warranty enquiries. It also applies to corporate gifting orders except where a signed contract states otherwise. It does not cover the short post-delivery window for damaged, incorrect or dead-on-arrival goods, which is governed by the Replacement Policy.

Definitions

  • Manufacturer warranty — a commitment given by the brand that made the product, on terms printed on its pack or warranty card, honoured by the manufacturer or its authorised service network.
  • Pass-through warranty — PlantAtHome delivering the manufacturer's warranty documentation and assisting the customer in reaching the service network, without becoming the warrantor.
  • Manufacturing defect — a fault present in the item when made or packed, distinct from damage caused after delivery.
  • Replacement window — the short period after delivery in which a claim may be raised under the Replacement Policy.
  • Consumable part — a component designed to wear out and be replaced in normal use, such as a blade, nozzle, filter, seal, battery or bulb.

Policy Statement

PlantAtHome does not manufacture the goods it sells and issues no warranty of its own beyond the statutory rights of the consumer and the replacement cover described in the Replacement Policy. Where a product carries a manufacturer warranty, PlantAtHome passes it through in full and assists the customer in raising it. Live plants and other perishable goods carry no conventional warranty, because their condition after delivery depends on watering, light, placement and season. Cover periods, assistance windows and category rules are held in the currently approved Warranty Configuration.

Responsibilities

RoleAccountability
Catalogue and MerchandisingRecords the correct warranty position on every listing before it is published
Customer SupportIdentifies the applicable cover, responds within {{support_response_sla}} and does not promise cover outside the configuration
OperationsEnsures warranty cards, serial records and invoices ship with the goods and are retrievable afterwards
Vendor ManagementRequires vendors to supply genuine, warranty-bearing stock and to honour defect claims within {{vendor_acceptance_sla}}

Policy Requirements

CategoryWarranty positionHonoured byClaim route
Powered gardening equipment such as trimmers, sprayers and pumpsManufacturer warranty on the terms printed on the pack or cardManufacturer or its authorised service centreService centre, with PlantAtHome assistance for the period in the currently approved Warranty Configuration
Electronics and electricals such as grow lights, timers and moisture metersManufacturer warranty on the terms printed on the packManufacturerService centre, with PlantAtHome assistance as above
Non-powered hand toolsNo conventional warranty; manufacturing defect cover onlyPlantAtHome or the fulfilling vendorReplacement claim within {{replacement_evidence_window}}
Pots, planters and ceramicsNo conventional warranty; defect and transit damage cover at delivery onlyPlantAtHome or the fulfilling vendorReplacement claim within {{replacement_evidence_window}}
Live plantsNo conventional warranty; survival after delivery is care-dependentPlantAtHome or the fulfilling vendorReplacement claim within {{live_plant_claim_window}}
SeedsNo germination warranty beyond the lot details declared on the packSeed producerAs per the currently approved Warranty Configuration
Fertilizers and consumablesSealed-pack integrity and the labelled shelf life onlyManufacturerClaim within {{replacement_evidence_window}}
FarmBox fresh producePerishable; no warranty of any kindPlantAtHomeFreshness claim on the day of delivery, as per the currently approved Warranty Configuration

Exclusions across all categories

  • Normal wear, cosmetic marks acquired in use, and consumable parts.
  • Damage from misuse, dropping, voltage fluctuation, water ingress beyond the rated protection, or use of a consumer-grade tool for commercial work.
  • Repair, opening or modification by anyone other than the manufacturer's authorised service network, and removed or defaced serial numbers.
  • Plant decline caused by over-watering or under-watering, unsuitable light, repotting, weather, pets, or pests introduced after delivery.
  • Natural variation in living goods and in handmade items, as described in the Replacement Policy.
  • Goods not purchased through PlantAtHome channels, and claims without a retrievable order or invoice reference.

Procedures

  1. The customer contacts PlantAtHome through {{support_channels}} with the order reference and a description of the fault, or approaches the manufacturer's service network directly.
  2. Support confirms the category position from the table above and states plainly whether cover is a manufacturer warranty, defect cover, or none.
  3. For manufacturer warranty items, Support supplies the invoice, serial or batch details and the nearest authorised service contact within {{support_response_sla}}, and tracks the case to closure within {{support_resolution_sla}}.
  4. For defect cover items, the claim is processed under the Replacement Policy, including its evidence requirements.
  5. Where a vendor supplied the goods, the vendor confirms within {{vendor_acceptance_sla}} and bears the cost of a proven manufacturing defect.
  6. Where the manufacturer accepts a defect but cannot repair or replace, any refund is approved within {{approval_limit_refund}} and processed within {{refund_processing_time}}.
  7. Declined claims are answered in writing with the reason and the escalation route, which follows {{escalation_timeline}}.
  8. Warranty correspondence and decisions are retained for {{data_retention_period}}.

Exceptions

Corporate gifting and institutional contracts may carry different service terms; those terms prevail where signed. Extended cover offered by a manufacturer or a third-party plan is a contract between that provider and the customer, and PlantAtHome's role remains assistance only. Goodwill resolutions outside this policy require management approval within {{approval_limit_refund}}, must be logged as goodwill, and set no precedent.

Compliance

Listings must describe warranty cover accurately and must not imply cover that the manufacturer does not give, consistent with the Consumer Protection Act, 2019 and the Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020. Nothing in this policy restricts a consumer's statutory rights. Tax documents supporting a warranty claim are issued in line with {{gst_invoice_timeline}}. This policy is reviewed at {{review_frequency_default}} and whenever a supplier changes its warranty terms.

Violations

Claims supported by falsified invoices, altered serial numbers or third-party goods are rejected and may lead to account restriction and recovery of amounts already paid. Vendors who supply goods without the promised warranty documentation, or who refuse valid defect claims, are subject to {{penalty_schedule}} and may be suspended from the catalogue. Staff who state warranty cover beyond the configuration, or who commit PlantAtHome as warrantor, are dealt with under internal disciplinary procedure.

Related Documents

  • Replacement Policy
  • Return and Refund Policy
  • Shipping and Delivery Policy
  • Customer Grievance Redressal Policy

title: Gift Card Policy
related_titles: Fraud Prevention and Risk Management Policy
html:
DRAFT — LEGAL REVIEW REQUIRED. This document is an operational or legal draft and must be reviewed and approved by authorized management and, where required, qualified legal counsel before becoming effective.

Purpose

This policy governs gift cards issued by PlantAtHome, a brand of Silvestrix Green LLP: how they are created and sold, how they are redeemed, what happens to an unspent balance, and how misuse is prevented. Gift cards are stored value, so they attract fraud and create obligations that outlive the sale. The policy sets one consistent treatment for purchased cards and for promotional cards issued free, so that support agents, finance and customers all read the same rules.

Scope

Applies to all PlantAtHome gift cards, digital or printed, issued through the website, app, support team, or a corporate gifting arrangement, and to all staff who issue, adjust or cancel them. It covers redemption against live plants, pots and planters, tools, seeds, fertilizers, accessories, FarmBox produce and corporate gifting orders. It does not cover discount coupons, cashback, loyalty points or referral credit, which are governed separately.

Definitions

  • Gift card — a code carrying a stored monetary value redeemable against PlantAtHome orders.
  • Purchased gift card — a card issued against consideration actually paid by a purchaser.
  • Promotional gift card — a card issued without consideration, as a campaign reward, goodwill gesture or service compensation.
  • Activation — the point at which an issued card becomes redeemable, following successful payment settlement or campaign approval.
  • Remaining balance — the unspent value held against a card after one or more redemptions.
  • Beneficiary — the person holding the code and redeeming it, who may differ from the purchaser.

Policy Statement

A gift card is a prepaid instrument redeemable only for goods sold by PlantAtHome. It is not a bank deposit, carries no interest, and is not exchangeable for cash except where applicable law requires it. Purchased cards are activated only after payment settles. Promotional cards are issued under an approved campaign and are subject to the restrictions that campaign declares. Denominations, validity, redemption limits and combinability are held in the currently approved Gift Card Configuration and are not restated here.

Responsibilities

RoleAccountability
FinanceOwns the outstanding gift card liability, reconciles issuance against redemption, and approves cancellations above {{approval_limit_refund}}
MarketingDefines promotional campaigns and their restrictions before any promotional card is issued
Customer SupportHandles balance, expiry and lost-card enquiries within {{support_response_sla}} and never discloses a full code to an unverified caller
Risk and TechnologyMonitors redemption patterns using {{risk_scoring_model}}, reviews flagged activity at {{risk_review_frequency}} and holds suspect codes

Policy Requirements

AttributePurchased gift cardPromotional gift card
ConsiderationPaid in full by the purchaser before activationNone; issued under an approved campaign or as compensation
ValidityNot less than the minimum validity prescribed for prepaid instruments under applicable Reserve Bank of India directions, as set in the currently approved Gift Card ConfigurationAs per the currently approved Gift Card Configuration and the campaign terms
TransferableYes, by sharing the code with a beneficiaryNo; tied to the account it was issued to
Partial redemptionPermitted; the remaining balance stays on the code until validity endsPermitted unless the campaign declares single use
Refundable to cashNo, except on cancellation within {{cancellation_window}} or where law requiresNo
Combinable with offers or other cardsAs per the currently approved Gift Card ConfigurationAs per the currently approved Gift Card Configuration
Reissue if lostYes, on identity verification, for the unredeemed balanceAt management discretion; not guaranteed

Gift cards cannot be used to buy other gift cards, and cannot be redeemed for cash, credited to a bank account or used to settle amounts owed to PlantAtHome outside an order. Cards are accepted only in cities and categories currently serviceable at the time of checkout.

Procedures

Issuance and purchase

  1. The purchaser selects a denomination from the configuration, names a beneficiary and pays through Razorpay; the card activates only after settlement is confirmed.
  2. The code and its terms are delivered to the beneficiary over WhatsApp, email or SMS, and a purchase record is written against the purchaser's account.
  3. Promotional cards are issued only from an approved campaign record naming its restrictions, validity and issuing authority.

Redemption and balance

  1. The beneficiary applies the code at checkout; the value is applied to the order total and any shortfall is paid by another method.
  2. Where the order value is lower than the card value, the remaining balance is retained on the same code and is visible to the account holder.
  3. Where an order paid partly by gift card is cancelled or refunded, the gift card portion returns to the same code with its original validity, and only the portion paid by another method returns to that method within {{refund_processing_time}}.
  4. A tax invoice is issued for the underlying goods at redemption, in line with {{gst_invoice_timeline}}.

Lost, stolen, fraud and cancellation

  1. The purchaser or beneficiary reports loss through {{support_channels}}; Support verifies identity against the issuing order and blocks the code immediately.
  2. Value already redeemed before the block cannot be recovered; only the unredeemed balance may be reissued.
  3. Codes showing bulk redemption, mismatched devices or chargeback-linked purchases are frozen pending review under {{risk_scoring_model}}, and the holder is informed of the reason and the escalation route per {{escalation_timeline}}.
  4. A purchaser may cancel an unredeemed purchased card within {{cancellation_window}}; refunds are approved within {{approval_limit_refund}} and {{refund_approval_sla}} and processed within {{refund_processing_time}} to the original payment method.
  5. Issuance, redemption, adjustment and cancellation events are logged with the acting user and retained for {{data_retention_period}}. Beneficiary contact details are handled under the privacy notice, with subject requests answered within {{dsr_response_time}}.

Exceptions

Corporate gifting arrangements may use bulk-issued cards with contract-specific denominations, validity and reporting; those terms prevail where signed. Extension of an expired card, or reinstatement of a frozen one, requires management approval within {{approval_limit_refund}}, must be logged with reasons, and creates no precedent.

Compliance

Gift cards are issued and operated to be consistent with applicable Reserve Bank of India directions on prepaid payment instruments, the Consumer Protection Act, 2019 and the Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020, including clear disclosure of validity and restrictions before purchase. Outstanding balances are carried as a liability and reconciled by Finance at {{review_frequency_default}}, at which point this policy is reviewed alongside the configuration.

Violations

Obtaining, reselling or redeeming gift cards through stolen payment instruments, chargeback-reversed purchases, code enumeration or campaign abuse leads to cancellation of the codes, reversal of affected orders, restriction of the account and, where warranted, referral to law enforcement. Staff who issue, extend or adjust gift card value outside an approved campaign or beyond {{approval_limit_refund}}, or who share codes with anyone other than a verified holder, are dealt with under internal disciplinary procedure.

Related Documents

  • Return and Refund Policy
  • Replacement Policy
  • Customer Grievance Redressal Policy
  • Fraud Prevention and Risk Management Policy

title: Promotional Policy
html:
DRAFT — LEGAL REVIEW REQUIRED. This document is an operational or legal draft and must be reviewed and approved by authorized management and, where required, qualified legal counsel before becoming effective.

Purpose

This policy sets out how PlantAtHome, a brand of Silvestrix Green LLP, designs, publishes, applies, monitors and withdraws promotional offers. It exists so that a customer sees the same offer terms wherever the offer appears, so that support staff can resolve a disputed discount without improvising, and so that every rupee of discount is traceable to a configured, approved campaign rather than to an individual decision.

Scope

This policy applies to all promotional mechanics offered under the PlantAtHome brand: coupon codes, automatically applied cart discounts, category and vertical offers, free shipping offers, bundle and combo pricing, seasonal campaigns, first-order offers, referral offers and corporate gifting quotations. It covers the website, the mobile app, WhatsApp Business, email and SMS campaigns, and applies equally to orders fulfilled directly and to orders fulfilled by approved nursery vendors. It applies to all employees, contractors and agencies who create, publish or communicate an offer on behalf of PlantAtHome.

Definitions

  • Promotion Engine — the system of record in which every offer, its eligibility rules and its limits are configured and evaluated at checkout.
  • Promotion Configuration — the currently approved set of values in the Promotion Engine for a given campaign, including minimum order value, discount cap, usage limits, applicable catalogue and campaign period.
  • Promotion Code — an alphanumeric code a customer enters to claim an offer, whether public or restricted to named accounts.
  • Stacking — the application of more than one promotion to the same order or the same line item.
  • Campaign Period — the start and end timestamps between which an offer is valid, as set in the Promotion Configuration.
  • Order Value — the value of eligible items before shipping charges and applicable taxes, unless the Promotion Configuration states otherwise for a specific campaign.

Policy Statement

All discounts are granted through the Promotion Engine. No employee, vendor or agency may offer, promise or apply a discount outside it. Where an offer is advertised, the advertised terms and the configured terms must be identical; if they diverge, the offer is suspended and corrected rather than honoured selectively. Promotions are commercial invitations, not entitlements: PlantAtHome may modify, suspend or withdraw any promotion prospectively, but will honour a validly claimed discount on an order already confirmed and paid.

Responsibilities

RoleResponsibility
MarketingDrafts the campaign brief, customer-facing terms and creative; owns the accuracy of every published claim.
Category / CatalogueConfirms the eligible product set, stock position and that discounted pricing remains commercially viable per SKU.
FinanceApproves the discount exposure and confirms tax and invoicing treatment before publication.
EngineeringImplements and tests the Promotion Configuration and ensures the checkout displays the discount and the final payable amount.
Customer SupportApplies the configured terms to customer queries and escalates suspected misuse or misconfiguration.
Vendor OperationsConfirms settlement treatment for vendor-fulfilled items, per the currently approved Vendor Settlement Configuration.

Policy Requirements

Every promotion must carry a complete configuration before it is published. The following attributes are mandatory; their values are held in the Promotion Engine and are never restated as fixed text in customer communication except by reference to the live offer terms.

AttributeRequirementSource of value
EligibilityCustomer segment, account status, city serviceability and first-order statusAs per the currently approved Promotion Configuration
Minimum order valueEvaluated on eligible items onlyAs per the currently approved Promotion Configuration
Maximum discountAbsolute cap applied after percentage calculationAs per the currently approved Promotion Configuration
Free shippingApplied where the order qualifies{{free_shipping_threshold}}
Usage limitsPer code, per customer and per campaignAs per the currently approved Promotion Configuration
StackingDisallowed unless a campaign is explicitly configured as combinableAs per the currently approved Promotion Configuration
Campaign periodStart and end timestamps, Indian Standard TimeAs per the currently approved Promotion Configuration
Catalogue scopeNamed SKUs, categories or verticals; exclusions listed explicitlyAs per the currently approved Promotion Configuration

Offers apply only to in-stock, serviceable items. Live plants, FarmBox produce and vendor-listed items may be excluded from a campaign where stock or freshness cannot be assured. A promotion never overrides delivery serviceability: if a pin code is not serviceable, no offer makes it so. Discounts are shown on the tax invoice in the manner required for GST reporting, and the invoice is issued within {{gst_invoice_timeline}}.

Procedures

  1. Marketing raises a campaign brief stating the objective, mechanic, audience and intended catalogue scope.
  2. Category and Finance review commercial viability and approve the exposure within {{approval_limit_expense}}.
  3. Engineering configures the offer in the Promotion Engine and tests it on a live-like cart, including a negative test that the offer correctly fails when eligibility is not met.
  4. Marketing publishes creative only after the configuration is live and verified; published terms link to the offer terms held in the Promotion Engine.
  5. Redemption, discount exposure and misuse signals are monitored through the campaign period and reviewed at {{review_frequency_default}}.
  6. At campaign end the offer is expired in the Promotion Engine and the code is retired; expired codes are never silently re-enabled under the same name.

Exceptions

A goodwill discount or service-recovery credit outside an active campaign may be issued only through a configured service-recovery mechanic, on a named order, with a recorded reason, and within {{approval_limit_refund}}. Corporate gifting and bulk quotations are priced under a written quotation rather than a public promotion code; such quotations are not combinable with public offers. Any other exception requires written approval from authorised management before it is communicated to a customer.

Compliance

Promotional communication must comply with the Consumer Protection Act, 2019 and the Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020, including the prohibition on misleading advertisements and on advertising goods that cannot be supplied. Savings claims must be measured against a price at which the item was genuinely offered. Marketing messages over WhatsApp, email and SMS are sent only to recipients with a valid basis for contact and always carry a working opt-out. Records of campaign approvals, configurations and redemption reports are retained for {{data_retention_period}}.

Violations

Codes obtained by bulk automated collection, credential sharing, fake or duplicate accounts, repeated order-and-return cycling, or resale of restricted codes constitute misuse. Where misuse is identified, PlantAtHome may decline the discount, cancel the affected order before dispatch, recover the discount value from a refund, and restrict the account from future promotions. Staff who apply discounts outside the Promotion Engine, or who publish terms not matching the configuration, are subject to disciplinary action under the applicable HR policy. Suspected fraud may be reported to the relevant authorities.

title: Loyalty Policy
html:
DRAFT — LEGAL REVIEW REQUIRED. This document is an operational or legal draft and must be reviewed and approved by authorized management and, where required, qualified legal counsel before becoming effective.

Purpose

This policy establishes the framework under which PlantAtHome, a brand of Silvestrix Green LLP, would operate a customer loyalty programme. It is written in advance of launch so that the commercial, accounting, privacy and fraud questions are settled before any customer is invited to earn a reward, and so that no team ships a points mechanic without an agreed ruleset behind it.

Scope

The PlantAtHome loyalty programme is not currently active. No points are being earned, held or redeemed, no tiers exist, and no customer holds a loyalty balance with PlantAtHome. Nothing in this document creates a present entitlement, a promise to launch, or a right to any reward. This policy applies from the date a loyalty programme is formally approved and launched, and would then cover the website, the mobile app and any linked channel, across all verticals: live plants, gardening tools, pots and planters, seeds, fertilizers, accessories, FarmBox fresh produce and corporate gifting.

Definitions

  • Programme — a loyalty scheme operated by PlantAtHome under this policy, once approved and launched.
  • Points — a non-monetary unit of account recorded against a customer account, redeemable only as described in the Loyalty Programme Configuration.
  • Tier — a customer status band determining earn rate and benefits.
  • Qualifying Spend — the net value of delivered, non-returned, non-cancelled eligible items, excluding shipping, taxes and any amount paid using Points.
  • Loyalty Programme Configuration — the currently approved set of values governing earn rates, tier thresholds, expiry, redemption limits and reward catalogue.

Policy Statement

PlantAtHome will not launch a loyalty programme until this policy is approved, the earn and burn liability is accounted for, and the programme is implemented in the platform as a system of record. Points, if introduced, are a promotional benefit and not money: they carry no cash value, cannot be purchased, transferred, gifted, sold or bequeathed, and are not property of the customer. Because Points represent a future obligation, the Programme will at all times be governed by a configuration under Finance approval rather than by ad hoc marketing decisions.

Responsibilities

RoleResponsibility
Authorised managementApproves the launch, the Loyalty Programme Configuration and any material change to earn or redemption economics.
FinanceAccounts for the outstanding Points liability, approves earn rates and reviews breakage at {{review_frequency_default}}.
MarketingOwns tier design, reward catalogue and all customer communication about the Programme.
EngineeringImplements the ledger, ensures every accrual and redemption is an auditable entry, and prevents balance changes outside the ledger.
Customer SupportAnswers balance and redemption queries within {{support_response_sla}} and escalates suspected abuse.
Risk and ComplianceReviews fraud controls and privacy impact at {{risk_review_frequency}}.

Policy Requirements

Should the Programme launch, the following attributes must be configured and published before enrolment opens. Values are held in the Loyalty Programme Configuration and are never fixed in prose.

AttributeRuleSource of value
Earn basisPoints accrue on Qualifying Spend only, after delivery is confirmedAs per the currently approved Loyalty Programme Configuration
Tier thresholdsAssessed on a rolling qualifying period per accountAs per the currently approved Loyalty Programme Configuration
Redemption minimum and capMinimum redeemable balance and maximum share of an order payable in PointsAs per the currently approved Loyalty Programme Configuration
Points expiryExpiry on inactivity, with advance notice to the customerAs per the currently approved Loyalty Programme Configuration
Reversal on returnPoints earned on a returned or cancelled item are reversed; Points spent are restored{{return_request_window}} and {{refund_processing_time}}
Excluded categoriesCorporate gifting, bulk orders and specified vendor-fulfilled items may be excludedAs per the currently approved Loyalty Programme Configuration
Stacking with promotionsCombination with promotional codes governed by the promotion rulesAs per the currently approved Promotion Configuration

Points accrue to one verified account identified by a single verified mobile number. Balances may not be merged, pooled across households, or moved between accounts. Points may not be redeemed for cash, converted to a bank transfer, or refunded as money; where an order paid partly in Points is refunded, the Points component returns as Points and the money component returns as money.

Procedures

  1. A launch proposal is prepared setting out earn economics, expected breakage and the projected liability.
  2. Finance and authorised management approve the proposal and the initial Loyalty Programme Configuration.
  3. Engineering implements an append-only Points ledger in which every accrual, reversal, expiry and redemption is a recorded entry attributable to an order or an administrative action.
  4. Programme terms are published to customers before enrolment opens, and enrolment is explicit rather than automatic.
  5. Balances, breakage, redemption rates and abuse signals are reviewed at {{review_frequency_default}}; fraud controls are reviewed at {{risk_review_frequency}}.
  6. Any change to earn or expiry rules is notified to enrolled customers in advance and applies prospectively.

Exceptions

Discretionary Points issued as service recovery are permitted only against a named order, with a recorded reason, and within {{approval_limit_refund}}. Corporate accounts, resellers and institutional buyers are ordinarily excluded from the Programme and are handled under separate commercial terms. Any exception to expiry, tier assignment or redemption limits requires written approval from authorised management and is recorded in the ledger.

Compliance

The Programme, once live, will be operated consistently with the Consumer Protection Act, 2019 and the Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020, including clear disclosure of terms before enrolment and no misleading representation of reward value. Personal data processed for the Programme is handled under the Privacy Policy and the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023, is used only for stated purposes, and is retained for {{data_retention_period}}. Ledger records supporting the Points liability are retained for the period required under applicable tax and accounting rules.

Violations

Creating duplicate or synthetic accounts, using another person's account or contact number, systematically ordering and returning items to farm Points, exploiting a configuration defect, or attempting to sell or transfer Points constitutes abuse. PlantAtHome may withhold accrual, reverse Points already credited, decline redemption, suspend Programme participation, or terminate a customer's Programme membership. Termination of Programme membership forfeits the unredeemed balance and does not by itself close the customer's shopping account; conversely, closure of a shopping account forfeits any unredeemed balance. Where a defect is found in the Programme's favour or the customer's favour, the correction is applied on the ledger and explained to the customer.

Related Documents

  • Terms and Conditions
  • Privacy Policy
  • Returns and Refunds Policy
  • Subscription Policy

title: Subscription Policy
html:
DRAFT — LEGAL REVIEW REQUIRED. This document is an operational or legal draft and must be reviewed and approved by authorized management and, where required, qualified legal counsel before becoming effective.

Purpose

This policy establishes the framework under which PlantAtHome, a brand of Silvestrix Green LLP, would offer recurring subscriptions — most plausibly for FarmBox fresh produce, and potentially for consumables such as fertilizers and growing media. It is written in advance of launch so that recurring billing, delivery scheduling, substitution and cancellation rules are agreed before a customer is asked to authorise a repeating payment.

Scope

Subscriptions are not currently offered by PlantAtHome. No customer holds an active subscription, no recurring payment mandate is in force, and no recurring charge is being raised. This document creates no present offering and no commitment to launch one. On approval and launch it would apply to all subscription products across the website and mobile app, to both direct and vendor-fulfilled subscription items, and to hyperlocal rider delivery and pan-India courier delivery alike.

Definitions

  • Subscription — a standing arrangement to supply a defined item or box at a stated frequency until cancelled.
  • Billing Cycle — the recurring period for which a customer is charged, as set in the Subscription Configuration.
  • Cut-off — the point before a scheduled delivery after which changes, skips or cancellations apply from the following cycle.
  • Skip — omitting one scheduled delivery while keeping the Subscription active.
  • Pause — suspending deliveries and billing for a defined interval.
  • Substitution — supplying a comparable item where a subscribed item is unavailable.
  • Subscription Configuration — the currently approved set of values governing frequencies, cut-offs, pause limits, retry behaviour and price-change notice.

Policy Statement

A recurring charge is only ever raised against an explicit, informed, revocable mandate given by the customer through Razorpay. A subscription must be as easy to cancel as it was to start, from the customer's own account, without contacting support. Price increases and material changes apply only prospectively and only after notice. PlantAtHome will not launch subscriptions until mandate handling, dunning, skip and pause controls, and the delivery calendar are implemented and tested end to end.

Responsibilities

RoleResponsibility
Authorised managementApproves launch, pricing and the Subscription Configuration.
FinanceOwns mandate compliance, billing accuracy, refunds and reconciliation with Razorpay settlements.
Supply and CategoryGuarantees availability against the forward order book and defines the approved substitution set per item.
OperationsBuilds the delivery calendar, assigns hyperlocal or courier fulfilment and manages failed-delivery handling.
EngineeringImplements mandates, cut-offs, skip and pause, dunning retries and customer-facing self-service cancellation.
Customer SupportHandles subscription queries within {{support_response_sla}} and resolves within {{support_resolution_sla}}.

Policy Requirements

Every subscription product must publish, before purchase, the item or box contents, the frequency, the amount and the Billing Cycle, the cut-off, and how to skip, pause or cancel. The following controls are mandatory; values are held in the Subscription Configuration.

ControlRuleSource of value
Frequency and billing cycleSelected at purchase from the published optionsAs per the currently approved Subscription Configuration
RenewalRenews automatically until cancelled, with a pre-charge reminderAs per the currently approved Subscription Configuration
Change cut-offEdits, skips and pauses take effect from the next uncommitted cycleAs per the currently approved Subscription Configuration
Pause limitsMaximum pause duration and pauses permitted per yearAs per the currently approved Subscription Configuration
CancellationSelf-service, effective for cycles not yet committed{{cancellation_window}}
Failed paymentRetries and grace period before suspensionAs per the currently approved Subscription Configuration
Delivery windowHyperlocal same-day rider or pan-India courier by serviceability{{delivery_sla_hyperlocal}} / {{delivery_sla_courier}}
Failed deliveryReattempts before the cycle is closed out{{delivery_attempts}}
Price change noticeAdvance notice, with the right to cancel before the new price appliesAs per the currently approved Subscription Configuration
Refunds on a missed cycleCredited or refunded where a paid cycle was not delivered{{refund_processing_time}}

Because fresh produce and live plants are perishable and seasonal, a subscribed item may be substituted with an item of equal or greater value from the pre-approved substitution set for that product. Substitutions are notified before or with dispatch. A customer who does not accept substitution may skip that cycle before cut-off or cancel. Quality claims on perishable and live items follow the standard evidence route within {{live_plant_claim_window}}.

Procedures

  1. At purchase the customer selects frequency and delivery address, reviews the full recurring terms, and authorises the Razorpay mandate.
  2. Before each cycle the platform sends a pre-charge reminder identifying the amount, the charge date and the link to skip, pause or cancel.
  3. At cut-off the cycle is committed, the order is created and routed to hyperlocal or courier fulfilment by pin code serviceability.
  4. If a charge fails, retries run per the Subscription Configuration and the customer is notified on each attempt; after the grace period the subscription is suspended, not silently cancelled, and no undelivered cycle is charged.
  5. Skips, pauses, address changes and cancellations submitted before cut-off apply to the next cycle; those submitted after cut-off apply to the cycle following.
  6. Subscription health — churn, failed payments, substitution rate and missed cycles — is reviewed at {{review_frequency_default}}.

Exceptions

A cycle already dispatched cannot be cancelled and is handled under the returns route applicable to the item. Where a delivery address moves outside serviceable coverage, the subscription is paused and the customer notified; it is cancelled without penalty if coverage does not resume. Compensation beyond a cycle's value requires approval within {{approval_limit_refund}}. Corporate and institutional standing orders are contracted separately and are outside this policy.

Compliance

Recurring mandates are executed through Razorpay in line with Reserve Bank of India requirements for recurring e-mandates, including pre-debit notification and customer-controlled revocation; PlantAtHome does not store card credentials. Disclosure of recurring terms before purchase, and cancellation that is not obstructed, are required by the Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020. Tax invoices are issued per cycle within {{gst_invoice_timeline}}. Subscriber data is processed under the Privacy Policy and retained for {{data_retention_period}}.

Violations

Charging a customer without a valid mandate, charging for an undelivered cycle, obstructing cancellation, or substituting outside the approved substitution set are serious breaches; each is corrected, refunded within {{refund_processing_time}} where money was taken, and reported to Finance. Repeated fraudulent chargebacks, use of stolen payment instruments, or abuse of skip and refund mechanics may result in suspension of subscription privileges and account restriction. Staff breaches are handled under the applicable HR policy.

Related Documents

  • Terms and Conditions
  • Shipping and Delivery Policy
  • Returns and Refunds Policy
  • Cancellation Policy
  • Privacy Policy
  • Promotional Policy

title: Cookie Policy
html:
DRAFT — LEGAL REVIEW REQUIRED. This document is an operational or legal draft and must be reviewed and approved by authorized management and, where required, qualified legal counsel before becoming effective.

Purpose

This policy explains how PlantAtHome, a brand of Silvestrix Green LLP, uses cookies and similar browser storage on its website and mobile app, what each category is used for, and how a visitor can control them. It is written conditionally: it describes what a category is used for where that category is deployed, rather than asserting that every category listed is currently in use. The authoritative, live list of what is actually set on a given page is the consent or preferences interface where one is deployed, and the browser's own storage inspector.

Scope

This policy covers cookies, local storage, session storage and comparable identifiers set through the PlantAtHome website and mobile app, whether set by PlantAtHome directly or by a third party whose service is embedded in a page. It covers browsing visitors, registered customers, vendor users and staff using our web interfaces. It does not cover the independent practices of external sites reached through links from our pages, or of payment, courier or messaging providers on their own properties.

Definitions

  • Cookie — a small text file stored by the browser and returned to a server on subsequent requests.
  • Similar technology — local storage, session storage, pixels, SDK identifiers and comparable mechanisms that persist or transmit information from a device.
  • First-party — set by a PlantAtHome domain. Third-party — set by another domain whose script, frame or asset is loaded by our page.
  • Session cookie — deleted when the browser closes. Persistent cookie — retained until it expires or is deleted.
  • Necessary — required for the site to function; the site cannot be provided without them.

Policy Statement

PlantAtHome uses browser storage for the narrowest set of purposes that lets the shop work and lets us fix it when it does not. Necessary cookies are always set because the service cannot be delivered without them. Any non-necessary category is deployed only where a legitimate purpose has been identified and, where consent is required, only after that consent is obtained. We do not sell cookie-derived data, and we do not use cookies to infer sensitive personal characteristics.

Responsibilities

RoleResponsibility
EngineeringMaintains the inventory of cookies and storage keys actually set, and ensures no new third-party script ships without review.
MarketingRequests analytics or advertising tags, states the purpose, and does not deploy tags outside the reviewed process.
Privacy ownerReviews the inventory at {{review_frequency_default}} and keeps this policy aligned with what is actually deployed.
Customer SupportRoutes cookie and privacy queries to the privacy owner and responds within {{support_response_sla}}.

Policy Requirements

The categories below describe purposes. A category is present only where the corresponding functionality is deployed; where it is not deployed, no cookie in that category is set.

CategoryPurpose where deployedConsentTypical lifetime
NecessarySign-in sessions and OTP login state, cart contents, checkout and payment flow, security and anti-fraud tokens, serviceable-city selection, load balancingNot required; the service cannot function without themSession or as set in the currently approved Platform Configuration
FunctionalRemembering preferences such as language, recently viewed plants, saved delivery city and interface settingsRequested where deployed and where requiredAs set in the currently approved Platform Configuration
AnalyticsAggregate measurement of page performance, errors, search and checkout drop-off, used to fix defects and improve the catalogueRequested where deployed and where requiredAs set in the currently approved Platform Configuration
MarketingMeasuring campaign response and, where deployed, showing relevant PlantAtHome advertising on third-party platformsRequested where deployed; declining does not restrict shoppingAs set in the currently approved Platform Configuration

Third-party cookies may be set by services embedded in our pages. In practice these can include the payment provider during checkout, map and address-lookup services on address entry, and, where deployed, an analytics or advertising provider. Such providers process data under their own notices; we limit embedded third parties to those with an operational purpose. Storage used only to hold a device identifier for the mobile app, or to keep an unsent form draft in the browser, serves the same purposes as the categories above and is treated the same way.

Procedures

  1. Before any new script, pixel or SDK is added to a page, the requesting team records its purpose, the data it transmits and its category; Engineering and the privacy owner review it.
  2. Where a consent interface is deployed, non-necessary categories are set only after the visitor accepts, and the choice is honoured until the visitor changes it or clears their browser.
  3. A visitor can change or withdraw a choice at any time through that interface where deployed, and in all cases through browser settings.
  4. All major browsers allow cookies to be viewed, blocked and deleted, and offer a private browsing mode; mobile operating systems provide an advertising-identifier reset. Blocking necessary cookies will break sign-in, cart and checkout.
  5. The cookie inventory is re-checked at {{review_frequency_default}} and after any release that adds a third-party integration, and this policy is corrected if it no longer matches reality.

Exceptions

Necessary cookies cannot be declined while continuing to use the shop; a visitor who blocks them can browse only in a degraded, signed-out state. Short-lived diagnostic storage may be enabled on a named environment to investigate a live incident, with the reason recorded and the storage removed when the incident is closed. Any exception to the review process requires written approval from the privacy owner before release.

Compliance

Personal data derived from cookies is processed under the Privacy Policy and, as applicable, the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 and the Information Technology Act, 2000 and rules made under it. Where a visitor is in a jurisdiction requiring prior consent for non-necessary storage, non-necessary categories are not set before consent is obtained. Requests to access or erase personal data associated with cookie identifiers are handled as data subject requests and answered within {{dsr_response_time}}. Cookie-derived records are retained for {{data_retention_period}} unless a shorter period applies.

Violations

Adding a tracking script outside the review process, deploying a marketing tag before consent where consent is required, or misstating a cookie's purpose in this policy are breaches of this policy. On discovery the tag is removed or gated, affected storage is cleared where technically possible, this policy is corrected, and the incident is assessed for notification obligations under the incident process. Staff breaches are handled under the applicable HR policy. Visitors who believe cookies are being used inconsistently with this policy can raise a grievance through the published support channels ({{support_channels}}) and will receive a response within {{support_response_sla}}.

Related Documents

  • Privacy Policy
  • Terms and Conditions
  • Data Retention Policy
  • Accessibility Statement

title: Accessibility Statement
html:
DRAFT — LEGAL REVIEW REQUIRED. This document is an operational or legal draft and must be reviewed and approved by authorized management and, where required, qualified legal counsel before becoming effective.

Purpose

This statement sets out how PlantAtHome, a brand of Silvestrix Green LLP, approaches accessibility on its website and mobile app, what we know is currently working against users of assistive technology, and how anyone can tell us about a barrier and get help completing a purchase in the meantime. It is written to be accurate rather than reassuring: an honest list of known gaps is more useful to a customer than a conformance badge.

Scope

This statement covers the PlantAtHome customer website and mobile app, including product browsing, search, the cart, checkout, order tracking and account pages, across all verticals: live plants, gardening tools, pots and planters, seeds, fertilizers, accessories, FarmBox fresh produce and corporate gifting. It does not cover third-party interfaces we embed or hand off to, such as the payment provider's checkout, map and address-lookup components, or courier tracking pages hosted by delivery partners; those are controlled by their operators. Internal admin and vendor consoles are outside the scope of this public statement.

Definitions

  • Assistive technology — software or hardware used to access digital content, including screen readers, screen magnifiers, switch access, voice control and browser zoom.
  • WCAG — the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines published by the W3C, used here as a working reference standard.
  • Barrier — anything on our interface that prevents a user from completing a task they could otherwise complete.
  • Assisted purchase — completing an order for a customer over a supported channel when they cannot complete it themselves on the interface.

Policy Statement

PlantAtHome is committed to making buying plants and garden supplies usable by as many people as possible, including people using assistive technology. We use WCAG 2.1 Level AA as our working reference target when designing and building new interfaces. We have not completed an independent accessibility audit and we do not claim that our website or app conforms to WCAG 2.1 Level AA, or to any level, at this time. No certification, third-party evaluation or formal conformance assessment has been carried out. Accessibility here is an active programme of work with known gaps, described below, and not a completed project.

Responsibilities

RoleResponsibility
DesignSpecifies colour contrast, focus states, target sizes and error messaging when designing new screens.
EngineeringBuilds with semantic markup, keyboard operability and labelled controls; treats a reported barrier as a defect, not a feature request.
Content and CatalogueSupplies meaningful alternative text for product images and writes plain-language product and care information.
Customer SupportAcknowledges accessibility reports within {{support_response_sla}}, offers an assisted purchase immediately, and logs the barrier.
Product ownerPrioritises logged barriers and reviews the open list at {{review_frequency_default}}.

Policy Requirements

Work in progress and honest limitations, as currently understood:

AreaCurrent position
Image alternative textCoverage across a large plant catalogue is incomplete; some product images carry generic or missing alternative text.
Keyboard operationCore browsing and checkout paths are being made keyboard-operable; some filter panels, carousels and modal dialogs may still trap or lose focus.
Screen reader labellingSome controls, especially in filters, quantity steppers and the address form, may be announced without a clear name or state.
Colour and contrastThe design system targets adequate contrast, but older screens and promotional creative may not meet it.
Embedded third partiesThe payment interface, map and address lookup, and courier tracking pages are supplied by third parties; we do not control their accessibility.
Media and documentsPlant-care videos may lack captions or transcripts, and invoices and some downloadable documents are PDFs that may not be fully tagged.
Voice and AI featuresVoice search and photo-based plant diagnosis depend on device capabilities and may not be usable by every customer; a typed or assisted alternative is available.
Mobile appSupport for platform accessibility services is partial and lags the website on some screens.

Where a barrier prevents a purchase, we will complete the order for the customer over a supported channel ({{support_channels}}) at the same price and with the same offers that apply on the website, including delivery to any serviceable address.

Procedures

  1. Report a barrier through any published support channel ({{support_channels}}), describing the page or screen, the device, browser or app version, the assistive technology in use, and what you were trying to do.
  2. We acknowledge within {{support_response_sla}} and, in the same reply, offer to complete the task with you rather than making you wait for a fix.
  3. The barrier is logged as a defect with the affected task and assistive technology recorded, and is targeted for resolution within {{support_resolution_sla}} where the fix is within our control.
  4. Where the barrier sits in a third-party component, we raise it with that provider, tell you so plainly, and keep the assisted route open until it is resolved.
  5. Accessibility checks — keyboard traversal of the buy path and a screen reader pass over browse, cart and checkout — form part of pre-release testing for new customer-facing screens.
  6. The open barrier list and this statement are reviewed at {{review_frequency_default}} and updated when the position changes.

Exceptions

We cannot guarantee accessibility of content or interfaces we do not control, including third-party payment, mapping and courier pages, and user-generated content such as customer reviews and photographs. Legacy screens scheduled for replacement may be remediated by replacement rather than by patching, and we will say so when reporting back on a specific barrier. Any decision to defer a fix beyond {{support_resolution_sla}} is recorded with a reason and an alternative route for the customer.

Compliance

We aim to operate consistently with the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016 and the accessibility expectations applying to digital services in India, and we use WCAG 2.1 Level AA as our reference standard for new work. This statement records our current position; it is not a declaration of conformance and should not be read as one. If a formal audit is completed in future, its scope, date and findings will be published here in place of this paragraph.

Violations

Shipping a new customer-facing screen without the pre-release accessibility checks, or closing a reported barrier without either a fix or a working alternative for the customer, is a breach of this statement and is reopened on discovery. If you are not satisfied with our response, escalate through the grievance route in the Customer Grievance Redressal Policy; escalations follow {{escalation_timeline}}. We would rather hear about a barrier bluntly than not hear about it, and we will not treat a report as a complaint about the customer's equipment.

Related Documents

  • Terms and Conditions
  • Privacy Policy
  • Cookie Policy
  • Customer Grievance Redressal Policy

DRAFT — LEGAL REVIEW REQUIRED. This document is an operational or legal draft and must be reviewed and approved by authorized management and, where required, qualified legal counsel before becoming effective.

Purpose

This SOP defines how PlantAtHome (Silvestrix Green LLP) evaluates, approves and activates a nursery or supplier as an approved vendor. It exists because a vendor who ships live plants directly to a customer carries our brand, our invoice and our delivery promise. The procedure ensures that every vendor is a verifiable legal entity, is financially payable, can grow or source healthy stock, can pack it so it survives transit, and can dispatch inside the delivery windows the storefront has already promised the customer.

Scope

Applies to all new vendor applications across every vertical — live plants, pots and planters, gardening tools, seeds, fertilizers, accessories, FarmBox fresh produce and corporate gifting — for both hyperlocal same-day and pan-India courier fulfilment. It covers first-time onboarding only. Re-activation of a suspended vendor, category expansion for a live vendor, and termination are governed by the Vendor Performance Management and Penalty Policy and the Vendor Offboarding SOP.

Definitions

  • Onboarding File — the record in the admin vendor module holding every document, audit score, approval and rejection note for one applicant.
  • Stage Owner — the role accountable for clearing one stage; only that role may mark it passed.
  • Master Catalogue — the single canonical product catalogue; vendor SKUs are mapped to it, never created outside it.
  • Penny-drop — a token credit to the vendor account to confirm the beneficiary name before settlement is enabled.
  • Activation — the point at which vendor SKUs become purchasable in serviceable cities.

Roles and Responsibilities

  • Vendor Onboarding Executive — owns the file end to end, chases documents, keeps stage status current.
  • Compliance Analyst — entity, PAN and blacklist verification.
  • Finance — GST and bank verification, commercial annexures.
  • Field Operations — nursery inspection.
  • Quality and Category Team — quality audit, packaging audit, catalogue and image review.
  • Logistics — delivery capability and lane assignment.
  • Head of Vendor Operations — final approval authority.
  • Vendor Success — training and go-live support.

Prerequisites

Before Stage 1 opens: the applicant's operating city is confirmed against the current delivery coverage set; the intended categories are open for supplier addition; and the applicant has been given the document checklist, the packaging specification and the current commercial terms summary in writing.

Trigger

A vendor application submitted through the vendor sign-up form, a referral logged by the category team, or a sourcing lead raised by Field Operations during city expansion.

Step-by-Step Procedure

Stages run in order. A stage may not be marked passed while an earlier mandatory stage is open. Every rejection is recorded with a reason on the Onboarding File.

SLA

Stage-level turnaround targets are held in the currently approved Vendor Onboarding Configuration and are measured from the moment the stage owner receives complete inputs; time spent waiting on the vendor is excluded and shown separately on the file. Once live, the vendor is measured against {{vendor_acceptance_sla}}, {{vendor_dispatch_sla}} and {{vendor_return_rate_threshold}}, with settlement on {{vendor_settlement_cycle}}.

Quality Checks

  • No stage may be self-certified: the stage owner and the person marking it complete must be different from the vendor.
  • Quality, packaging and image evidence must be attached to the file, not merely described.
  • Bank and GST records must match the verified legal entity name exactly before settlement is enabled.
  • A random sample of newly activated vendors is re-audited at {{review_frequency_default}} to confirm on-file evidence matches live performance.

Exceptions

A remote video inspection may replace a physical visit where travel is impractical, provided the walkthrough is geo-tagged and retained. Provisional activation with a restricted SKU set may be granted where every stage except catalogue breadth is cleared. Waiver of any verification, quality, packaging or agreement stage is not permitted; all other exceptions require written approval from the Head of Vendor Operations and are recorded on the file with the reason and expiry.

Escalation Process

A stage stalled beyond its configured turnaround escalates from the Onboarding Executive to the Vendor Manager, then to the Head of Vendor Operations, following {{escalation_timeline}}. Disputes over quality or packaging outcomes are escalated to the Quality Head, whose re-audit decision is final for onboarding purposes. Compliance findings — forged documents, restricted species, identity mismatch — bypass the ladder and go directly to Legal and the Head of Vendor Operations.

Records and Audit Trail

The Onboarding File retains the document pack, verification results, inspection and audit evidence, catalogue and image approvals, the executed agreement, training records and the activation checklist, with actor and timestamp on every stage transition. Records are retained for {{data_retention_period}} after activation or rejection. Rejected applications retain the reason so that repeat applications are recognised.
