title: Vendor Verification Policy
html:
DRAFT — LEGAL REVIEW REQUIRED. This document is an operational or legal draft and must be reviewed and approved by authorized management and, where required, qualified legal counsel before becoming effective.

Purpose

PlantAtHome, a brand of Silvestrix Green LLP, sells live plants, gardening tools, pots and planters, seeds, fertilizers, accessories, FarmBox fresh produce and corporate gifting through its own fulfilment and through approved nursery vendors. This policy sets out what must be verified about a vendor before that vendor may list a product, receive an order, or be paid, and how that verification is refreshed over the life of the relationship. Verification exists to protect customers from unfit or misdescribed stock, to protect Silvestrix Green LLP from GST input mismatches and payment fraud, and to give Finance a verified beneficiary record before any settlement leaves the account.

Scope

This policy applies to every applicant and every active vendor supplying any PlantAtHome vertical, whether fulfilling hyperlocal same-day orders from a local nursery or shipping pan-India by courier. It binds the Vendor Onboarding, Category, Finance and Compliance functions, and every employee who holds the permission to approve, reactivate or edit a vendor account in the admin console. Logistics and courier partners are onboarded under a separate contracting process and are out of scope.

Definitions

  • Vendor — a legal entity approved to list stock on PlantAtHome and to fulfil customer orders under a signed Vendor Agreement.
  • Verification File — the complete set of documents, check results, inspection reports and approvals held against the vendor record.
  • Authorised Signatory — the individual empowered to bind the vendor entity to the Vendor Agreement.
  • Operational Location — the nursery, polyhouse, warehouse or workshop from which stock is actually grown, held and dispatched, which may differ from the registered address.
  • Fraud Indicator — an observed pattern that requires escalation before approval, listed under Policy Requirements.
  • Re-verification — a scheduled or triggered repeat of verification on an already active vendor.

Policy Statement

No vendor account is approved for listing, and no settlement is released, until the Verification File is complete and each check below has passed and been recorded against the vendor record. Verification is evidence-based: a claim made on the application form is not accepted without an independent document or system check supporting it. Verification is never treated as a one-time gate; every active vendor is re-verified at {{review_frequency_default}} and immediately on any trigger event.

Responsibilities

  • Vendor Onboarding — collects documents, runs identity, address and duplicate-account checks, and maintains the Verification File.
  • Finance — validates GST registration and bank beneficiary details, and blocks settlement where either is unverified or has changed.
  • Category and Operations — inspects the operational location, confirms sourcing capability and confirms hyperlocal serviceability against the delivery coverage configuration.
  • Compliance — reviews licences, adjudicates fraud escalations and approves or refuses conditional approvals.
  • Vendor — provides true and current documents and notifies PlantAtHome of any change to entity, GSTIN, bank account or operational location before the change takes effect.

Policy Requirements

Verification areaEvidence requiredVerification methodAccountable
Business identityCertificate of incorporation, LLP agreement, partnership deed or proprietor declaration, with entity PANEntity name and constitution cross-matched across all submitted documents and the PAN recordVendor Onboarding
Authorised signatoryGovernment photo identity document and proof of authority to contractIdentity matched to the person who executes the Vendor AgreementVendor Onboarding
Tax informationGSTIN, or a signed declaration where the vendor is below the registration threshold; HSN codes for the applied categoriesGSTIN status, legal name and principal place of business checked on the GST portal against the applicationFinance
Bank verificationCancelled cheque or bank letter in the entity nameTest credit to the account; the beneficiary name returned must match the entity name before settlement is enabledFinance
Registered addressUtility bill, registered rent agreement or property tax receiptCompared against the GST principal place of businessVendor Onboarding
Nursery or operational locationGeo-tagged photographs of the growing, storage and packing areaPhysical or live video inspection, filed as an inspection report; serviceability confirmed against the delivery coverage configurationCategory and Operations
Product sourcingDeclaration of own-grown versus traded stock, named upstream suppliers, and any nursery, seed or fertilizer dealer licence applicable to the categories applied forLicence numbers recorded with validity dates diarised for renewalCompliance
Previous performanceTrade references and marketplace historyDuplicate search across PAN, GSTIN, bank account, contact number and email for prior or delisted PlantAtHome accountsVendor Onboarding

The following are fraud indicators and must be escalated to Compliance before approval: a beneficiary name that does not match the entity; a bank account, address or contact number shared with a suspended or delisted vendor; catalogue images traced to another website or grower; a claimed supply volume that the inspected site cannot physically hold; refusal of or repeated postponement of site inspection; a cancelled or suspended GSTIN; and pressure to release settlement ahead of {{vendor_settlement_cycle}}.

Procedures

  1. The applicant submits the vendor application and uploads documents through the vendor console.
  2. Vendor Onboarding runs identity, address, GST and duplicate-account checks and records each result against the vendor record.
  3. Finance runs the bank test credit and records the returned beneficiary name.
  4. Category and Operations complete the operational location inspection and confirm which categories and cities the vendor may serve.
  5. Compliance clears licences and any fraud escalation.
  6. The Vendor Agreement is executed by the verified authorised signatory, and the account is approved only for the categories and locations inspected.
  7. Re-verification runs at {{review_frequency_default}}, and higher-risk vendors are reviewed at {{risk_review_frequency}} using {{risk_scoring_model}}.
  8. Re-verification is triggered immediately, and listings are paused, on any change of entity, GSTIN, bank account or operational location, or on a confirmed fraud indicator.

Exceptions

A conditional approval may be granted where one non-critical document is pending, provided the vendor is restricted to a limited catalogue, settlement remains held, and the exception is approved in writing by Compliance and the Head of Category and recorded in the Verification File with an expiry date drawn from the currently approved Vendor Onboarding Configuration. Identity, GST and bank verification are never waived.

Compliance

Verification Files are retained for {{data_retention_period}} and are treated as confidential vendor data under the Data Protection and Privacy Policy, with access limited to the functions named above. Vendor Onboarding samples approved files at {{review_frequency_default}} to confirm that every mandatory check was performed and evidenced, and reports exceptions to management.

Violations

Submission of a forged, altered or borrowed document, concealment of a prior delisted account, or diversion of settlement to an unverified account results in immediate suspension of listings, a hold on payouts through {{vendor_settlement_dispute_window}}, recovery of amounts due, and termination of the Vendor Agreement. Financial penalties, where contractually provided, are applied under {{penalty_schedule}}. Confirmed fraud is reported to the relevant authorities. Employees who approve a vendor without the required checks are dealt with under internal disciplinary procedures.

Related Documents

  • Vendor Onboarding and Account Management SOP
  • Product Quality Standards
  • Vendor Pricing Policy
  • Vendor Settlement and Payout Policy
  • Anti-Fraud and Suspicious Activity Policy

title: Product Quality Standards
html:
DRAFT — LEGAL REVIEW REQUIRED. This document is an operational or legal draft and must be reviewed and approved by authorized management and, where required, qualified legal counsel before becoming effective.

Purpose

This standard defines the minimum identification data, physical condition, labelling and packaging that every product listed on PlantAtHome must meet, so that the item a customer receives is the item the listing described. Most PlantAtHome disputes are description disputes rather than defect disputes: a plant smaller than expected, a pot of a different diameter, a fertilizer pack without the printed grade. This standard closes that gap at the catalogue stage rather than at the refund stage.

Scope

Applies to every SKU offered on PlantAtHome, whether fulfilled directly by Silvestrix Green LLP or by an approved nursery vendor, across live plants, pots and planters, gardening tools, seeds, fertilizers, accessories, FarmBox fresh produce and corporate gifting kits, and to both hyperlocal and courier fulfilment. The physiological condition of live stock — root establishment, pest and disease load, hardening and acclimatisation, transit tolerance — is governed by the Live Plant Quality Standards; this document governs catalogue accuracy, non-living goods and the condition disclosures that appear on the listing.

Definitions

  • SKU — a single sellable configuration of a product, distinct in species or model, size and pot or pack.
  • Master catalogue — the approved product record from which all listings are generated.
  • Botanical name — the accepted binomial of genus and species, with cultivar in single quotation marks.
  • Size — overall plant height measured from the top of the growing medium to the highest natural growing point, or the stated dimension of a non-living product.
  • Pot size — nominal top internal diameter with material and drainage status.
  • Condition class — the disclosed state of the item, such as standard, seasonal or sold-as-is.

Policy Statement

A SKU is published only when its identification data is complete and verified, its physical stock matches that data, and its labelling and packaging meet this standard. Where a vendor cannot supply stock matching the published record, the correct action is to mark the SKU out of stock, never to substitute a different species, grade or pot size. Substitution without customer consent is treated as misdescription.

Responsibilities

  • Vendor — submits accurate catalogue data, holds stock that matches it, and labels and packs to this standard.
  • Category Management — reviews and approves catalogue submissions, owns the master catalogue, and blocks non-conforming SKUs.
  • Operations and Quality — inspects first dispatch and audit samples, and records failures against the vendor scorecard.
  • Customer Support — routes description-related complaints back to Category so the catalogue record is corrected, not only the individual order.

Policy Requirements

AttributeStandardReference
Botanical nameAccepted binomial, cultivar in single quotes; trade nicknames are not permitted in this fieldMaster catalogue taxonomy
Common nameAt least one common name; regional names permitted as additional entriesMaster catalogue taxonomy
Category and verticalMapped to a single approved category; multi-category listing of the same SKU is not permittedAs per the currently approved Catalogue Configuration
Size and gradeStated as the band the stock actually falls in, measured as defined aboveAs per the currently approved Catalogue Size Configuration
Pot size and materialNominal top diameter, material, and whether drainage holes are presentAs per the currently approved Catalogue Configuration
Condition classDeclared on the listing; any cosmetic variance must be disclosed before purchaseThis standard
SeedsSpecies, packet weight or count, lot number, packing date and validity as printed on the packSeeds Act, 1966 and pack declaration
Fertilizers and plant careNet weight, nutrient grade and statutory particulars exactly as printed by the manufacturer; tamper seal intactStatutory label
Tools, pots and accessoriesMaterial, dimensions, weight, finish and any assembly requirementMaster catalogue attributes
FarmBox produceVariety, pack weight, harvest date and storage instructionAs per the currently approved FarmBox Handling Configuration

General quality requirements: pots and planters must be free of cracks, chips and glaze faults unless the SKU is explicitly listed sold-as-is; tools must be free of rust, with secure handle-to-head joints and intact edge protection; seeds and fertilizers must be within printed validity and in unbroken manufacturer packaging; no product may be repacked, relabelled or rebranded; and every batch must remain traceable to the supplying vendor and lot.

Image accuracy: listing images must show the actual SKU at the stated size and in the stated pot. Representative imagery is permitted only where the category permits it and the visible variance stays inside the tolerances in the currently approved Image Standards Configuration, as detailed in the Vendor Product Image Standards.

Labelling: each unit carries the SKU code, botanical and common name, size or net quantity, and a care card for live plants. Pre-packaged commodities carry the declarations required under the Legal Metrology (Packaged Commodities) Rules, 2011, including retail sale price, net quantity, country of origin and the name and address of the packer or importer, plus batch and expiry where applicable.

Packaging: packing follows the Packaging and Dispatch Standards. Courier consignments require the growing medium secured against movement, a moisture barrier at the soil surface, collar or sleeve protection for foliage, and rigid protection for ceramic and glass. Hyperlocal rider consignments may use returnable crates where the route supports it.

Procedures

  1. The vendor submits catalogue data and images for the SKU through the vendor console.
  2. Category Management reviews identification data, images and condition disclosure before the SKU is published.
  3. Operations inspects the first dispatch against the published record and records the result.
  4. Audit samples are drawn from live orders at {{review_frequency_default}} and after any spike in description-related returns.
  5. A failed SKU is blocked from sale until corrected; a failed batch is quarantined and not dispatched.
  6. Repeat failures are escalated to the vendor scorecard review.

Exceptions

Seasonal stock, clearance stock and deliberately imperfect items such as hand-thrown terracotta with visible variation may be listed only under a sold-as-is condition class, with the variance described and imaged on the listing and the exception approved by Category Management. An exception never removes the customer's statutory rights or the obligations of the Returns and Refunds Policy.

Compliance

This standard supports the obligations of Silvestrix Green LLP under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019 and the Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020 on accurate product information, and under the Legal Metrology (Packaged Commodities) Rules, 2011 on declarations. Vendors handling regulated goods remain responsible for their own obligations under the Seeds Act, 1966 and the Insecticides Act, 1968. Quality outcomes are measured against {{vendor_quality_target}} and {{vendor_return_rate_threshold}}.

Violations

Publishing data that does not match dispatched stock, substituting species, grade or pot size without customer consent, dispatching expired or unsealed regulated goods, or removing statutory label declarations results in the SKU being delisted and the cost of the resulting refund, replacement and return leg being recovered from the vendor. Persistent breach is handled under {{penalty_schedule}} and may lead to category suspension or termination under the Vendor Verification Policy.

Related Documents

  • Live Plant Quality Standards
  • Vendor Product Image Standards
  • Packaging and Dispatch Standards
  • Vendor Verification Policy
  • Returns and Refunds Policy

title: Vendor Product Image Standards
html:
DRAFT — LEGAL REVIEW REQUIRED. This document is an operational or legal draft and must be reviewed and approved by authorized management and, where required, qualified legal counsel before becoming effective.

Purpose

On PlantAtHome the image is the product. A customer buying a live plant cannot inspect leaf colour, plant fullness or pot finish before purchase, and judges size almost entirely from the photograph. This standard defines what a vendor product image must show, how it must be captured, and what post-processing is forbidden, so that images sell accurately and do not generate avoidable returns, replacements or advertising complaints.

Scope

Applies to every image a vendor uploads or supplies for use on PlantAtHome, in any placement: catalogue listing, category and search results, the mobile app, WhatsApp Business messages, email campaigns, and paid or organic social placements. It covers live plants, pots and planters, tools, seeds, fertilizers, accessories, FarmBox produce and corporate gifting kits, and applies equally to images produced by PlantAtHome on the vendor's behalf. Specific technical values — pixel dimensions, aspect ratio, file format, maximum file size, minimum number of angles — are held in the currently approved Image Standards Configuration and are enforced by the upload checks rather than restated here.

Definitions

  • Primary image — the first image shown in listing and search results.
  • Secondary image — any additional image in the listing gallery.
  • Scale reference image — an image showing the complete plant in its supplied pot, from which a customer can judge real size.
  • Lifestyle image — a staged or in-situ image showing the product in a room, balcony or garden setting.
  • Permitted correction — post-processing that makes the photograph more faithful to the physical item.
  • Misleading edit — post-processing that makes the item appear better, larger, fuller or different from what ships.

Policy Statement

Every image must represent stock the vendor actually holds and will dispatch under that SKU. The primary image must show that item alone, at the listed size and in the listed pot, against a clean background. Where an image cannot be made faithful by permitted correction, the answer is to re-shoot the product, never to edit the photograph toward the desired appearance.

Responsibilities

  • Vendor — captures or commissions images of its own stock, warrants that it owns or is licensed to use every image supplied, and re-shoots when stock or packaging changes.
  • Category Management — reviews images before publication, rejects with a stated reason, and may commission replacement photography.
  • Brand and Marketing — maintains the Image Standards Configuration and the presentation rules for campaign placements.
  • Customer Support — flags listings where complaints indicate the image overstates the product, for Category re-review.

Policy Requirements

RequirementStandardWhere defined
Resolution and aspect ratioUploads must meet the minimum pixel dimensions and the fixed aspect ratio; images are rejected automatically below the minimumAs per the currently approved Image Standards Configuration
File format and sizeApproved formats only, within the maximum upload size; no screenshots and no re-compressed low-quality copiesAs per the currently approved Image Standards Configuration
Primary image compositionOne product, centred, filling the frame to the configured margin, on a plain white or neutral backgroundAs per the currently approved Image Standards Configuration
Lighting and colourEven, diffused, daylight-balanced light; no harsh shadow across the product; foliage, flower and glaze colour must match the physical itemThis standard
Angles and coverageThe configured minimum set of angles, always including a scale reference image and a top-down view of the foliage or pack faceAs per the currently approved Image Standards Configuration
Detail imagesClose-ups of the features that drive returns: leaf condition, pot base and drainage, tool head-to-handle joint, legible seed and fertilizer labelThis standard
Lifestyle imagesPermitted as secondary images only, and only when the product is shown at true relative scaleThis standard
Watermarks and overlaysProhibited: vendor logos, contact numbers, website addresses, prices, offer badges, borders and promotional text burned into the imageThis standard
Image ownershipVendor-owned or licensed; supplier catalogue and stock library images may not be used for live plant SKUsVendor Agreement

Permitted editing: cropping and straightening, exposure and white-balance correction toward true colour, dust and sensor-spot removal, and background clean-up to a plain neutral field.

Prohibited editing: saturation or hue shifts that change flower or foliage colour; cloning or compositing to add leaves, blooms or fruit; replacing the pot; removing damage, pest marks or discoloration; assembling a plant from more than one photograph; using an artificial or generated image of a plant PlantAtHome sells as live stock; and any manipulation of perspective or props that makes the plant appear larger than the listed size.

An image is treated as misleading, regardless of technique, if the delivered item would surprise a reasonable customer on size, fullness, colour, pot type or quantity supplied. Images showing a group of plants must state the quantity supplied in the listing, and images of mature specimens used to illustrate growth potential must be clearly captioned as such and never used as the primary image.

Brand consistency: PlantAtHome may crop, re-background, re-shoot or replace any vendor image to maintain a consistent catalogue presentation, and may use vendor-supplied images across its storefront, app, WhatsApp, email and advertising placements under the licence granted in the Vendor Agreement.

Procedures

  1. The vendor uploads images against the SKU in the vendor console.
  2. Automated checks validate format, dimensions, aspect ratio and file size against the configuration and reject failures immediately with the reason.
  3. Category Management reviews the remaining images for accuracy, composition, editing and overlays before the SKU is published.
  4. Rejected images are returned with a specific reason; the vendor re-shoots and resubmits within the period stated in the currently approved Image Standards Configuration, and the SKU stays unpublished until then.
  5. Where returns or complaints indicate a listing overstates the product, Category re-reviews the images and may suspend the listing pending re-shoot.
  6. Images are re-reviewed whenever the SKU's size band, pot or packaging changes.

Exceptions

Seasonal, made-to-order and corporate gifting SKUs may use a representative image where individual variation is inherent, provided the listing states that the item varies and the variation stays inside the tolerance in the currently approved Image Standards Configuration. Manufacturer-supplied images may be used for sealed branded goods such as fertilizers and tools where the vendor holds written permission from the brand owner. Both exceptions require Category Management approval recorded against the SKU.

Compliance

Accurate imagery supports the obligations of Silvestrix Green LLP under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019 and the Guidelines for Prevention of Misleading Advertisements and Endorsements, 2022, and unlicensed use of third-party photographs exposes both parties under the Copyright Act, 1957. Image review outcomes feed the vendor scorecard alongside {{vendor_quality_target}} and {{vendor_return_rate_threshold}}, and a listing whose returns are driven by image mismatch is treated as a quality failure, not a customer preference return.

Violations

Uploading images of stock the vendor does not hold, copying images from another seller or grower, applying a prohibited edit, or embedding vendor contact details or offers in an image results in immediate removal of the images and suspension of the affected listings. Costs of resulting refunds, replacements and return legs are recoverable from the vendor and repeat breaches are actioned under {{penalty_schedule}}, up to termination under the Vendor Verification Policy. Any third-party copyright claim arising from a vendor-supplied image is the vendor's responsibility under the indemnity in the Vendor Agreement.

Related Documents

  • Product Quality Standards
  • Live Plant Quality Standards
  • Vendor Verification Policy
  • Returns and Refunds Policy

title: Vendor Pricing Policy
html:
DRAFT — LEGAL REVIEW REQUIRED. This document is an operational or legal draft and must be reviewed and approved by authorized management and, where required, qualified legal counsel before becoming effective.

Purpose

This policy defines how a vendor's price becomes the price a customer pays on PlantAtHome, how commission and taxes are applied, who funds a discount, and when a price change may take effect. It exists because PlantAtHome prices differ by city — hyperlocal same-day supply and pan-India courier supply carry different cost structures — and because the vendor sets only one input into that calculation. Clarity here prevents settlement disputes and prevents a customer being charged a price the vendor never intended.

Scope

Applies to every SKU supplied by an approved vendor across all PlantAtHome verticals and both fulfilment lanes, and to Finance, Category Management, Marketing and Vendor Operations. It covers marketplace retail sales, corporate gifting quotations fulfilled through vendors, and promotional pricing. It does not govern the vendor's own pricing on its own or other channels.

Definitions

  • Vendor price — the amount the vendor sets for a SKU in a given city, on which settlement is calculated, exclusive of PlantAtHome commission and of delivery cost.
  • Customer selling price — the price displayed to the customer, derived by the platform from the vendor price and the applicable configuration.
  • Maximum retail price — the statutory printed price on a pre-packaged commodity.
  • Commission — the fee retained by Silvestrix Green LLP for platform, payment, support and marketing services.
  • Promotional funding — the split of a discount between the platform and the vendor for a named campaign.
  • Price update window — the period in which a submitted price change becomes effective for new orders.

Policy Statement

The vendor sets the vendor price. PlantAtHome derives and displays the customer selling price. A vendor never edits the customer selling price directly, and PlantAtHome never settles a vendor at less than the vendor price agreed for the order, less only commission, taxes and deductions this policy permits. Every order is priced by the record in force at the moment of order confirmation, and no later price change alters an order already placed.

Responsibilities

  • Vendor — maintains accurate vendor prices per SKU and city, keeps them within the printed maximum retail price where one applies, and honours the price on every accepted order.
  • Finance — owns commission, tax and settlement configuration, and reconciles settled amounts to order records.
  • Category Management — reviews price submissions for plausibility and approves listing of prices that fall far outside the category norm.
  • Marketing — defines campaigns and records promotional funding before a campaign goes live.

Policy Requirements

ElementRuleWhere configured
Vendor priceSet per SKU per serviceable city; exclusive of commission and delivery costVendor console
Customer selling priceDerived by the platform from vendor price plus applicable city margin and rounding; never edited by the vendorAs per the currently approved City Pricing Configuration
CommissionApplied on the order value in line with {{commission_model}} for the SKU's categoryVendor Agreement and commission configuration
TaxesGST applied at the rate for the SKU's HSN code; the vendor issues a compliant tax invoice within {{gst_invoice_timeline}}Tax configuration
Delivery chargeNever added into the vendor price; charged to the customer or absorbed per the delivery configuration and {{free_shipping_threshold}}Delivery and shipping configuration
DiscountsRecorded per campaign as platform-funded, vendor-funded or shared before the campaign startsPromotions and Discounting Policy
SettlementVendor price less commission, taxes and permitted deductions, released on {{vendor_settlement_cycle}}Vendor Settlement and Payout Policy
Settlement disputesRaised with the order reference within {{vendor_settlement_dispute_window}}Vendor Settlement and Payout Policy

Price accuracy. The vendor price must correspond to stock the vendor can actually supply at that price. Where a SKU is a pre-packaged commodity carrying a printed maximum retail price, the customer selling price must not exceed it, and the vendor must inform Category Management when the printed price on new stock changes.

Price updates. Price changes are submitted through the vendor console and take effect forward only, within the price update window in the currently approved City Pricing Configuration. Orders already confirmed are fulfilled and settled at the price in force at confirmation. Price changes are locked for SKUs enrolled in a live campaign for the duration of that campaign.

Promotional participation. Enrolment in a campaign is by written acceptance of the campaign terms, including the funding split, before the campaign starts. A vendor may decline a campaign; declining does not by itself affect ranking or order allocation. Vendor-funded discount amounts are deducted at settlement and shown as a separate line on the settlement statement.

Unauthorised changes. Raising a price after an order is confirmed, cancelling or short-shipping an accepted order because the price has become unfavourable, requesting payment or a top-up directly from the customer, or including a price, offer or contact detail on packaging, invoices or product images is prohibited. Acceptance and dispatch obligations continue to run to {{vendor_acceptance_sla}} and {{vendor_dispatch_sla}} regardless of any pending price change.

Independence. PlantAtHome does not dictate the price at which a vendor sells through its own or any third-party channel. The vendor likewise makes no claim about PlantAtHome pricing to customers.

Procedures

  1. The vendor submits or updates the vendor price per SKU and city in the vendor console.
  2. Automated validation checks the price against the category band and against the printed maximum retail price where one applies.
  3. Category Management reviews any price flagged as an outlier before it goes live.
  4. The platform derives and publishes the customer selling price from the applicable configuration.
  5. At order confirmation the pricing record is captured against the order and becomes the basis for settlement.
  6. Finance settles on {{vendor_settlement_cycle}} with a statement itemising commission, taxes, promotional funding and other deductions.
  7. Disputes are raised with the order reference within {{vendor_settlement_dispute_window}} and resolved against the captured pricing record.

Exceptions

Negotiated pricing for corporate gifting, bulk landscaping and institutional orders may depart from catalogue pricing, provided the quotation is issued by PlantAtHome, the vendor price is agreed in writing before acceptance, and approval is obtained from an authorised approver in line with the currently approved Delegation of Authority Configuration. Temporary price protection during a documented input-cost shock may be approved by Finance for a defined period recorded against the SKU. No exception permits a change to the price of an order already confirmed.

Compliance

Pricing displays and promotional claims must comply with the Consumer Protection Act, 2019 and the Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020, including accurate display of the total price payable, and with the Legal Metrology (Packaged Commodities) Rules, 2011 on retail sale price declarations. Tax treatment follows the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 and the marketplace obligations that apply to Silvestrix Green LLP. Finance reconciles a sample of settlements against captured order pricing at {{review_frequency_default}}.

Violations

Repricing an accepted order, cancelling to avoid a committed price, exceeding a printed maximum retail price, soliciting payment outside the platform, or claiming promotional funding not agreed in the campaign record results in withholding of the disputed settlement amount, recovery of any customer refund or goodwill cost, and action under {{penalty_schedule}}. Repeated breach results in suspension of listings and may lead to termination under the Vendor Verification Policy. Employees who approve pricing outside their authority are dealt with under internal disciplinary procedures.

Related Documents

  • Vendor Settlement and Payout Policy
  • Promotions and Discounting Policy
  • Product Quality Standards

title: Packaging Manual
related_titles: Sustainable Packaging and Waste Management Policy
html:
DRAFT — LEGAL REVIEW REQUIRED. This document is an operational or legal draft and must be reviewed and approved by authorized management and, where required, qualified legal counsel before becoming effective.

Purpose

This manual is the single packing instruction for every PlantAtHome (Silvestrix Green LLP) outbound consignment. It exists to protect living stock in transit, prevent breakage of ceramic and glass items, keep FarmBox produce saleable on arrival, present the brand consistently at unboxing, and produce a packed unit that survives both the hyperlocal rider lane and the pan-India courier lane. Correct packing is also our first defence in damage disputes: a consignment packed and photographed to this manual is the evidence we rely on when a customer raises a claim within {{live_plant_claim_window}}.

Scope

Applies to all PlantAtHome fulfilment staff, packing contractors, and approved nursery vendors who pack orders on their own premises for dispatch under the PlantAtHome brand. It covers all product classes sold: small plants, medium plants, large plants and specimens, ceramic planters, fragile accessories, FarmBox fresh produce and corporate gifting. It covers outbound customer shipments, replacement shipments and return-leg repacking. It does not cover inbound vendor receiving, warehouse storage or courier label generation, which are handled in the dispatch SOP.

Definitions

  • Product class — the packing category a SKU maps to in the catalogue; it determines materials and method, not the marketing category.
  • Packaging Configuration — the approved master list of box sizes, board specifications, void-fill types, sleeve and label artwork and per-class consumable allowances maintained by Operations.
  • Root ball wrap — the moisture-retaining sleeve around soil and roots that keeps the medium intact and prevents soil escape into the carton.
  • Ventilation — deliberate, protected air openings in the outer carton for live botanical goods.
  • Fragile handling unit — a ceramic or glass item individually wrapped and suspended so that no face touches the carton wall.
  • Pre-seal check — the mandatory inspection completed and recorded before tape is applied.

Policy Statement

PlantAtHome packs to the survival requirement of the goods and the duration of the chosen lane, not to the cheapest available consumable. No consignment leaves a facility unless it has been packed to the class instruction below, passed the pre-seal check, and been photographed. Where the two conflict, plant survival and customer safety take precedence over material cost and over presentation.

Responsibilities

  • Packing Operator — selects the class instruction, packs, completes the pre-seal check and captures pack photographs.
  • Fulfilment Supervisor — audits packed units daily, releases only compliant consignments, and holds anything failing the check.
  • Vendor — packs to this manual within {{vendor_dispatch_sla}} and is measured against {{vendor_quality_target}} and {{vendor_return_rate_threshold}}.
  • Category and Quality — assigns each SKU to a product class and owns changes to the Packaging Configuration.
  • Logistics — confirms the lane before packing, since courier consignments require the reinforced specification.

Policy Requirements

Product classMaterialsProtection and ventilationMoisture and presentationPre-seal check
Small plantsNursery pot, root ball wrap, corrugated cell insert and single-wall carton per the currently approved Packaging ConfigurationPot immobilised in a cell so foliage bears no load; punched vents on opposing carton facesMedium watered to damp, never saturated; care card and branded sleeve on top layerPot cannot shift when the carton is inverted; no loose soil
Medium plantsRoot ball wrap, collar brace, double-wall carton per the currently approved Packaging ConfigurationStem collared at the pot rim; foliage gathered loosely, never compressedDamp medium plus moisture-retaining wrap; care card visible on openingCarton withstands a controlled tilt with no internal movement
Large plants and specimensTimber or reinforced base, trunk sleeve, upright crate or open-frame pack per the currently approved Packaging ConfigurationBase-anchored and strapped upright; open faces for airflow; "this way up" and live plant marking on all vertical facesRoot ball wrapped for the full {{delivery_sla_courier}} lane duration; foliage tied, not baggedTwo-person lift test; unit stands unsupported without leaning
Ceramic plantersIndividual wrap, corner protection, void fill and double-wall carton per the currently approved Packaging ConfigurationEach piece a fragile handling unit; drainage hole plugged; no ceramic-to-ceramic contactWiped clean and dust-free; fragile marking on all facesShake test produces no audible movement
Fragile accessoriesBlister or moulded insert, inner carton, outer carton per the currently approved Packaging ConfigurationBoxed-in-box with suspended inner; blades, glass and probes sheathedRetail packaging kept undamaged and outward-facingSharp edges fully sheathed; inner box floats on all sides
FarmBox produceFood-grade liner, ventilated produce carton and insulation per the currently approved Packaging ConfigurationVent slots kept clear of liner; heavy items below, leafy items on topChilled at pack-out; packed only against the {{delivery_sla_hyperlocal}} lane; harvest and pack date on the labelNo crushing, no free liquid, liner intact
Corporate giftingRigid gift box, branded sleeve, ribbon and insert card per the currently approved Packaging ConfigurationEach component seated in its own recess; outer transit carton over the gift boxPresentation surface unmarked; no price or internal documents inside the gift boxRecipient list, personalisation and item count matched against the order line

Every class additionally requires: recyclable or reusable outer cartons and paper-based void fill wherever the class instruction permits; plastic used only where moisture retention or food safety demands it; consumables reused only if structurally sound and unmarked; and no third-party or vendor branding on the outer carton.

Procedures

  1. Confirm the order lane and product class before pulling any material; courier consignments take the reinforced specification.
  2. Stage the item, inspect it against the quality standard and reject damaged or diseased stock back to inventory before packing.
  3. Prepare the goods: wrap the root ball, plug drainage holes, sheath sharp parts, chill produce.
  4. Protect: immobilise inside the carton so no product face contacts a carton wall and nothing shifts on inversion.
  5. Ventilate and retain moisture as the class instruction requires; never seal a live plant in an unvented carton.
  6. Add brand items — care card, sleeve, invoice as required by the invoicing policy — then complete the pre-seal check.
  7. Photograph the open packed carton and the sealed, labelled carton; both images are retained as claim evidence for at least {{replacement_evidence_window}}.
  8. Seal, apply orientation and handling marks, and hand over to the rider or courier against the dispatch SOP.

Exceptions

Deviations are permitted only for oversized specimens, customer-requested gift presentation, or a documented consumable stock-out where a like-for-like or better substitute exists. Any deviation requires Fulfilment Supervisor approval before sealing and must be recorded against the order. Substituting a lower specification, omitting ventilation on live goods, or shipping FarmBox produce on the courier lane are never permitted exceptions.

Compliance

Supervisors audit a sample of packed consignments each shift. Operations reviews class instructions and the Packaging Configuration at {{review_frequency_default}}, and sooner if damage or plant-mortality claims cluster on a class, lane, city or vendor. Vendor packing quality is tracked against {{vendor_quality_target}} and {{vendor_return_rate_threshold}}, with findings fed into the vendor scorecard.

Violations

A consignment failing the pre-seal check is held and repacked, not dispatched. Repeated non-compliance by internal staff is handled as a performance matter under the applicable HR policy. Repeated non-compliance by a vendor attracts {{penalty_schedule}}, recovery of avoidable replacement and return-leg costs, and may lead to suspension of order allocation or termination under the vendor agreement.

title: Hyperlocal Delivery SOP
html:
DRAFT — LEGAL REVIEW REQUIRED. This document is an operational or legal draft and must be reviewed and approved by authorized management and, where required, qualified legal counsel before becoming effective.

Purpose

This procedure defines how PlantAtHome, a brand of Silvestrix Green LLP, books, hands over, tracks and closes same-day rider deliveries in serviceable cities. It exists so that the hyperlocal lane runs identically across the Delivery Desk, the master fulfilment point and approved nursery vendors, so live plants spend the least possible time in transit, and so every delivery attempt leaves a record that can be defended to a customer, a delivery partner or a payment gateway.

Scope

Applies to every order or vendor shipment group routed to the hyperlocal lane — live plants, pots and planters, tools, seeds, fertilizers, accessories, FarmBox fresh produce and corporate gifting consignments — whether picked from the master fulfilment point or directly from an approved vendor nursery, prepaid or COD. It excludes pan-India courier shipments, which follow the Courier Delivery SOP, and customer self-collection. Where one order sources from more than one pickup point, each shipment group is booked, tracked and closed separately under this SOP.

Definitions

  • Hyperlocal lane — point-to-point same-day delivery by a rider engaged through an integrated delivery partner.
  • Shipment group — the line items sourced from a single pickup point, booked as one rider task.
  • Booking attempt — one request to a delivery partner, recorded with the partner's own order reference and status; a shipment may carry several booking attempts.
  • Handover — physical transfer of sealed, labelled packages from the pickup point to the assigned rider.
  • Proof of delivery (POD) — the partner-returned confirmation: recipient name, timestamp, geo-point, and photograph or delivery OTP where the partner supports it.
  • Failed attempt — a task closed without POD, including customer unreachable, address unreachable, refusal, and rider cancellation after pickup.

Roles and Responsibilities

  • Delivery Desk Coordinator — quotes, books, monitors and closes rider tasks; owns proactive customer contact during transit.
  • Pickup point (master packer or vendor dispatch) — packs to standard, verifies contents against the pick list, and completes handover checks.
  • Customer Support — handles inbound contact, reschedules, and records customer delivery instructions on the order.
  • Operations Lead — approves re-booking after repeated failure, lane changes, and any goodwill remedy within {{approval_limit_refund}}.
  • Finance — reconciles COD remittance and delivery partner invoices against booked tasks.

Prerequisites

  • Delivery pincode confirmed serviceable for the hyperlocal lane, and the vendor opted in for that area.
  • Live partner credentials configured for the operating environment, with the partner enabled in the Delivery Integration Configuration.
  • Packages sealed, labelled and, for fragile goods, packed per the Fragile Handling SOP.
  • Pickup address, contact number, package weight and dimensions, and COD amount present on the shipment record.
  • Customer contact number verified for WhatsApp, email or SMS notification.

Trigger

The shipment group reaches ready-for-pickup: payment success for prepaid orders, or order confirmation for COD orders, after vendor acceptance within {{vendor_acceptance_sla}} and packing within {{vendor_dispatch_sla}}. Auto-booking may raise the task without human action; the Coordinator still owns the outcome.

Step-by-Step Procedure

  1. Open the shipment group and confirm lane selection. Request quotes; the returned list spans both lanes, but a single quote belongs to one lane only — never book a courier quote as a rider task.
  2. Verify drop latitude and longitude are populated and plausible. A zero or missing geo-point causes partners to refuse or misprice the quote; correct the address before booking.
  3. Book the task and confirm a partner reference is returned. If booking fails, read the partner error verbatim, correct the named field, and re-book. Do not create duplicate tasks for the same shipment group.
  4. Notify the customer over the configured channel that a rider is assigned, with the tracking link.
  5. At the pickup point, complete handover checks: package count against the task, seal intact, label matches the order, fragile orientation observed, plant upright and watered per dispatch guidance, and COD amount read back to the rider.
  6. Record handover on the shipment. Photograph the sealed packages if the order contains fragile or high-value items.
  7. Monitor status transitions. Where the partner sends no webhook, rely on the scheduled reconciliation against the authenticated tracking endpoint; treat any inbound callback as a trigger to re-verify, never as the final authority.
  8. On delivery, capture POD onto the order timeline and release the customer-facing delivery confirmation.
  9. On a failed attempt, contact the customer, agree a re-attempt window, and re-book within the allowance in {{delivery_attempts}}. Log the failure reason from the partner.
  10. Where re-attempts are exhausted, initiate return to the pickup point, restore inventory on receipt, and route any refund through the Returns and Refunds Policy.
  11. For COD, confirm collected value against the task before marking the order complete, and hand the reconciliation to Finance.

SLA

MilestoneOwnerTarget
Booking raised after ready-for-pickupDelivery DeskAs per the currently approved Delivery Booking Configuration
Packed and handed to riderPickup point{{vendor_dispatch_sla}}
Handover to PODDelivery partner{{delivery_sla_hyperlocal}}
Re-attempts before returnDelivery Desk{{delivery_attempts}}
First response to a delivery queryCustomer Support{{support_response_sla}}
Live plant condition claim acceptedCustomer Support{{live_plant_claim_window}}

Quality Checks

  • Every completed task carries a POD artefact; a shipment marked delivered without one is reopened.
  • Booking attempts per shipment are reviewed against duplicates and cancelled tasks at {{review_frequency_default}}.
  • Failure reasons are sampled for address-quality defects and fed back to the address capture flow.
  • Partner invoices are matched line by line to booked tasks before payment.

Exceptions

Oversized or heavy planters that exceed the rider vehicle class configured for the partner are re-routed to a larger vehicle class or to the courier lane with Operations Lead approval. Deliveries into gated premises, offices or corporate gifting drops that require scheduled entry are booked to an agreed slot rather than immediate dispatch. Where a serviceable pincode is temporarily unreachable due to weather, civic restriction or partner outage, the Coordinator holds the shipment, informs the customer, and records the hold reason on the order.

Escalation Process

Unassigned riders, stalled tasks and unreachable customers escalate from the Delivery Desk to the Operations Lead, and thereafter to the partner's account contact, on the steps in {{escalation_timeline}}. Incidents involving lost consignments, injury, or damage to customer property are raised under {{incident_severity_model}} and notified to management the same working session. Repeated partner failure is logged against the partner for review under {{penalty_schedule}}.

Records and Audit Trail

The order timeline retains booking attempts, partner references, status transitions, handover confirmation, POD artefacts, customer notifications and failure reasons. Photographs and PODs are stored in the media library keyed to the shipment. Records are retained for {{data_retention_period}} and are the evidence base for consumer complaints, partner claims and payment disputes.

Related Documents

  • Shipping and Delivery Policy
  • Returns and Refunds Policy
  • Customer Support Escalation SOP

title: Courier Delivery SOP
html:
DRAFT — LEGAL REVIEW REQUIRED. This document is an operational or legal draft and must be reviewed and approved by authorized management and, where required, qualified legal counsel before becoming effective.

Purpose

This procedure defines how PlantAtHome, a brand of Silvestrix Green LLP, ships orders pan-India through courier partners engaged via an aggregator: selecting a service, generating the air waybill, producing label, invoice and manifest, releasing the consignment at pickup, following tracking events, and closing exceptions such as non-delivery and return to origin. It exists so that shipments leave the building with correct paperwork the first time and so that every courier exception has an owner.

Scope

Applies to all consignments outside hyperlocal serviceable areas, and to consignments inside those areas that are re-routed to courier because of size, weight or scheduling. Covers pots and planters, tools, seeds, fertilizers, accessories and corporate gifting. Live plants ship by courier only where the variety is approved for courier transit in the master catalogue. Excludes rider deliveries, which follow the Hyperlocal Delivery SOP, and FarmBox fresh produce, which is not courier-eligible.

Definitions

  • Aggregator — the integrated platform through which courier services are rated, booked and tracked.
  • AWB — air waybill, the courier-issued tracking number that identifies the consignment. Labels, manifests and pickup requests are all keyed to an assigned AWB.
  • Manifest — the consolidated handover sheet listing the AWBs released to a courier in one pickup.
  • Volumetric weight — dimensional weight derived from package size; the courier charges on the greater of dead and volumetric weight.
  • NDR — non-delivery report raised by the courier after an unsuccessful attempt.
  • RTO — return to origin, the consignment's journey back to the pickup address after attempts are exhausted or the customer refuses.

Roles and Responsibilities

  • Shipping Desk — rates, books, generates paperwork, raises pickups and works the daily exception queue.
  • Pickup point (master packer or vendor dispatch) — packs, weighs, measures, affixes label and invoice, and releases against the manifest.
  • Customer Support — contacts the customer on NDR, captures re-attempt instructions and communicates delays.
  • Operations Lead — approves lane changes, courier switches, RTO decisions and claim filings.
  • Finance — validates freight and weight-discrepancy charges, and reconciles COD remittance.

Prerequisites

  • Aggregator credentials active for the environment, and the pickup address registered and verified with the aggregator.
  • Seller account documentation complete; label, manifest and pickup generation are blocked while account verification is pending.
  • Accurate dead weight and all three package dimensions recorded on the shipment.
  • Delivery pincode confirmed serviceable, and prepaid or COD mode set correctly on the order.
  • Fragile consignments packed and evidenced per the Fragile Handling SOP.

Trigger

The shipment group is packed and marked ready to ship, and the delivery address falls outside the hyperlocal lane, or an Operations Lead has re-routed it to courier.

Step-by-Step Procedure

  1. Open the shipment group, confirm weight and dimensions, and request rates. Compare the returned services on price, transit estimate and past performance; select one service. A quote belongs to one lane only.
  2. Create the courier order and request AWB assignment. Confirm the AWB is returned and stored on the shipment.
  3. If assignment fails, read the recorded assignment error before retrying. Typical causes are an unregistered or unverified pickup address, incomplete seller verification, a non-serviceable destination pincode, or weight and dimensions outside the selected service. Fix the named cause; repeated blind retries create orphan orders.
  4. Generate the label and the packing slip. Raise the GST invoice within {{gst_invoice_timeline}} and enclose it with the consignment; the invoice is order-keyed and can be produced even where AWB-dependent paperwork is unavailable.
  5. Affix the label to the largest flat face, clear of seams and tape, with the barcode unobstructed. For multi-package consignments, label each package and mark its sequence.
  6. Add the AWB to the day's manifest and raise the pickup request for the courier.
  7. At handover, count packages against the manifest, obtain the courier representative's acknowledgement, and record the handover on each shipment.
  8. Follow tracking events daily until delivery. Investigate any consignment with no movement beyond the threshold in the approved Courier Exception Configuration.
  9. On NDR, contact the customer within {{support_response_sla}}, confirm address or availability, and submit the re-attempt instruction to the courier within the allowance in {{delivery_attempts}}.
  10. Where attempts are exhausted or the customer refuses, authorise RTO. On receipt, inspect, photograph, restock saleable goods and process any refund under the Returns and Refunds Policy within {{refund_processing_time}}.
  11. For loss or in-transit damage, assemble the claim pack — packing evidence, invoice, label image, tracking history, customer report — and file within the courier's claim window as stated in the approved Courier Claims Configuration.
  12. Retrieve and attach POD for delivered consignments, and close the shipment.

SLA

MilestoneOwnerTarget
AWB assigned after ready to shipShipping DeskAs per the currently approved Courier Booking Configuration
Packed and manifestedPickup point{{vendor_dispatch_sla}}
Pickup to deliveryCourier partner{{delivery_sla_courier}}
NDR worked and instruction submittedCustomer Support{{support_response_sla}}
Delivery attempts before RTOShipping Desk{{delivery_attempts}}
Refund after RTO receipt and inspectionFinance{{refund_processing_time}}

Quality Checks

  • No consignment leaves without label, packing slip and tax invoice; the manifest count must equal the physical package count.
  • Weight-discrepancy notices are matched against recorded dimensions before acceptance, and disputed with packing photographs where they disagree.
  • Aged shipments — assigned AWB but never picked up — are reviewed daily and cancelled or re-booked.
  • Courier-level delivery success, NDR rate and RTO rate are reviewed at {{review_frequency_default}} and inform service selection.

Exceptions

Consignments containing restricted goods, oversized planters or fragile ceramics beyond the courier's accepted limits are held and re-routed to the hyperlocal lane or a surface freight arrangement with Operations Lead approval. Where a destination becomes non-serviceable after booking, the AWB is cancelled and the order re-rated. Corporate gifting bulk drops may be consolidated into a single consignment with a delivery contact named on the label.

Escalation Process

Missed pickups, stalled tracking, repeated NDR without a genuine attempt and disputed weight charges escalate from the Shipping Desk to the Operations Lead and then to the aggregator's account manager along {{escalation_timeline}}. Suspected loss or theft is raised under {{incident_severity_model}}. Persistent courier underperformance is documented for commercial review under {{penalty_schedule}}.

Records and Audit Trail

Each shipment retains the rate selection, courier order and AWB, assignment errors, label and manifest references, invoice number, pickup acknowledgement, tracking event history, NDR notes, RTO inspection photographs and POD. Claim packs are stored against the shipment. Records are retained for {{data_retention_period}}.

Related Documents

  • Fragile Handling SOP
  • Shipping and Delivery Policy
  • Returns and Refunds Policy
  • Vendor Onboarding and Compliance SOP

title: Fragile Handling SOP
html:
DRAFT — LEGAL REVIEW REQUIRED. This document is an operational or legal draft and must be reviewed and approved by authorized management and, where required, qualified legal counsel before becoming effective.

Purpose

This procedure defines how PlantAtHome, a brand of Silvestrix Green LLP, packs, labels, photographs and dispatches breakable and heavy goods — ceramic and terracotta pots, glass planters and terrariums, cement and stone planters, and glazed decorative accessories — so that they survive rider and courier transit, and so that when a package does arrive damaged the business holds the evidence needed to settle with the customer and recover from the carrier or vendor.

Scope

Applies at every pickup point — the master fulfilment point and every approved nursery vendor — to any item flagged fragile or heavy in the master catalogue, to buy-with-pot combinations where a plant ships inside a breakable pot, and to corporate gifting sets containing ceramics or glass. It applies to both delivery lanes, with the stricter courier standard used whenever the lane is not yet fixed at packing time.

Definitions

  • Fragile class — the packing tier assigned to an item in the approved Packaging Standard Configuration, derived from material, wall thickness, weight and glaze.
  • Double-boxing — an inner carton holding the wrapped item, seated inside a larger outer carton with cushioning on all sides, so no rigid contact path reaches the item.
  • Void fill — cushioning that occupies empty space and stops movement; it is not the same as suspension, which holds the item away from every wall.
  • Dunnage — rigid inserts, corner blocks and dividers that carry stacking load around the item.
  • Evidence pack — the photographs and records captured before sealing and at handover that prove condition and packing at dispatch.

Roles and Responsibilities

  • Packer — classifies the item, packs to the matrix below, labels, and captures the evidence pack.
  • Pickup point supervisor — spot-checks packed consignments before handover and signs off heavy items.
  • Vendor dispatch — applies the same standard for vendor-fulfilled orders; non-compliance is recorded against the vendor.
  • Delivery Desk and Shipping Desk — refuse handover of consignments that fail the pre-dispatch check.
  • Customer Support — collects customer damage evidence and opens the claim.
  • Operations Lead — approves remedies, vendor recovery and carrier claim filing.

Prerequisites

  • Packing materials in stock: corrugated cartons in the approved sizes, bubble or foam wrap, corner blocks, kraft or air-pillow void fill, edge protectors, water-resistant tape and fragile labels.
  • Item fragile class visible on the pick list.
  • Camera or scanner-linked device available at the packing bench for the evidence pack.
  • Weighing scale and measuring tape at the bench, since double-boxing changes both billable weight and lane eligibility.

Trigger

A pick list contains an item flagged fragile or heavy, or a plant is being paired with a ceramic, glass or cement pot at packing.

Step-by-Step Procedure

  1. Inspect the item before packing. Reject chipped, hairline-cracked or crazed stock back to inventory; never pack a defect and hope it passes.
  2. Empty and plug drainage holes, and stuff hollow cavities so the walls are supported from inside. Detach and wrap saucers, lids and loose parts separately.
  3. Wrap the item completely, covering rim, base and any handle or spout, and secure the wrap so it cannot unroll in transit.
  4. Seat the wrapped item in the inner carton with cushioning beneath it first, then around it, so the item does not touch any inner wall. Shake the closed inner carton: audible or felt movement means repack.
  5. Place the inner carton centrally in the outer carton on a cushioned base, fill every remaining void, and add corner blocks or edge protectors for stacking load.
  6. Where a plant ships potted in a breakable container, immobilise the root ball, protect the foliage with a collar, and orient the package upright; the pot is packed to its own fragile class, not to the plant's.
  7. Seal the outer carton with taped centre seam and both edge seams. Reinforce base seams on heavy consignments.
  8. Label: fragile and orientation marks on opposing faces, a heavy-item mark and two-person lift notice where the weight class requires it, and the shipping label flat on an unobstructed face.
  9. Capture the evidence pack: the item in the inner carton before closure, the inner carton seated in the outer, and the sealed outer carton showing all six faces and the label.
  10. Weigh and measure the finished package, record both on the shipment, and confirm the booked lane still accepts it.
  11. Hand over only after the supervisor's pre-dispatch check. Note any carrier remark or refusal on the shipment.
  12. On a reported damage, collect the customer's photographs of packaging and contents within {{replacement_evidence_window}}, match them against the evidence pack, and route the remedy through the Returns and Refunds Policy while the Operations Lead files the carrier or vendor claim.

SLA

Fragile classInner protectionOuter constructionLabellingEvidence required
Glass and terrariumsFull wrap, cavity support, suspension or full void fill as per the approved Packaging Standard ConfigurationDouble-boxed, cushioned on all sidesFragile and orientation marks on opposing facesFull evidence pack
Ceramic and glazed potsFull wrap, plugged drainage, wrapped saucer packed separatelyDouble-boxed with corner blocksFragile and orientation marksFull evidence pack
TerracottaFull wrap with rim and base reinforcementSingle carton with dunnage, double-boxed for courier laneFragile markSealed-carton photographs
Cement, stone and heavy plantersWrap plus rigid base supportReinforced carton or crate as per the approved Packaging Standard ConfigurationFragile, orientation and two-person lift marksFull evidence pack and supervisor sign-off
Plant potted in a breakable containerRoot ball immobilised, foliage collar, pot packed to its own classPer the pot's class, upright orientation enforcedFragile, orientation and live plant marksFull evidence pack

Packing must be completed inside the dispatch window in {{vendor_dispatch_sla}}; a fragile consignment is never released early at the cost of the checks above.

Quality Checks

  • Supervisor spot-check on a sample of fragile consignments each dispatch session, using the shake test and the label check.
  • Damage rate tracked by fragile class, pickup point and carrier, and reviewed at {{review_frequency_default}}.
  • Vendor damage rate assessed against {{vendor_quality_target}} and {{vendor_return_rate_threshold}}.
  • Consignments dispatched without a complete evidence pack are recorded as a packing defect regardless of whether they arrive intact.

Exceptions

Items too large or too heavy for the approved carton range are crated or moved to the hyperlocal lane with a larger vehicle class. Customer-requested gift wrapping is applied to the inner carton only, never in place of protection. Where approved packing materials are unavailable, the consignment is held rather than under-packed, and the shortage is raised to the Operations Lead the same session.

Escalation Process

A failed pre-dispatch check goes to the pickup point supervisor for repack. Repeat failures at one pickup point, or a damage cluster on one carrier, route, or vendor, escalate to the Operations Lead along {{escalation_timeline}} and are treated under {{incident_severity_model}} where customer safety or high-value corporate gifting is involved. Vendor recovery follows {{penalty_schedule}}.

Records and Audit Trail

Evidence packs are stored in the media library keyed to the shipment, alongside the packing class applied, packer identity, finished weight and dimensions, supervisor sign-off, carrier handover acknowledgement, customer damage evidence and claim outcome. Records are retained for {{data_retention_period}} and are the primary defence in carrier claims and consumer complaints.

title: Vendor Inventory Policy
html:
DRAFT — LEGAL REVIEW REQUIRED. This document is an operational or legal draft and must be reviewed and approved by authorized management and, where required, qualified legal counsel before becoming effective.

Purpose

This policy defines the inventory accuracy obligations of nursery vendors and other approved suppliers who list stock into the PlantAtHome master catalogue operated by Silvestrix Green LLP. Live plants, seeds and FarmBox produce are perishable, seasonal and individually variable, and a large share of PlantAtHome orders carry a same-day hyperlocal delivery promise. Stock that is published but not physically present converts directly into a cancelled order, an avoidable refund and a broken commitment to the customer. This policy sets the standard for how vendor stock is published, reserved, corrected and audited.

Scope

This policy applies to every active vendor account on the PlantAtHome vendor portal, to every SKU mapped to that vendor in the master catalogue, and to every route through which stock reaches the platform — portal edits, bulk spreadsheet import, and any approved integration or feed. It covers plants, pots and planters, gardening tools, seeds, fertilizers, accessories, FarmBox produce and any bundle whose components the vendor supplies. It binds vendor owners, vendor staff holding catalogue access, and the PlantAtHome category and operations teams who review vendor stock.

Definitions

  • Available Stock — units the vendor holds in saleable, grade-compliant condition at the registered pickup location and not committed to any other channel.
  • Reserved Stock — units held against a placed PlantAtHome order and no longer offered for sale.
  • Stock Tracking — the per-SKU setting that makes the platform decrement inventory automatically when an order is placed.
  • Discrepancy — any difference between published and physical stock, however discovered.
  • Oversell — acceptance of an order the vendor cannot fulfil because published stock exceeded physical stock.
  • Cycle Count — a scheduled physical count of a defined subset of SKUs, reconciled against the platform figure.
  • Availability Gate — platform logic that hides a SKU from a customer's city when no serviceable vendor holds stock.

Policy Statement

Published stock is a supply commitment, not an estimate. A vendor showing a quantity against a SKU warrants that those units exist, meet the catalogue grade and size description, and will be released to PlantAtHome ahead of any other sales channel until the order is dispatched or formally cancelled. Vendors must operate a single source of truth for stock: where the vendor also sells at a nursery counter, on another marketplace or in bulk, the PlantAtHome figure must be reduced as those sales occur.

Out of stock is an acceptable and fully reversible state. Overselling is not. Quoting an unrealistic price, withholding order acceptance or stalling dispatch are never acceptable substitutes for marking a SKU out of stock.

Responsibilities

  • Vendor owner — accountable for stock accuracy on the account, nominates staff with catalogue access, and ensures cycle counts are performed and signed off.
  • Vendor catalogue staff — publish updates at every triggering event and raise discrepancies rather than absorbing them silently.
  • PlantAtHome category team — monitors accuracy metrics, approves bulk imports and validates seasonal delistings.
  • PlantAtHome operations and support — reroute or cancel affected orders, inform the customer, and log every failure against the vendor scorecard.
  • PlantAtHome finance — applies recoveries arising from oversell in the settlement run.

Policy Requirements

Stock must be refreshed on each of the events below. Timing references the currently approved Inventory Update Configuration and the vendor's contracted service levels; no figure in this table is fixed by this document.

EventRequired vendor actionTiming
New intake, potting batch or harvest readyPublish available quantity, grade and pot size before the listing is offeredAs per the currently approved Inventory Update Configuration
Sale through any non-PlantAtHome channelDecrement the PlantAtHome quantity by the units soldSame working session, as per the currently approved Inventory Update Configuration
Plant mortality, pest damage or breakageDecrement and record the loss reasonAs per the currently approved Inventory Update Configuration
Seasonal or weather-driven unavailabilitySet the SKU out of stock with a reason code; do not delete the listingBefore the next order routing window
Accepted order cannot be fulfilledRaise a discrepancy on the order, never cancel silentlyWithin {{vendor_acceptance_sla}}
Cycle count variance foundCorrect to the counted figure and submit the count sheetSame day as the count

Procedures

  1. Update stock through the vendor portal, or through the approved import template for bulk changes; ad-hoc changes requested over chat or phone are not actioned.
  2. On order placement the platform reserves stock automatically for tracked SKUs; the vendor confirms availability at acceptance within {{vendor_acceptance_sla}}.
  3. Where stock is short, the vendor raises a discrepancy with the counted quantity so operations can reroute the line to another serviceable vendor before the customer is contacted.
  4. Cycle counts are performed on the schedule set by the category team, covering fast-moving and high-value SKUs first, with sheets retained for audit.
  5. Repeated variance on a SKU triggers a full physical audit of that SKU group, jointly attended by the category team where required.
  6. Accuracy, oversell and cancellation data feed the vendor scorecard reviewed at {{review_frequency_default}}.

Exceptions

Temporary exceptions may be granted in writing by the category head, for example a made-to-order or grow-on SKU listed against a stated lead time, a nursery closure for weather or pest treatment, or a migration window during onboarding. Verbal assurances create no exception. Any exception states the SKUs covered and its end date, and is reviewed before renewal.

Compliance

Inventory accuracy is a scored measure on the Vendor Service Level Agreement scorecard. PlantAtHome may audit vendor stock records, count sheets and pickup-location holdings on reasonable notice. Sustained failure to meet the accuracy target results in reduced order routing, removal of the vendor from the availability gate for affected cities, or suspension of listing rights until a corrective action plan is completed.

Violations

Oversell, unreported discrepancy, and publishing stock the vendor does not hold are treated as breaches under the Vendor Penalty Matrix, with recoveries applied through the settlement run in line with {{penalty_schedule}}. Deliberate misstatement of stock to win order routing is treated as misrepresentation and may lead to termination of the vendor agreement.

Related Documents

  • Vendor Service Level Agreement
  • Vendor Penalty Matrix
  • Vendor Settlement Policy
  • Vendor Returns Handling Policy
  • Vendor Packaging Standards

title: Vendor Settlement Policy
html:
DRAFT — LEGAL REVIEW REQUIRED. This document is an operational or legal draft and must be reviewed and approved by authorized management and, where required, qualified legal counsel before becoming effective.

Purpose

This policy sets out how Silvestrix Green LLP calculates, deducts from, reconciles and releases payouts to nursery vendors and other approved suppliers who fulfil PlantAtHome orders. It exists so that every vendor can reproduce its own payout from the order ledger without asking anyone, and so that disputes are raised against a defined statement rather than a remembered conversation.

Scope

This policy covers all orders fulfilled by a vendor across plants, pots and planters, tools, seeds, fertilizers, accessories, FarmBox produce and corporate gifting, on both hyperlocal and pan-India courier lanes, prepaid or cash on delivery. It covers commission, recoveries, refund and return adjustments, penalties, taxes withheld at source and the dispute process. It does not cover pricing or catalogue margin construction, which sit with the category team.

Definitions

  • Settlement Cycle — the recurring period in which eligible orders are aggregated and paid, as defined by {{vendor_settlement_cycle}}.
  • Eligible Order — a delivered order line that has cleared the applicable return or claim window and carries no open dispute or fraud hold.
  • Vendor Payable — the vendor's agreed supply value for a line, before deductions.
  • Deduction — any commission, recovery, penalty, refund adjustment or statutory withholding applied against the vendor payable.
  • Settlement Statement — the line-level statement issued for each cycle showing gross value, every deduction with its reason code, and the net amount released.
  • Hold — a temporary block on a payout or part of a payout pending investigation, KYC completion or bank verification.

Policy Statement

PlantAtHome settles vendors on a fixed cycle against a transparent, line-level statement. Every deduction must carry a reason code that traces to an order, a return, a documented penalty event or a statutory obligation. Deductions are never applied retrospectively without a statement line, and the vendor always has a defined window to contest one. Payouts are released only to the bank account verified against the vendor's KYC records, and only while KYC and GST registration details remain valid.

Responsibilities

  • Vendor — keeps KYC, GST and bank details current, issues compliant tax invoices for supplies, and raises disputes with evidence inside the dispute window.
  • PlantAtHome finance — runs the cycle, issues statements, applies deductions with reason codes and releases net payouts.
  • PlantAtHome operations — confirms delivery, return and damage outcomes that determine eligibility.
  • PlantAtHome category team — owns the agreed supply price and commission arrangement for each vendor and SKU group.

Policy Requirements

Deductions are limited to the categories below. Rates and amounts are held in configuration and in the vendor's signed commercial annexure, not in this document.

DeductionBasisValue reference
Platform commissionPer eligible delivered line{{commission_model}}
Delivery cost recoveryWhere the vendor agreement places the shipping cost with the vendorAs per the currently approved Shipping Cost Configuration
Refund adjustmentCustomer refund on a line already settled or pending settlementRefund value attributable to the vendor line
Return and reverse-pickup recoveryReturn accepted on grounds attributable to the vendorAs per the currently approved Returns Cost Configuration
Service level penaltiesConfirmed breach recorded on the vendor scorecard{{penalty_schedule}}
Statutory withholdingTax deducted or collected at source on marketplace suppliesRates prescribed under the Income-tax Act, 1961 and the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017
Advances and recoverablesAny advance, packaging material charge or agreed recoverableAs recorded in the vendor commercial annexure

Procedures

  1. At the close of each {{vendor_settlement_cycle}}, delivered lines that have cleared {{return_request_window}}, and live plant lines that have cleared {{live_plant_claim_window}}, are marked eligible.
  2. Cancelled, undelivered, returned and disputed lines are excluded; a line returned after settlement is recovered in the following cycle as a refund adjustment.
  3. Deductions are applied in the order shown above, and statutory withholding is computed on the value prescribed by law rather than on the net figure.
  4. The settlement statement is published to the vendor portal with a downloadable line-level breakdown and reason codes.
  5. Net payout is released to the verified bank account; a failed transfer is retried against corrected bank details supplied by the vendor.
  6. Withholding certificates and the platform's tax statements are made available for the vendor's own return filing.

Exceptions

Payouts may be withheld in whole or in part where KYC or GST registration has lapsed, where bank details fail verification, where a fraud or chargeback investigation is open, or where a court, tax authority or payment partner directs a hold. Off-cycle payouts are exceptional, require finance head approval within {{approval_limit_expense}}, and are adjusted in the next regular cycle.

Compliance

Statements, invoices and withholding records are retained for {{data_retention_period}}. Vendors must issue tax invoices in line with {{gst_invoice_timeline}} and reconcile settlement statements against their own books each cycle. PlantAtHome reserves the right to audit vendor invoices and supporting documents where a mismatch is identified.

Violations

Raising a dispute after {{vendor_settlement_dispute_window}} closes the claim for that cycle, save where PlantAtHome finds a platform error. Invoicing for goods not supplied, inflating supply values, or presenting invoices that do not match the settled lines is treated as fraud under the Vendor Penalty Matrix, and may result in immediate suspension of payouts, recovery of amounts already released, and termination of the vendor agreement.
