  • Vendor Penalty Matrix
  • Vendor Returns Handling Policy
  • Vendor Inventory Policy

title: Vendor Packaging Standards
html:
DRAFT — LEGAL REVIEW REQUIRED. This document is an operational or legal draft and must be reviewed and approved by authorized management and, where required, qualified legal counsel before becoming effective.

Purpose

This standard defines how vendors must pack goods supplied to PlantAtHome customers. Packaging is the single largest controllable driver of damage claims, replacement cost and negative reviews in this business: a plant travels upright, alive and thirsty; a ceramic planter travels heavy and brittle; fertilizer travels as a spill risk beside both. The standard exists so that a parcel packed by any vendor arrives in the same condition and presents the same brand experience as one packed in-house.

Scope

This standard applies to all vendor-fulfilled shipments across both delivery lanes — same-day hyperlocal rider and pan-India courier — and across every category: live plants, pots and planters, gardening tools, seeds, fertilizers, accessories, FarmBox produce and corporate gifting. Courier consignments are held to the stricter requirements throughout, since they endure sorting, stacking and longer transit. Category-specific packing sequences are published as separate packaging SOPs, which this standard governs.

Definitions

  • Primary packaging — the material in direct contact with the product: sleeve, root wrap, pot bag, seed pouch or tool sheath.
  • Secondary packaging — the outer carton or crate presented to the rider or courier.
  • Void fill — cushioning material that immobilises contents inside the carton.
  • Ventilation — deliberate airflow openings in live-plant cartons.
  • Fragile line — ceramic, terracotta, glass, or any item flagged fragile in the master catalogue.
  • Packaging SOP — the category-level procedure listing the exact materials and packing sequence for a product group.

Policy Statement

Every shipment must survive its intended lane without movement inside the carton, without soil escape, and without water pooling on other items. Live plants are packed to keep the root ball moist, the pot immobilised and the foliage unbent, with airflow. Packaging is also brand surface: cartons, tapes, inserts and labels must follow the approved PlantAtHome presentation, and no vendor branding, invoice of the vendor's own, or third-party marketing material may be inserted into a customer parcel.

Responsibilities

  • Vendor — sources approved materials, trains packing staff on the applicable packaging SOP, and packs to this standard for every order.
  • Vendor packing supervisor — performs the pre-handover check and is accountable for what leaves the nursery.
  • PlantAtHome category and quality team — publishes packaging SOPs, approves materials and runs packaging audits.
  • PlantAtHome operations — records packaging-related damage claims against the originating vendor.

Policy Requirements

RequirementStandard
MaterialsCorrugated cartons of the grade specified for the lane and weight band in the approved Packaging Material Configuration; no reused cartons carrying other brands' printing
Product protectionContents immobilised with void fill; no product touching an outer wall on a courier consignment
VentilationLive-plant cartons carry ventilation openings per the applicable Packaging SOP; sealed unventilated cartons are not permitted for live plants
Moisture controlRoot ball watered and wrapped to hold moisture without free water; liner between soil and carton; fertilizers and liquids double-sealed and never packed above textiles or foliage
Fragile handlingCorner protection, fragile marking on the outer, and separation of ceramic or glass items from heavier goods in the same consignment
LabellingPlatform shipping label applied flat and scannable; orientation and handling marks visible; statutory declarations for pre-packaged goods as required under the Legal Metrology Act, 2009 and applicable rules
Brand presentationApproved PlantAtHome tape, care card and insert set only; no vendor or third-party marketing inserts
SustainabilityRecyclable or reusable material preferred; plastic use minimised and reported in line with the Plastic Waste Management Rules, 2016

Procedures

  1. Pick the order and verify each line against the packing list before any material is opened.
  2. Apply the primary packaging defined in the category Packaging SOP for that product group.
  3. Select the carton size that leaves room for void fill without leaving the contents loose; do not oversize.
  4. Load heavy and fragile items first, immobilise, then place live plants upright with foliage clear of the closure line.
  5. Insert the approved care card and any gifting message; seal, then apply the shipping label and handling marks.
  6. Complete the pre-handover check: correct lines, no movement when the carton is tilted, no leakage, label scannable, ventilation intact.
  7. Photograph the packed consignment where the SOP requires it, so packaging evidence exists if a claim is raised within {{replacement_evidence_window}}.

Exceptions

Alternative materials may be used only with written approval from the category and quality team, normally after a trial consignment is reviewed. Oversized plants, crated corporate gifting orders and bulk FarmBox consignments follow their own approved packaging SOPs. Material shortages are not an exception: a vendor unable to pack to standard must hold the order and inform operations rather than ship sub-standard.

Compliance

Packaging quality is scored on the vendor scorecard through the damage rate and product quality measures in the Vendor Service Level Agreement. PlantAtHome may audit packing stations, sample outbound consignments and request material invoices, at a frequency no less than {{review_frequency_default}} for active vendors.

Violations

Damage, leakage or misdeclaration traced to packaging is charged to the originating vendor under the Vendor Penalty Matrix in line with {{penalty_schedule}}, together with the replacement or refund cost. Inserting third-party marketing material, or shipping goods without the statutory declarations required for pre-packaged commodities, is treated as a serious violation and may suspend order routing.

Related Documents

  • Vendor Service Level Agreement
  • Vendor Returns Handling Policy
  • Vendor Penalty Matrix
  • Vendor Inventory Policy

title: Vendor Service Level Agreement
html:
DRAFT — LEGAL REVIEW REQUIRED. This document is an operational or legal draft and must be reviewed and approved by authorized management and, where required, qualified legal counsel before becoming effective.

Purpose

This agreement defines the service levels a vendor must sustain to receive order routing from PlantAtHome, and the measures by which performance is scored. PlantAtHome sells a delivery promise as much as a plant: hyperlocal orders are promised same day, and courier orders are promised on a published transit estimate. Both promises are only as reliable as the vendor behind the line. This document converts that dependency into measurable, reviewable commitments.

Scope

This agreement applies to every active vendor account and to every order line routed to it, across all categories and both delivery lanes. It applies from the moment a line is routed to the vendor until the line is delivered, returned or cancelled, and it governs the scorecard used in vendor reviews, routing decisions and contract renewal.

Definitions

  • Routed line — an order line assigned to the vendor by the platform for fulfilment.
  • Acceptance — the vendor's confirmation on the portal that the line will be fulfilled at the stated quantity and grade.
  • Dispatch — handover of a packed consignment to the assigned rider or courier partner, evidenced by a scan or pickup confirmation.
  • Scorecard — the periodic performance record combining the measures in this agreement.
  • Measurement window — the rolling period over which each measure is computed, as set in the approved Vendor Scorecard Configuration.
  • Vendor-attributable — an outcome caused by vendor act or omission, as distinct from customer, courier, platform or force majeure causes.

Policy Statement

Vendors are measured on outcomes the customer experiences, not on effort. Every measure below is computed from platform data, over the approved measurement window, and only on vendor-attributable events. Targets are held in configuration so they can be tuned by category and city without reopening this agreement; they are never fixed in this text. Sustained performance above target earns higher routing priority and preferred placement in the master catalogue; sustained performance below target reduces routing before it results in penalties.

Responsibilities

  • Vendor owner — accountable for the scorecard, attends the performance review and owns any corrective action plan.
  • Vendor operations staff — accept, pack and dispatch within the contracted service levels and record exceptions honestly.
  • PlantAtHome category team — owns targets, runs reviews and adjusts routing weight.
  • PlantAtHome operations and support — attributes each failure to the correct party and maintains the evidence trail.

Policy Requirements

The KPI framework below forms the vendor scorecard. Targets and measurement windows are read from the currently approved Vendor Scorecard Configuration.

KPIWhat it measuresTarget reference
Order acceptance rateRouted lines accepted within {{vendor_acceptance_sla}}, as a share of lines routedAs per the currently approved Vendor Scorecard Configuration
Dispatch performanceAccepted lines handed to the rider or courier within {{vendor_dispatch_sla}}, supporting {{delivery_sla_hyperlocal}} and {{delivery_sla_courier}}As per the currently approved Vendor Scorecard Configuration
Product quality scoreAudit and inspection results on plant health, grade, size and finish against the catalogue description{{vendor_quality_target}}
Customer ratingPost-delivery ratings and reviews on lines supplied by the vendorAs per the currently approved Vendor Scorecard Configuration
Return rateVendor-attributable returns as a share of delivered lines{{vendor_return_rate_threshold}}
Damage rateLines with damage or leakage claims raised within {{replacement_evidence_window}} and traced to packing or handlingAs per the currently approved Vendor Scorecard Configuration
Cancellation rateLines cancelled after routing for vendor reasons, including stock-out and non-acceptanceAs per the currently approved Vendor Scorecard Configuration
Inventory accuracyCycle count variance and oversell incidents against published stockAs per the currently approved Vendor Scorecard Configuration
Support responsivenessVendor replies to operations and escalation queries within {{support_response_sla}}As per the currently approved Vendor Scorecard Configuration

Procedures

  1. The platform records acceptance, dispatch, delivery, return and claim events automatically; manual entries require an operations note and evidence.
  2. Each failure is attributed to vendor, courier, customer, platform or force majeure before it is scored; only vendor-attributable events count against the vendor.
  3. Scorecards are published to the vendor portal and reviewed with the vendor at {{review_frequency_default}}.
  4. A vendor below target on any measure agrees a corrective action plan with the category team, with named actions and a review date.
  5. Where the plan does not restore performance, routing weight is reduced, then restricted by city or category, then suspended.
  6. Attribution errors are corrected by raising a scorecard dispute with evidence, following the escalation path within {{escalation_timeline}}.

Exceptions

Measures are suspended for events outside vendor control that PlantAtHome accepts in writing: declared force majeure, courier partner outage, platform incident, or a city-level restriction. Onboarding vendors may be scored on an observation basis for their initial measurement window before targets apply. New categories added to an existing vendor may be granted a stated ramp period by the category head.

Compliance

Continued order routing depends on meeting these service levels. PlantAtHome may audit vendor records, packing stations and stock holdings to verify scorecard inputs, and may re-verify KYC before renewal. Scorecard data is retained for {{data_retention_period}}.

Violations

Breaches are handled under the Vendor Penalty Matrix, with financial consequences applied through the settlement run in line with {{penalty_schedule}}. Manipulating scorecard inputs — false dispatch scans, false acceptance, or misreported stock — is treated as a serious violation and grounds for immediate suspension and termination.

Related Documents

  • Vendor Penalty Matrix
  • Vendor Inventory Policy
  • Vendor Packaging Standards
  • Vendor Returns Handling Policy
  • Vendor Settlement Policy

title: Vendor Returns Handling Policy
html:
DRAFT — LEGAL REVIEW REQUIRED. This document is an operational or legal draft and must be reviewed and approved by authorized management and, where required, qualified legal counsel before becoming effective.

Purpose

This policy defines what a vendor must do when a PlantAtHome customer returns, rejects or claims against a line the vendor supplied. Returns in this business are unusual: a dead or damaged plant cannot wait in a queue, reverse pickup on the hyperlocal lane is often faster than on courier, and the evidence that decides the case is a photograph taken by a customer in the first hours after delivery. This policy sets the sequence, the evidence standard and the cost allocation so that customers are resolved quickly and vendors are charged fairly.

Scope

This policy applies to all vendor-fulfilled lines across every category and both delivery lanes, and covers customer-initiated returns, live plant health claims, damage and leakage claims, wrong or missing item claims, and refused or undelivered consignments returned to origin. It governs vendor obligations only; the customer-facing return entitlement is set out in the customer returns and refunds policy published on the storefront.

Definitions

  • Return request — a customer request raised within {{return_request_window}}, or within {{live_plant_claim_window}} for live plant health claims.
  • Claim evidence — photographs, unboxing media or written description submitted within {{replacement_evidence_window}}.
  • Reverse pickup — collection of the returned goods from the customer by rider or courier.
  • Inspection — the vendor's assessment of returned goods against the claim reason.
  • Vendor-attributable return — a return caused by wrong item, poor quality, unhealthy plant, packaging failure or short shipment.
  • Restock — return of a saleable unit to available stock after inspection.

Policy Statement

The customer outcome is decided by PlantAtHome, not by the vendor. Where a claim meets the published entitlement and the evidence standard, PlantAtHome will approve the refund or replacement and settle the customer first; cost allocation between PlantAtHome and the vendor is then resolved separately through inspection and the settlement run. A vendor may contest attribution but may not delay a customer resolution, refuse a reverse pickup, or contact the customer directly to negotiate.

Responsibilities

  • Vendor — acknowledges return notifications, accepts reverse pickups, inspects promptly, records findings with photographs and adjusts inventory.
  • PlantAtHome support — validates the claim against entitlement and evidence, communicates with the customer and approves the outcome.
  • PlantAtHome operations — schedules the reverse leg on the correct lane and attributes the return reason.
  • PlantAtHome finance — applies refund adjustments and return recoveries in the settlement statement.

Policy Requirements

Return reasonVendor obligationCost allocation
Wrong or missing itemConfirm the picked quantity from the packing record and dispatch the correct item on priorityVendor, per the currently approved Returns Cost Configuration
Unhealthy or dead plant on arrivalInspect returned unit or claim media; supply a replacement of equal gradeVendor where plant condition at dispatch is the cause
Damage or leakage in transitProvide packing photographs and material details for the consignmentVendor where packing failed the Vendor Packaging Standards; otherwise courier or platform
Product not as describedVerify against the catalogue grade, size and pot specificationVendor where the supplied unit differs from the listing
Customer change of mind, where permittedAccept the returned unit and restock if saleablePlatform, per the currently approved Returns Cost Configuration
Refused or undelivered consignmentReceive the return to origin, inspect and restockAs determined by the delivery attempt record and {{delivery_attempts}}

Procedures

  1. PlantAtHome notifies the vendor on the portal when a return or claim is raised against a vendor line, with the reason code and customer evidence.
  2. The vendor acknowledges within {{support_response_sla}}; no acknowledgement does not stall the customer outcome, which proceeds on the evidence held.
  3. Operations schedules the reverse leg; the vendor keeps the registered pickup location staffed to receive it.
  4. The vendor inspects on receipt, photographs the unit and records findings against the claim reason on the portal.
  5. Saleable units are restocked and the inventory figure updated the same day, in line with the Vendor Inventory Policy; unsaleable units are recorded as loss with the reason.
  6. Replacements are dispatched on the same service level as an original order, within {{vendor_dispatch_sla}}.
  7. Refunds approved by PlantAtHome are processed to the customer within {{refund_processing_time}}, and the corresponding vendor adjustment appears on the next settlement statement.
  8. Attribution disputes are raised with inspection evidence within {{vendor_settlement_dispute_window}} and escalated per {{escalation_timeline}}.

Exceptions

Claims raised outside the applicable window, or without evidence where evidence is required, are assessed case by case by support within {{approval_limit_refund}}. Perishable FarmBox produce and opened fertilizer or seed packs are not restocked and are recorded as loss regardless of the outcome. Corporate gifting consignments follow the resolution terms in the signed corporate order confirmation.

Compliance

Return rate and damage rate are scored measures under the Vendor Service Level Agreement. Inspection records, claim media and reverse pickup evidence are retained for {{data_retention_period}} and may be audited. Nothing in this policy limits customer rights under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019.

Violations

Refusing a reverse pickup, failing to inspect, restocking an unsaleable unit, or contacting a customer directly about a claim is a breach handled under the Vendor Penalty Matrix in line with {{penalty_schedule}}. Repeated vendor-attributable returns above {{vendor_return_rate_threshold}} reduce order routing and may lead to suspension of the affected SKU group.

Related Documents

  • Vendor Service Level Agreement
  • Vendor Settlement Policy
  • Vendor Packaging Standards
  • Vendor Penalty Matrix
  • Vendor Inventory Policy

title: Vendor Penalty Matrix
html:
DRAFT — LEGAL REVIEW REQUIRED. This document is an operational or legal draft and must be reviewed and approved by authorized management and, where required, qualified legal counsel before becoming effective.

Purpose

This document sets out the breaches for which PlantAtHome applies consequences to a vendor, how each breach is evidenced, and how the consequence escalates when the same breach repeats. Its purpose is predictability: a vendor should be able to read a breach code on a settlement statement and know exactly what it means, what evidence supports it, and what happens if it recurs.

Scope

This matrix applies to every active vendor account and to all vendor-fulfilled lines across categories and both delivery lanes. It covers operational breaches, quality and packaging breaches, inventory breaches, and conduct breaches including fraud. It is applied alongside the Vendor Service Level Agreement, which defines the measures, and the Vendor Settlement Policy, which defines how recoveries are deducted.

Definitions

  • Breach event — a single confirmed, vendor-attributable failure recorded against an order line or an account-level check.
  • Confirmation — attribution completed by operations, with the platform record or evidence that supports it.
  • Penalty — the financial consequence set by {{penalty_schedule}} and applied through the settlement run.
  • Operational consequence — a non-financial consequence such as reduced routing, category restriction, delisting or account suspension.
  • Repeat — a further breach event of the same code within the measurement window in the approved Vendor Scorecard Configuration.

Policy Statement

Penalties are corrective, not a revenue line. Every penalty must trace to a confirmed breach event with evidence, must appear as a coded line on the settlement statement, and must be disputable. Where a breach causes a direct cost — a replacement plant, a reverse pickup, a customer refund — that cost is recovered separately from the penalty and is stated separately. Operational consequences are applied ahead of financial ones wherever reduced routing will fix the problem.

Responsibilities

  • PlantAtHome operations — records and attributes breach events and holds the evidence.
  • PlantAtHome category team — approves operational consequences and agrees corrective action plans.
  • PlantAtHome finance — applies penalties and cost recoveries to the settlement statement with reason codes.
  • Vendor owner — reviews breach lines each cycle, disputes with evidence where warranted and closes corrective actions.

Policy Requirements

The matrix below is the complete list of penalty-bearing breaches. Penalty values are held in configuration and are never stated in this document.

BreachTrigger and evidenceOperational consequencePenalty
Late order acceptanceAcceptance outside {{vendor_acceptance_sla}}, from the platform timestampReduced routing priority on repeat{{penalty_schedule}}
Late dispatchHandover outside {{vendor_dispatch_sla}}, from rider or courier scanRemoval from same-day hyperlocal routing on repeat{{penalty_schedule}}
Incorrect or short shipmentCustomer claim upheld against the packing recordMandatory pre-dispatch check on affected SKUs{{penalty_schedule}}
Poor product qualityAudit or claim result below {{vendor_quality_target}}SKU group delisting until re-inspection passes{{penalty_schedule}}
Damaged or non-compliant packagingDamage claim traced to packing under the Vendor Packaging StandardsPackaging re-audit before routing resumes{{penalty_schedule}}
Inventory mismatch or oversellCycle count variance, or an accepted line the vendor cannot fulfilStock re-verification and reduced routing{{penalty_schedule}}
Repeated cancellationVendor-caused cancellations above the configured rateRouting suspension for the affected city or category{{penalty_schedule}}
Excess returnsVendor-attributable returns above {{vendor_return_rate_threshold}}Corrective action plan, then SKU group restriction{{penalty_schedule}}
Fraud or misrepresentationFalse scans, false acceptance, invoicing for goods not supplied, counterfeit or misdeclared productsImmediate suspension, payout hold, termination and referral to authorities{{penalty_schedule}}, plus full recovery of losses
Policy violation, generalConfirmed breach of any vendor policy not listed above, including direct customer contact on claims and third-party insertsWritten warning, then routing restriction{{penalty_schedule}}

Procedures

  1. Operations records the breach event with its code, the order line and the supporting evidence.
  2. Attribution is confirmed before any consequence is raised; courier, customer, platform and force majeure causes are excluded.
  3. A first occurrence normally results in a written warning and a coded statement line; a repeat within the measurement window escalates to the operational consequence in the matrix.
  4. Persistent breaches across multiple codes trigger a corrective action plan with the category team and a review date.
  5. Penalties and direct cost recoveries are applied in the settlement run under the Vendor Settlement Policy, shown as separate lines.
  6. The vendor may dispute a breach line with evidence within {{vendor_settlement_dispute_window}}; unresolved disputes escalate per {{escalation_timeline}}.
  7. Breach history is reviewed with the vendor at {{review_frequency_default}} and informs contract renewal.

Exceptions

No penalty is applied for events PlantAtHome accepts as outside vendor control, including declared force majeure, courier partner outage, platform incident and city-level restrictions. Onboarding vendors are warned rather than penalised during their initial observation window. Waivers require category head approval, are recorded against the breach event, and are not precedent for later events.

Compliance

Breach records, evidence and dispute outcomes are retained for {{data_retention_period}} and are available to the vendor on the portal. This matrix is read together with the vendor agreement; where the signed agreement states a different commercial consequence, the agreement prevails and this matrix governs process and evidence.

Violations

Attempts to evade this matrix — falsifying evidence, coaching customers to withdraw claims, tampering with scans or splitting accounts to reset breach history — are treated as fraud, attract the fraud row above, and are grounds for immediate termination and recovery of amounts already settled.

title: Employee Handbook
html:
DRAFT — LEGAL REVIEW REQUIRED. This document is an operational or legal draft and must be reviewed and approved by authorized management and, where required, qualified legal counsel before becoming effective.

Purpose

This handbook introduces employment at Silvestrix Green LLP, the entity that operates the PlantAtHome brand. It explains how the business runs, what the company expects of every employee, what employees can expect in return, and — most importantly — where the detailed rule for any given situation actually lives. It is an orientation document and a map to the policy set. It is not a contract of employment and does not create one.

Scope

This handbook applies to all employees of Silvestrix Green LLP, including probationary, full-time, part-time and fixed-term staff across catalogue and merchandising, vendor operations, warehouse and dispatch, delivery coordination, customer support, finance, and engineering. Interns, consultants, contracted riders and nursery vendor staff are not employees; they are governed by their own engagement terms, and by the Code of Conduct whenever they are on company premises or using company systems. Where a signed employment contract or a statutory entitlement conflicts with anything written here, the contract or the statute governs.

Definitions

  • Company / LLP — Silvestrix Green LLP, the GST-registered legal entity employing you.
  • PlantAtHome — the consumer brand under which the Company sells live plants, tools, pots and planters, seeds, fertilizers, accessories, FarmBox fresh produce and corporate gifting.
  • Vendor — an approved nursery or supplier that stocks or fulfils PlantAtHome orders.
  • Company systems — the admin console, order and inventory management, vendor portal, WhatsApp Business API, email and SMS gateways, payment dashboards, code repositories and cloud infrastructure.
  • Configuration — an approved register of operational values (entitlements, limits, timelines) maintained outside policy text so it can change without rewriting policy.

Policy Statement

PlantAtHome sells living stock on short delivery clocks. A wrong plant name in the catalogue, a pot packed without dunnage, or an unanswered customer message costs the Company a plant, a customer and a review at the same time. The Company therefore expects four things of everyone: accuracy in what we publish, care in how we handle living inventory, honesty with customers and vendors, and respect toward colleagues. In return, the Company commits to lawful and non-discriminatory treatment, a safe workplace, timely payment of wages, and statutory benefits under applicable Indian law.

Responsibilities

  • Employees — read this handbook and the policies it points to, acknowledge them, and ask a manager when a situation is not covered rather than improvising.
  • Managers — brief their teams on policy changes, approve leave and expenses within their limits, and escalate conduct issues instead of settling them informally.
  • Human Resources — maintain this handbook and the acknowledgement register, run onboarding and exit, and own the Leave Configuration.
  • Function heads — approve documented exceptions for their teams and confirm that role-specific working arrangements remain lawful.

Policy Requirements

Working arrangements

Roles differ, and so do their arrangements. Warehouse, dispatch and delivery-coordination roles work published shift rosters aligned to hyperlocal cut-offs and courier pickup windows. Vendor operations and quality roles travel to nurseries and log visits in the vendor portal. Support, catalogue, finance and engineering roles work the standard schedule, remote or hybrid where the function head has approved it. Whatever the arrangement, attendance is recorded in the approved system, and coverage during festive and corporate gifting peaks is planned by the function, not negotiated individually.

Communication norms

Customer contact happens only on company channels — the WhatsApp Business API, company email and the SMS gateway — never a personal phone number or personal account, because those conversations are business records and must remain auditable. Internal decisions that affect an order, a vendor or a customer belong in the relevant system (order notes, vendor portal, ticket) and not solely in a chat thread. Only authorised spokespeople speak for PlantAtHome publicly.

Where each detailed rule lives

TopicGoverning document
Professional conduct, conflicts of interest, harassment reporting, fraud, social mediaCode of Conduct
Leave types, entitlements, approval flowLeave Policy
Confidential information, data protection, exit obligationsConfidentiality Policy
Probation, performance review, exit processThis handbook, Procedures below

Procedures

  1. Joining — submit identity, address, bank, tax and qualification documents to HR, receive system access provisioned to your role, and acknowledge this handbook and the linked policies.
  2. Probation — new employees serve {{probation_period}}, closed by a written confirmation or extension decision from the reporting manager.
  3. Performance review — conducted at {{review_frequency_default}} against role objectives agreed with the manager.
  4. Raising a concern — take it to your manager first; where the manager is the subject, or the matter involves harassment, fraud or customer data, go directly to HR under the Code of Conduct.
  5. Exit — serve the notice period stated in your contract, hand over live orders, vendor relationships and credentials, return all assets, and complete the confidentiality acknowledgement before final settlement.

Exceptions

Role-specific variations to working arrangements — split shifts, field rosters, on-call rotations for delivery or engineering — require written approval from the function head and HR, recorded against the role rather than the individual. No exception may reduce a statutory entitlement or waive an obligation under the Confidentiality Policy.

Compliance

HR reviews this handbook at {{review_frequency_default}} and after any material change in law or operating model. Employees acknowledge it at joining and after each material revision; the acknowledgement register is the record of compliance. Not having read the handbook is not a defence to breaching a policy it points to.

Violations

Breaches of the arrangements described here are handled under the Code of Conduct, proportionate to seriousness and to any repetition, and may extend to termination for conduct involving dishonesty, customer data misuse or safety risk. Nothing here limits the Company's rights or an employee's protections under applicable law.

  • Leave Policy
  • Confidentiality Policy

title: Code of Conduct
html:
DRAFT — LEGAL REVIEW REQUIRED. This document is an operational or legal draft and must be reviewed and approved by authorized management and, where required, qualified legal counsel before becoming effective.

Purpose

This Code sets the standard of behaviour expected of everyone working for Silvestrix Green LLP under the PlantAtHome brand. PlantAtHome handles customer addresses and phone numbers, vendor commercial terms, cash on delivery, refund authority and live inventory — every one of which can be abused quietly. This Code states what is unacceptable, how to report it, and what happens next.

Scope

Applies to all employees, and to interns, consultants, contracted riders and vendor staff whenever they are on Company premises, in a partner nursery on Company business, or using Company systems. It applies during working hours and outside them wherever conduct affects the Company, its customers, its vendors or a colleague.

Definitions

  • Conflict of interest — any personal, family or financial interest that could reasonably influence a decision made on the Company's behalf.
  • Company asset — devices, admin and vendor portal credentials, payment dashboards, vehicles, packaging material, inventory and plant samples, brand assets and funds.
  • Confidential information — as defined in the Confidentiality Policy.
  • Internal Committee — the committee constituted under the Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013.

Policy Statement

The Company expects honest, respectful and lawful conduct without exception, and treats integrity failures as more serious than performance failures. A missed target is coachable; a manipulated refund, a concealed vendor interest or a harassed colleague is not. Retaliation against anyone who reports a concern in good faith is itself a serious violation.

Responsibilities

  • Employees — comply with this Code, disclose conflicts as soon as they arise, and report suspected misconduct.
  • Managers — model the standard, refuse to resolve conduct complaints privately, and escalate to HR.
  • HR — receive reports, run investigations, maintain records, and administer outcomes consistently.
  • Internal Committee — handle complaints of sexual harassment under the 2013 Act and its rules.
  • Finance and Vendor Operations — maintain the approval controls that make fraud detectable.

Policy Requirements

Professional and respectful workplace

Treat colleagues, customers, riders and vendor staff with courtesy. Discrimination or exclusion on the basis of sex, gender identity, religion, caste, disability, marital status, region or language is prohibited. Bullying, threats, slurs, sexual advances, and circulating sexual or demeaning content on Company channels are prohibited. Nursery and warehouse sites additionally require compliance with site safety instructions.

Conflicts of interest

Disclose in writing before acting: any ownership or family interest in a nursery, courier, packaging or gifting supplier; any personal relationship with a vendor's decision-maker; any outside work that competes with or supplies PlantAtHome. Employees may not approve vendor onboarding, allocate orders, set margins or release settlements where they hold an undisclosed interest. Gifts, hospitality or cash from vendors or couriers must be declined or declared; the Company does not offer or accept bribes or facilitation payments.

Confidential information and personal data

Customer contact details, addresses, order history, vendor pricing and commission terms, margin configuration, catalogue and market intelligence data, source code and credentials are confidential. Do not export customer lists, forward order data to personal accounts, or contact a customer from a personal number. Full obligations are in the Confidentiality Policy.

Company assets

Use assets for business purposes. Do not share admin credentials, take plants, pots or gifting stock without a recorded sale or approved sample requisition, or use brand assets for personal ventures. Cash collected on delivery is Company money from the moment of collection and must be remitted through the approved process.

Fraud and financial integrity

Prohibited without exception: creating or cancelling orders to inflate performance metrics; issuing refunds or replacements outside the approval authority set by {{approval_limit_refund}}; misusing discount or gifting codes; falsifying delivery proof, quality inspection records or plant-health evidence; inflating expenses beyond {{approval_limit_expense}}; and altering vendor settlement records governed by {{commission_model}}.

Social media and public statements

Only authorised spokespeople speak for PlantAtHome. Never publish customer names, photographs, addresses or order details, vendor terms, or internal screenshots. Personal posts must not present personal views as the Company's. Customer complaints seen on social channels are routed to support, not answered personally.

Procedures

  1. Report — raise a concern with your manager, or directly with HR where the manager is involved or the matter concerns harassment, fraud or customer data. Sexual harassment complaints go to the Internal Committee, which may be approached directly.
  2. Acknowledge — HR acknowledges the report and confirms whether it proceeds as a conduct investigation or under the 2013 Act.
  3. Investigate — a nominated investigator gathers records (system logs, order events, settlement records, messages) and hears both the complainant and the respondent.
  4. Decide — findings, the proposed outcome and the reasoning are documented and approved by HR with the function head.
  5. Close — the complainant is informed of the outcome to the extent permitted, and any control gap the case exposed is fixed.

Confidentiality is maintained throughout, and interim measures such as access suspension or separation of duties may be applied while an investigation runs.

Exceptions

No exceptions to the fraud, harassment, bribery or personal-data provisions. Narrow exceptions elsewhere — for example accepting a nominal vendor gift at a public trade event — require prior written approval from the function head and must be recorded in the conflicts register.

Compliance

HR reviews this Code at {{review_frequency_default}}. All employees acknowledge it at joining and after material revision. Vendor Operations and Finance test the associated controls — refund approvals, settlement changes, credential sharing — as part of routine review.

Violations

CategoryExamplesTypical response
BehaviouralDiscourtesy, unprofessional communication with a customer or vendorAs per the currently approved Disciplinary Action Configuration
SeriousUndisclosed conflict of interest, accepting vendor gifts, credential sharingAs per the currently approved Disciplinary Action Configuration
GrossFraud, theft of stock or COD cash, falsified evidence, harassment, customer data misuseTermination and, where warranted, referral to authorities

Retaliation against a good-faith reporter is treated in the gross category. Nothing in this Code limits any statutory right or remedy available to an employee or complainant.

  • Confidentiality Policy
  • Leave Policy

title: Leave Policy
html:
DRAFT — LEGAL REVIEW REQUIRED. This document is an operational or legal draft and must be reviewed and approved by authorized management and, where required, qualified legal counsel before becoming effective.

Purpose

This policy sets out the leave framework at Silvestrix Green LLP: the types of leave available, how leave is requested and approved, and how absence is covered in a business that dispatches perishable stock every day. Entitlement values are deliberately not written into this document — they are held in the Leave Configuration so they can be updated without reissuing policy.

Scope

Applies to all employees of Silvestrix Green LLP. Entitlements accrue by role category and employment type as defined in the Leave Configuration; probationary employees may have a reduced or deferred entitlement as recorded there. Interns, consultants and contracted riders are covered by their engagement terms, not this policy. Statutory leave under applicable Indian law applies regardless of anything in the Configuration.

Definitions

  • Leave Configuration — the approved register of entitlements, accrual rules, carry-forward, encashment and notice requirements, maintained by HR.
  • Leave year — the twelve-month cycle defined in the Leave Configuration against which accrual and carry-forward are calculated.
  • Planned leave — leave requested and approved before it is taken.
  • Unplanned leave — absence notified on or after the day it begins, permitted only for sickness or emergency.
  • Coverage plan — the named colleague and handover notes that allow a role's live work to continue during an absence.

Policy Statement

The Company expects employees to take their leave. Rest protects judgement, and judgement is what keeps a live-plant order correct. At the same time, hyperlocal dispatch windows, courier pickups and vendor commitments do not pause, so leave is granted against a coverage plan rather than on a first-come basis alone. Leave is applied for and approved in the HR system; a message to a manager is not an approved leave request.

Responsibilities

  • Employees — apply in advance for planned leave, notify sickness or emergency absence at the earliest opportunity, and hand over live orders, vendor follow-ups and open tickets before going on leave.
  • Managers — approve or decline within the request window, maintain a coverage plan for every shift-bound role, and never approve leave verbally outside the system.
  • Function heads — approve extended, unpaid and statutory leave, and resolve clashes during peak periods.
  • HR — maintain the Leave Configuration and holiday calendar, track balances and accruals, and ensure statutory compliance.

Policy Requirements

The following leave types are available. All entitlement, accrual and notice values are those in force in the Leave Configuration at the time of the request.

Leave typeEntitlementNoticeApprover
Earned / privilege leave{{leave_entitlement}}As per the currently approved Leave ConfigurationReporting manager
Casual leave{{leave_entitlement}}As per the currently approved Leave ConfigurationReporting manager
Sick leave{{leave_entitlement}}Earliest opportunity on the dayReporting manager, medical certificate as per the Leave Configuration
Public holidaysPer the approved holiday calendarNot applicableNot applicable
Maternity leavePer the Maternity Benefit Act, 1961As per statute and the Leave ConfigurationHR with function head
Paternity / parental leave{{leave_entitlement}}As per the currently approved Leave ConfigurationFunction head
Bereavement leave{{leave_entitlement}}Earliest opportunityReporting manager
Compensatory off (rostered peak or holiday working)As per the currently approved Leave ConfigurationClaimed within the window in the ConfigurationReporting manager
Leave without payDiscretionary, balances exhausted firstAs per the currently approved Leave ConfigurationFunction head with HR

Carry-forward, lapse and encashment of unused leave, and the treatment of leave on exit, follow the Leave Configuration in force at the end of the leave year or on the last working day respectively. Holidays are declared in the annual holiday calendar published by HR; site-specific holidays may differ for warehouse and dispatch locations.

Procedures

  1. Plan — check the team roster and peak-period constraints before selecting dates.
  2. Apply — raise the request in the HR system with dates, leave type and the coverage plan, giving the notice stated in the Leave Configuration.
  3. Approve — the manager approves or declines in the system with a reason; a declined request must state the operational conflict.
  4. Hand over — before the first day of leave, reassign open orders, vendor escalations, support tickets and on-call duties to the named cover.
  5. Unplanned absence — notify the reporting manager at the earliest opportunity on the first day, then regularise the request in the system on return; supporting documentation for sickness is required as specified in the Leave Configuration.
  6. Extend — a request to extend leave in progress must be raised before the approved leave ends; unnotified absence beyond approved leave is treated as unauthorised.

Exceptions

During declared peak periods — festive demand, corporate gifting cycles and planned catalogue or system migrations — function heads may restrict discretionary leave for shift-bound roles, provided the restriction is published in advance and does not apply to sickness, statutory or emergency leave. Any exception to entitlement or notice for an individual requires written approval from HR and the function head and is recorded against the employee's leave record.

Compliance

HR reviews this policy and the Leave Configuration at {{review_frequency_default}} and after any change in applicable law. Leave balances, approvals and unauthorised absences are recorded in the HR system, and payroll is reconciled against approved leave each cycle.

Violations

Unauthorised absence, absence without handover, falsified medical or emergency documentation, and approving leave outside the system or outside authority are conduct matters handled under the Code of Conduct. Falsified documentation is treated as dishonesty, not as an attendance issue. Continued unauthorised absence beyond the period stated in the Leave Configuration may be treated as abandonment of employment, subject to applicable law.

title: Confidentiality Policy
html:
DRAFT — LEGAL REVIEW REQUIRED. This document is an operational or legal draft and must be reviewed and approved by authorized management and, where required, qualified legal counsel before becoming effective.

Purpose

This policy defines what Silvestrix Green LLP treats as confidential, who may access it, how it must be handled, and what obligations survive the end of employment. PlantAtHome holds customer addresses and phone numbers, vendor commercial terms, margin and pricing configuration, catalogue intelligence and payment records. Most of this can be copied silently, so the controls have to be explicit.

Scope

Applies to all employees, and to interns, consultants, contracted riders and vendor staff granted access to Company systems or information. It covers information in any form — systems, exports, spreadsheets, chat threads, printed picklists and invoices, photographs, and knowledge held in memory — and applies wherever the information is held, including personal devices used for work.

Definitions

  • Confidential information — any non-public information of the Company, its customers, vendors or partners that is obtained through your role.
  • Personal data — information relating to an identifiable individual, including customer names, phone numbers, delivery addresses, geolocation, order history and employee records.
  • Need-to-know — access limited to what a role actually requires to perform a task, and no broader.
  • Data principal request — a request from an individual to access, correct or erase their personal data.
  • Approved system — a Company-provisioned system of record; personal email, personal cloud storage and personal messaging accounts are never approved systems.

Policy Statement

Confidential information is accessed on a need-to-know basis, used only for the purpose it was collected for, and never moved outside approved systems. A customer gives PlantAtHome an address so a plant can be delivered — not so it can sit in a personal spreadsheet. A vendor discloses commercial terms to trade with the Company, not to have them shared with a competing nursery. The Company processes personal data in line with the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 and other applicable Indian law.

Responsibilities

  • Employees — protect information they hold, use only their own credentials, and report suspected loss or exposure immediately.
  • Managers — request access for their team by role, review it periodically, and trigger revocation on transfer or exit.
  • Engineering and IT — provision role-based access, maintain logging, and execute revocation on the day it is requested.
  • HR — obtain confidentiality undertakings at joining and at exit, and hold the acknowledgement records.
  • Finance and Vendor Operations — restrict access to settlement, commission and pricing configuration to named roles.

Policy Requirements

CategoryExamplesAccess
Customer personal dataNames, phone numbers, delivery addresses, geolocation, order and support historySupport, dispatch and delivery coordination, on need-to-know
Vendor commercial informationVendor pricing, settlement records, terms governed by {{commission_model}}Vendor Operations and Finance, named roles only
Pricing and margin configurationCity pricing, margin rules, promotional and gifting ratesCategory, Finance and named engineering roles
Catalogue and market intelligenceSourcing lists, unpublished catalogue, demand analysisCategory and Merchandising
Technical and securitySource code, infrastructure configuration, API keys and gateway credentialsEngineering, on need-to-know
Corporate and employeeFinancials, contracts, employee records and payrollManagement, Finance and HR

Use restrictions

Do not export customer or vendor records except for an approved business purpose recorded with your manager. Do not forward data to personal email or upload it to personal cloud storage. Do not contact a customer from a personal phone number or personal WhatsApp — customer contact belongs on the WhatsApp Business API, Company email or the SMS gateway, where it is retained as a business record. Do not share credentials or work under someone else's login. Do not photograph screens containing customer or vendor data, or post order details, invoices or internal screens publicly. Discussing a customer's order in a shared or public setting is a disclosure like any other.

Data protection

Collect only the personal data a task requires, retain it for {{data_retention_period}}, and use approved deletion routines rather than local copies that outlive them. Personal data may be shared with vendors, couriers and payment or messaging providers only to the extent needed to fulfil an order or a legal obligation, and only under a contract with the recipient. Data principal requests are routed to the designated owner and answered within {{dsr_response_time}}.

Procedures

  1. Grant — the manager requests access by role; Engineering or IT provisions the minimum profile that fits the role.
  2. Review — access is reviewed at {{review_frequency_default}} and on every role change, with unused access removed.
  3. Handle — work inside approved systems; where an export is unavoidable, restrict it to the fields required, store it in the approved location, and delete it when the task closes.
  4. Report an incident — report suspected loss, unauthorised access or accidental disclosure immediately to your manager and Engineering; do not attempt to conceal or quietly correct it.
  5. Exit or transfer — return all devices, documents and printed records, delete Company data from any personal device, transfer files to the designated owner, and sign the exit confidentiality acknowledgement before final settlement. Access is revoked on the last working day, or earlier where the role requires it.

Exceptions

Disclosure outside these rules requires prior written approval from the function head, and from Legal where the recipient is external. No approval is needed — and none may be withheld — for disclosures required by law, by a court or by a lawful request from a public authority; route such requests to management and Legal before responding. Nothing in this policy prevents an employee from making a protected disclosure to a regulator or law enforcement, or from reporting harassment or an offence.

Compliance

This policy is reviewed at {{review_frequency_default}}. Access to customer, vendor and financial data is logged, and access reviews and incident records are retained. Employees acknowledge this policy at joining, on material revision, and at exit.

Violations

Unauthorised access, export or disclosure of confidential information or personal data is treated as gross misconduct under the Code of Conduct and may result in termination, recovery of losses, and civil or criminal proceedings. Confidentiality obligations continue after employment ends for as long as the information remains confidential, subject to applicable law; post-employment obligations are limited to the protection of confidential information and do not restrict an individual's lawful right to work, except as expressly agreed in a signed contract and permitted by law.

Related Documents

  • Employee Handbook
  • Code of Conduct

title: Live Plant Shipping SOP
html:
DRAFT — LEGAL REVIEW REQUIRED. This document is an operational or legal draft and must be reviewed and approved by authorized management and, where required, qualified legal counsel before becoming effective.

Purpose

To define how a live plant order is inspected, protected, packed, dispatched and handed over so the plant arrives alive, true to its listing, and inside the committed delivery window on both the hyperlocal rider lane and the pan-India courier lane.

Scope

Applies to every live plant line item fulfilled by PlantAtHome-operated facilities and by approved nursery vendors, in all serviceable cities and on both delivery lanes. Non-living SKUs (tools, standalone pots and planters, seeds, fertilizers, accessories) are in scope only when they ship in the same consignment as a live plant. FarmBox fresh produce is out of scope and follows its own handling.

Definitions

  • Category care standard — the watering, moisture band, ventilation, temperature-exposure and sealed-transit parameters approved for one plant category in the currently approved Live Plant Care Configuration.
  • Hyperlocal lane — same-city dispatch to a rider partner for direct delivery. Courier lane — dispatch to a pan-India courier partner against an AWB.
  • Root ball — the intact soil mass held by the roots inside the grow pot or wrap.
  • Handover proof — delivery evidence recorded against the order: OTP or signature, plus the delivery photograph where the partner supports it.

Roles and Responsibilities

  • Packer (vendor or facility) — performs inspection and packing; records the checklist and photographs.
  • Quality inspector — signs the plant off as dispatch-fit and owns rejects.
  • Fulfilment coordinator — assigns the lane, books the rider or courier, watches the dispatch window.
  • Category manager — owns and revises category care standards; approves seasonal and route holds.
  • Support agent — owns all customer communication on delays, failed delivery and plant condition claims.

Prerequisites

  • Vendor KYC active and the line accepted within {{vendor_acceptance_sla}}.
  • The category care standard for the SKU printed on the pick list.
  • Approved packaging kit: telescopic carton or crate, pot cradle or straps, root-ball sleeve, cushioning, ventilation die-cuts, orientation and fragile labels.
  • Working soil moisture meter, clean secateurs, quarantine bench, label printer bound to the order, and a GST-compliant invoice issued per {{gst_invoice_timeline}}.

Trigger

A live plant line is allocated to a fulfilment location and accepted by the vendor, or a replacement shipment is authorised under the Reverse Logistics SOP.

Step-by-Step Procedure

Plant care parameters are not universal. Watering volume, acceptable soil moisture band, ventilation, permissible temperature exposure and maximum time in a closed carton differ by category — succulents and cacti, tropical foliage, flowering plants, herbs, bonsai, aquatics and outdoor saplings all behave differently. Read the category care standard on the pick list for that SKU and apply it. Never apply a default, a habit carried from another category, or a figure remembered from another order.

  1. Pre-dispatch quality inspection. Match SKU, size grade, pot size and quantity to the order. Reject wilting, leaf loss, breakage, sunscald, chlorosis, or any plant not true to the listing. Rejects go to the quarantine bench and the line is re-allocated — never silently substituted.
  2. Watering assessment. Water only as the category care standard directs for the assigned lane and expected transit duration, and record what was done. Watering to a default before a long sealed transit causes rot; skipping it causes desiccation.
  3. Soil moisture check. Meter the root ball and confirm the reading sits inside the band the category standard defines. Outside the band, correct and re-meter before packing.
  4. Pest inspection. Inspect leaf undersides, axils, stem joints and the top soil layer for mealybug, scale, mites, aphids, fungus gnats and larvae. Any live infestation stops dispatch and quarantines the plant.
  5. Disease inspection. Check for fungal or bacterial spotting, mildew, stem and root rot, and viral mottling. Diseased plants are never packed and never trimmed to hide symptoms; the finding is logged against the vendor's quality record.
  6. Structural protection. Stake the main stem or cane, sleeve tall foliage against whip damage, and tie branches loosely enough not to bruise. Flowering heads get a collar, not direct wrap.
  7. Pot protection. Immobilise the pot to the carton base with a cradle or cross straps so the plant cannot swing. Ceramic and terracotta take an extra cushioned layer and a rim-crush-resistant carton.
  8. Soil protection. Cap the soil surface with a secured sleeve, mesh or wrap so the root ball stays intact and soil does not spill onto foliage.
  9. Ventilation. Cut ventilation apertures in the number and position the category standard specifies for that lane. Fully sealed cartons are permitted only where that standard allows them for the category and transit duration.
  10. Packaging. Close the carton without compressing foliage; secure co-ordered non-living items so they cannot shift onto the plant; include the category care card.
  11. Labelling. Apply the order label, the live plant and orientation markings on the required faces, and the invoice pouch. Scan-verify the label against the order before sealing.
  12. Dispatch timing. Hand over inside {{vendor_dispatch_sla}} and inside the daily cut-off for the assigned lane. A pack that misses the cut-off is opened, rested per the category standard and re-prepared — never held sealed overnight.
  13. Transit considerations. Apply the protection profile below for the lane and prevailing conditions.
  14. Delivery handover. The partner records handover proof against the order. On the hyperlocal lane the rider offers an open-box check where the customer is present. Condition photographs at handover support any claim raised within {{live_plant_claim_window}}.
  15. Failed delivery. If the attempt fails, stop here and follow the Failed Delivery SOP — a live consignment is triaged, never parked.
ConditionHyperlocal laneCourier lane
Normal conditionsCategory care standard plus base packaging kitCategory care standard, base kit and double-wall carton

SLA

Vendor acceptance {{vendor_acceptance_sla}}; dispatch {{vendor_dispatch_sla}}; delivery {{delivery_sla_hyperlocal}} on the hyperlocal lane and {{delivery_sla_courier}} on the courier lane; condition claims accepted within {{live_plant_claim_window}}; support first response {{support_response_sla}}.

Quality Checks

  • Two photographs per consignment — plant before packing and the sealed labelled carton — attached to the order.
  • Completed inspection checklist with the moisture reading and the category standard applied.
  • Sampled re-inspection of sealed packs by the quality inspector, with vendor performance measured against {{vendor_quality_target}}.
  • Claim reasons reviewed against packing evidence at {{review_frequency_default}} to feed back into the care standards.

Exceptions

  • Seasonal or weather holds on a category or route, approved by the Category Manager, override the dispatch window.
  • Oversized, heavy or specimen plants ship only on lanes cleared for them.
  • Where state agriculture or plant quarantine restrictions apply to an inter-state movement, the Category Manager clears the route before dispatch or the line is cancelled and refunded.
  • Corporate gifting consignments may carry bespoke presentation packing, provided ventilation and root-ball protection are not reduced.

Escalation Process

Packer to quality inspector for a fitness call; inspector to fulfilment coordinator for lane or cut-off risk; coordinator to Category Manager for care, route or seasonal decisions; unresolved or repeat issues to the Operations Head. Each step advances per {{escalation_timeline}}.

Records and Audit Trail

The inspection checklist, moisture reading, packing photographs, label and invoice, partner booking reference and handover proof are all stored against the order and its event timeline, with reject and quarantine entries against the vendor's quality record. Records are retained for {{data_retention_period}}.
