title: Failed Delivery SOP
html:
DRAFT — LEGAL REVIEW REQUIRED. This document is an operational or legal draft and must be reviewed and approved by authorized management and, where required, qualified legal counsel before becoming effective.

Purpose

To define what happens when a delivery attempt fails, so that every consignment is re-attempted, redirected or returned on a recorded decision, the customer is contacted before the next attempt, and live plants coming back are triaged before they die in a carton.

Scope

All failed delivery attempts on both the hyperlocal rider lane and the pan-India courier lane, across every vertical. Covers customer unavailable, phone unreachable, address incorrect or incomplete, entry or society restriction, refusal at the door, refusal to pay on a cash order, and partner or weather exceptions.

Definitions

  • Failed attempt — a delivery attempt closed by the partner without handover proof.
  • NDR — the non-delivery report the partner sends with its reason code.
  • Reattempt — a further delivery attempt on the same consignment, counted against {{delivery_attempts}}.
  • RTO — return to origin: the consignment is sent back to the fulfilment location or vendor.
  • Survival triage — inspection and revival assessment of a returned live plant against its category care standard.

Roles and Responsibilities

  • Fulfilment coordinator — validates the NDR, books reattempts, makes the reattempt-versus-RTO call.
  • Support agent — runs the customer contact ladder and records the outcome.
  • Delivery partner — supplies an accurate reason code and attempt evidence.
  • Nursery recovery desk — receives and triages returned live plants.
  • Operations lead — approves exceptions, waivers and RTO ahead of exhausted attempts.

Prerequisites

  • Partner NDR feed mapped onto the order event timeline, with reason codes normalised.
  • A verified customer contact number and approved WhatsApp templates on {{support_channels}}.
  • Serviceability data current enough to test any corrected address.
  • Recovery bench and grading area available at the receiving facility.

Trigger

A partner marks an attempt failed, an NDR is received, or a rider reports non-delivery on a hyperlocal task.

Step-by-Step Procedure

  1. Validate the failure. Read the partner reason code against the attempt evidence — timestamp, location stamp, call record. A vague or unevidenced reason is challenged with the partner before any customer contact.
  2. Record the attempt. Log the attempt on the order timeline. Attempts are counted and capped per {{delivery_attempts}}.
  3. Run the contact ladder in the order set out below, stopping as soon as the customer confirms a slot or a decision.
  4. Confirm or correct the address. Minor corrections within the same serviceable area are accepted and passed to the partner. An address outside the original lane's coverage cannot be reattempted — cancel and re-place, or move to RTO.
  5. Decide reattempt or RTO. Reattempt when the customer is reachable, the address is confirmed, attempts remain, and — for a live plant — the consignment can still be delivered inside the transit exposure its category care standard permits. Move to RTO when attempts are exhausted, the customer refuses or is unreachable at the end of the ladder, the address is unserviceable, or the plant would exceed its permitted transit exposure. Record the reason.
  6. Schedule the reattempt. Book the agreed slot with the partner and confirm it to the customer on the channel that reached them.
  7. Initiate RTO. Raise the return leg with the partner and hand the case to the Reverse Logistics SOP. Refund treatment, including any shipping recovery, follows the Delivery and Shipping Policy and the approved cancellation and refund rules — never quoted ad hoc to the customer.
  8. Plant survival triage on return. A returned live consignment is opened on arrival, never shelved sealed. Check soil moisture against the category band, water or dry as that standard directs, inspect for pest, rot, breakage and heat or cold damage, and photograph the plant. Assign a condition grade and route it to restock, the recovery bench or write-off under the Reverse Logistics SOP. Plants with live pest are quarantined, never returned to sellable stock.
  9. Close the loop. Notify the customer of the final outcome, update the order status, and if the failure was caused by packing, labelling or partner handling, raise it against the responsible party.
StepActionChannelTiming
1Automated failure notice with reschedule linkWhatsApp, then SMS fallbackOn NDR receipt
2Agent call to confirm slot and addressVoice on {{support_channels}}Within {{support_response_sla}}
3Second call plus written summary of optionsVoice and emailBefore the next attempt is booked
4Final notice stating that RTO will followWhatsApp and emailOnce {{delivery_attempts}} is reached

SLA

Customer contact begins within {{support_response_sla}} of the NDR; the reattempt-versus-RTO decision is made and recorded before the partner's next attempt window; total attempts are capped at {{delivery_attempts}}; case resolution targets {{support_resolution_sla}}; any refund arising is approved within {{refund_approval_sla}} and processed within {{refund_processing_time}}.

Quality Checks

  • Attempt evidence is sampled for false attempts — no call record, no location stamp, or an attempt outside the delivery window.
  • Every RTO carries a recorded reason and the contact ladder steps that preceded it.
  • Live plant returns carry triage photographs and a condition grade before disposition.
  • Repeat partner-caused failures are measured against {{penalty_schedule}} at {{review_frequency_default}}.

Exceptions

  • Perishable hyperlocal consignments may go to RTO before attempts are exhausted where the category care standard makes further transit unsafe.
  • Weather, civic disruption or partner network events pause the attempt counter with the Operations Lead's approval.
  • Restricted premises and gated societies may be delivered to an agreed collection point only with the customer's recorded consent.
  • Corporate gifting consignments follow the recipient list holder's instruction, not the recipient's, for redirection.

Escalation Process

Support agent to fulfilment coordinator when the ladder ends without contact; coordinator to Operations Lead for early RTO, waiver or partner dispute; Operations Lead to the Category Manager where plant survival is at stake, and to Finance where a refund exceeds {{approval_limit_refund}}. Stages advance per {{escalation_timeline}}.

Records and Audit Trail

NDR payloads, attempt timestamps and evidence, call and messaging logs, the recorded decision and its reason, triage photographs and grades, and the final order status are all retained against the order for {{data_retention_period}}.

Related Documents

  • Live Plant Shipping SOP
  • Reverse Logistics SOP
  • Customer Support Escalation SOP
  • Delivery and Shipping Policy
  • Returns, Refunds and Cancellations Policy

title: Reverse Logistics SOP
html:
DRAFT — LEGAL REVIEW REQUIRED. This document is an operational or legal draft and must be reviewed and approved by authorized management and, where required, qualified legal counsel before becoming effective.

Purpose

To govern the return leg end to end: booking the reverse pickup, receiving and grading what comes back, triggering the correct refund or replacement, attributing cost to the vendor where the fault is theirs, and disposing of the returned unit so that nothing unfit re-enters sellable stock.

Scope

Customer-initiated returns raised within {{return_request_window}}, live plant condition claims raised within {{live_plant_claim_window}}, replacement swaps, RTO consignments handed over from the Failed Delivery SOP, and vendor recalls. Categories listed as non-returnable in the Returns, Refunds and Cancellations Policy are out of scope except where the item is damaged, wrong or not as described.

Definitions

  • Reverse pickup — a partner task collecting from the customer address and dropping at the fulfilment location or vendor. The legs are inverted relative to a forward booking.
  • Condition grade — the graded outcome of inbound inspection, which drives both the refund decision and the disposition.
  • Disposition — where the received unit finally goes: sellable stock, recovery bench, write-off or disposal.
  • Vendor debit — a recovery raised against a vendor's settlement where fault is attributed to them.

Roles and Responsibilities

  • Support agent — validates eligibility and approves or declines the return against policy.
  • Reverse logistics coordinator — books the pickup, tracks the return leg, chases stalled pickups.
  • Grading inspector — inspects, photographs and grades every inbound unit.
  • Vendor manager — attributes fault and raises vendor debits.
  • Finance — releases refunds and applies debits in the settlement run.

Prerequisites

  • A return request recorded with a reason code, and customer evidence attached within {{replacement_evidence_window}} where the claim is damage, wrong item or plant condition.
  • Pickup pin code serviceable on a lane with reverse capability.
  • Grading bench, camera, moisture meter and a quarantine area separated from sellable stock.
  • The category care standard available for any live plant being received.

Trigger

A return or replacement is approved, an RTO is initiated under the Failed Delivery SOP, or a vendor recall is issued.

Step-by-Step Procedure

  1. Validate eligibility. Check the request against the window, the category's returnability and the evidence attached. Decline with a written reason where it fails; do not book a pickup for an ineligible request.
  2. Instruct the customer. Ask for the item in its original packing where available, with the pot upright and the soil surface covered for a live plant, and accessories included. Photographs before handover reduce grading disputes.
  3. Book the pickup. Select the lane, confirm the pickup address is the customer and the drop is the receiving facility or vendor, and record the partner reference on the order. Pickup attempts follow {{delivery_attempts}}; the contact ladder in the Failed Delivery SOP applies to failed pickups.
  4. Track the return leg until scanned in. A pickup with no movement is chased with the partner and, if it stays stalled, cancelled and rebooked rather than left open.
  5. Receive and quarantine. Open and inspect on arrival. Nothing goes to sellable stock directly from a return. Live plants are opened first, watered or dried per their category care standard, and checked for pest, rot and mechanical damage.
  6. Grade the unit using the matrix below, with photographs attached to the return record.
  7. Trigger refund or replacement. The grade and reason code decide the outcome under the Returns, Refunds and Cancellations Policy. Refunds are approved within {{refund_approval_sla}} and processed within {{refund_processing_time}} to the original payment method; anything above {{approval_limit_refund}} needs the next approval level. A replacement is dispatched under the Live Plant Shipping SOP as a fresh consignment.
  8. Attribute fault and raise the vendor debit. Where grading shows a packing, quality, wrong-item or condition failure at source, raise the debit against the vendor per {{commission_model}} and {{penalty_schedule}}, applied in the {{vendor_settlement_cycle}} run. The vendor may dispute within {{vendor_settlement_dispute_window}} with evidence. Vendors breaching {{vendor_return_rate_threshold}} enter review under the Vendor Fulfilment Agreement.
  9. Set the disposition per the matrix and move the stock physically to match the record. Pest-infested or diseased plants are never restocked.
  10. Close the loop. Notify the customer of the grade-driven outcome, close the return, and feed recurring reason codes into the packing and care standards at {{review_frequency_default}}.
GradeCondition on receiptDispositionFinancial trigger
AUnused, healthy, saleable as listedReturn to sellable stock after quarantine clearanceRefund or replacement per the Returns, Refunds and Cancellations Policy
BStressed or cosmetically damaged but recoverableRecovery bench, relisted only when regraded ARefund per policy; vendor debit per {{penalty_schedule}} where source fault
CDead, rotted, broken or pest-infestedQuarantine then disposal; written offRefund per policy; full vendor debit where source fault
DWrong item, incomplete, or not as listedReturn to vendor or correct the listingVendor debit and correction under the Vendor Fulfilment Agreement
ECustomer misuse or damage after deliveryHold pending decisionRefund declined or partial, with written reason to the customer

SLA

Eligibility decision within {{support_response_sla}} of the request; pickup booked immediately on approval; grading completed on the day of receipt for live plants; refund approval within {{refund_approval_sla}} and processing within {{refund_processing_time}}; vendor debits applied in the {{vendor_settlement_cycle}} run; end-to-end case closure targets {{support_resolution_sla}}.

Quality Checks

  • Every graded unit carries inbound photographs and a named inspector.
  • Grade against reason code is sampled for drift, particularly grade E declines.
  • Physical stock in quarantine, recovery and write-off is reconciled to the system record.
  • Vendor debit accuracy is reviewed before each settlement run.

Exceptions

  • Where pickup cost would exceed the recoverable value, the item may be written off in place with the customer keeping it, on Operations Lead approval.
  • Non-serviceable pickup pins are handled by customer self-dispatch with reimbursement per the approved shipping rules.
  • Live plants presenting a pest risk are quarantined on arrival and may be disposed of before grading is complete, with photographs standing as the record.
  • Corporate gifting bulk returns are consolidated into a single pickup and graded per unit.

Escalation Process

Grading inspector to reverse logistics coordinator on a disputed grade; coordinator to Vendor Manager for fault attribution; Vendor Manager to Finance for debits and to the Operations Head for a disputed settlement; refunds above {{approval_limit_refund}} and write-offs above {{approval_limit_expense}} escalate to the approver named in the delegation of authority. Stages advance per {{escalation_timeline}}.

Records and Audit Trail

The return request and reason code, customer evidence, pickup booking and attempt history, inbound photographs, grade and inspector, refund or replacement decision with approver, vendor debit and any dispute, and the final disposition entry are all retained against the order and the vendor record for {{data_retention_period}}.

Related Documents

  • Failed Delivery SOP
  • Live Plant Shipping SOP
  • Returns, Refunds and Cancellations Policy
  • Vendor Fulfilment Agreement
  • Customer Support Escalation SOP

title: Information Security Policy
html:
DRAFT — LEGAL REVIEW REQUIRED. This document is an operational or legal draft and must be reviewed and approved by authorized management and, where required, qualified legal counsel before becoming effective.

Purpose

PlantAtHome holds customer names, delivery addresses and phone numbers, order and payment references, vendor bank and KYC records, and employee personal data across its admin panel, storefront, vendor portal and connected integrations. This policy sets the minimum security controls every person with access to those systems must follow, so that customer and vendor data stays confidential, order and payout data stays accurate, and Silvestrix Green LLP can meet its obligations under Indian data protection and information technology law.

Scope

This policy applies to all employees, interns, apprentices, consultants and contract staff of Silvestrix Green LLP, and to anyone else issued a PlantAtHome login. It covers the admin panel and its role-based accounts, the storefront and mobile app back office, the vendor portal, the Razorpay dashboard, courier and rider partner consoles, the WhatsApp Business API account and email and SMS senders, cloud infrastructure, databases, media storage and code repositories, and every company-owned or personal device used to reach any of them. Nursery vendors and delivery partners are bound by the security clauses of their own agreements rather than by this policy.

Definitions

  • PlantAtHome Systems — any application, console, database, repository or integration account operated by or on behalf of the company.
  • Personal Data — any data that identifies a customer, vendor contact, rider or employee, including contact details, addresses, location pins and order history.
  • Privileged Access — the ability to change roles or permissions, reach production servers or databases, or handle payment, courier or messaging credentials.
  • Security Incident — any suspected or confirmed loss, exposure, unauthorised use or unavailability of PlantAtHome Systems or Personal Data, including phishing, lost devices and shared credentials.
  • Security Owner — the person nominated by management to maintain access registers, the security configuration and the incident log.

Policy Statement

Access to PlantAtHome Systems is granted on the principle of least privilege: the narrowest set of rights needed for a defined job, for as long as that job lasts, and no longer. Accounts are personal and never shared. Customer and vendor data is used only to fulfil orders, provide support and meet legal obligations, and is never copied to personal accounts, personal storage or unapproved tools. Every person covered by this policy has a standing duty to report anything that looks like a Security Incident, without waiting for certainty and without fear of blame for an honest report.

Responsibilities

  • Designated Partners — approve this policy, own residual risk, and jointly approve privileged access.
  • Security Owner — maintains the access register and security configuration, runs access reviews, triages incidents and reports outcomes to management.
  • Function heads — request, justify and promptly withdraw access for their teams; approve elevated rights within their function.
  • Engineering — enforces role-based permissions in the admin panel, keeps credentials out of source code, and applies security updates to hosted services.
  • All personnel — protect their credentials and devices, use only approved tools for company data, and report incidents immediately.

Policy Requirements

Access control and least privilege

Access tierTypical rightsApproval requiredAccess review
StandardOrder lookup, customer support replies, catalogue and content entryReporting manager{{review_frequency_default}}
ElevatedRefunds and cancellations, price and margin changes, vendor payout release, bulk export of customer dataFunction head; refund actions additionally bound by {{approval_limit_refund}}{{review_frequency_default}}
PrivilegedRole and permission assignment, server and database access, payment, courier and messaging credentials, production deploymentDesignated Partner and Security Owner jointly{{risk_review_frequency}}
Third-partyScoped vendor portal or agency accessFunction head, with written scope and an end date recorded in the access register{{risk_review_frequency}}

Authentication and passwords

  • Passwords must meet or exceed {{password_min_length}} and satisfy the currently approved Password Configuration.
  • Multi-factor authentication is mandatory wherever the system supports it, and always for privileged and payment-related accounts.
  • Company passwords are never reused on personal services, never shared over chat or email, and are stored only in the approved password manager.
  • Credentials are changed immediately on any suspicion of compromise and on the departure of anyone who knew a shared service password.

Device and data handling

  • Devices used for company work must have disk encryption, a screen lock, current operating system updates and active anti-malware where applicable.
  • Customer and vendor data may be exported only for a stated business reason, and never into personal email, personal drives, or AI or automation tools that are not on the approved list.
  • Card details are never collected, stored or requested by staff; card data remains with the payment gateway.
  • Backups run at {{backup_frequency}}, are retained for {{backup_retention}}, and are restore-tested at {{restore_test_frequency}}. Personal data is retained no longer than {{data_retention_period}}.

Procedures

  1. Joining — the function head raises an access request naming the role and tier; the Security Owner provisions it and records it in the access register.
  2. Change of role — old rights are removed before new rights are granted; transfers are not additive.
  3. Exit — all accounts, devices and credentials are revoked and collected as part of the exit checklist, before final settlement is released.
  4. Incident reporting — report to the Security Owner immediately on becoming aware, preserve evidence, do not attempt independent remediation on production systems, and make no disclosure to customers, vendors or media. Incidents are classified under {{incident_severity_model}}; those involving personal data are handled under the Data Protection and Privacy Policy, and related data subject requests are answered within {{dsr_response_time}}.
  5. Access review — the Security Owner circulates each function's access list on the cadence in the table above; unconfirmed accounts are disabled.

Exceptions

Any deviation requires a written exception approved by a Designated Partner and the Security Owner, recorded in the exception register with a business justification, a compensating control and an expiry date. Exceptions lapse automatically on expiry and are re-reviewed at {{review_frequency_default}}. No exception may be granted for sharing accounts, disabling multi-factor authentication on payment or privileged accounts, or storing customer data in personal accounts.

Compliance

This policy supports the company's obligations under the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 and the Information Technology Act, 2000 together with the rules made under it. The Security Owner reports access review results, open exceptions and incident trends to management at {{review_frequency_default}}, and the policy itself is reviewed at {{review_frequency_default}} or sooner after a significant incident or system change.

Violations

Breach of this policy may result in withdrawal of access and disciplinary action up to and including termination, and recovery of losses attributable to the breach. Deliberate misuse of customer or vendor data, unauthorised access, or concealment of an incident may additionally be referred for action under applicable law and, in the case of contractors and agencies, lead to termination of engagement.

Related Documents

  • Remote Work Policy
  • Asset Policy
  • Data Protection and Privacy Policy
  • Employee Onboarding and Offboarding SOP
  • Incident Response Plan

title: Remote Work Policy
html:
DRAFT — LEGAL REVIEW REQUIRED. This document is an operational or legal draft and must be reviewed and approved by authorized management and, where required, qualified legal counsel before becoming effective.

Purpose

PlantAtHome runs a mix of work that must happen on site — receiving and staging live plants, catalogue photography, hub dispatch, rider and vendor coordination — and work that can be done from anywhere, such as engineering, content, marketing and much of customer support. This policy sets out who may work remotely, how it is approved, and the standards of availability, security and performance that apply when they do, so that remote work never becomes invisible to the team or risky for customer data.

Scope

This policy applies to all employees, interns and contract staff of Silvestrix Green LLP whose role is capable of being performed away from a company site, and to occasional remote days taken by otherwise site-based staff. It covers work from home, from another city, and from any temporary location. It does not apply to nursery vendors, delivery partners or agencies, whose working arrangements are governed by their own agreements, and it does not change any term of employment other than the location and manner of work.

Definitions

  • Remote work — performing the role from a location other than a company office, hub, warehouse or studio.
  • Hybrid — an approved split between remote days and on-site days, recorded in the team's roster.
  • Core hours — the overlapping hours during which a remote employee must be reachable, as set in the currently approved Remote Work Configuration.
  • Approved workspace — a private, reliably connected location where company screens and calls cannot be seen or overheard by others.

Policy Statement

Remote work at PlantAtHome is a business arrangement, not an entitlement or a benefit attached to a grade. It is approved where the role can be delivered to the same standard remotely, where the person has demonstrated they can work without close supervision, and where customer and vendor commitments are unaffected. Approval is always conditional and may be varied or withdrawn when business needs, performance or security require it.

Responsibilities

  • Function heads — decide eligibility for their roles, maintain the roster, and confirm that remote arrangements still work at each review.
  • Reporting managers — set written objectives, hold regular check-ins, and raise availability or output concerns early rather than at appraisal time.
  • Remote employees — maintain an approved workspace, stay reachable during core hours, protect company data and equipment, and keep their calendar and status accurate.
  • Security Owner — confirms device and network requirements before remote access to elevated or payout-related functions is enabled.
  • People and Operations — records approvals, tracks equipment issued, and reviews this policy at {{review_frequency_default}}.

Policy Requirements

Role groupRemote eligibilityApproverConditions
Engineering, design, content, marketingFull or hybrid remoteFunction headAvailability during core hours per the currently approved Remote Work Configuration
Customer supportHybrid or shift-based remoteFunction head with Support LeadMust sustain {{support_response_sla}} and {{support_resolution_sla}} on all {{support_channels}}
Finance, vendor payouts, catalogue pricingHybrid onlyFinance Lead with Security OwnerPayout release and refunds only from a company device on an approved network, within {{approval_limit_refund}}
City operations, hub, dispatch, rider coordinationNot eligible — site-dependent—Occasional exception only, per the Exceptions section
Catalogue photography and plant careNot eligible — asset-dependent—Editing and post-production may be done remotely
  • Eligibility — regular remote or hybrid arrangements are normally considered only after successful completion of {{probation_period}}, and only where the last performance discussion recorded no delivery or reliability concern.
  • Working hours and availability — contracted hours are unchanged. Remote employees must be reachable on the approved messaging and calling tools during core hours, respond within the response norms set for their function, and mark planned absence in the shared calendar in advance.
  • Security — the Information Security Policy applies in full. Work is done on the assigned company device from an approved workspace, over a private network rather than open public Wi-Fi, with screens locked when unattended and calls involving customer or vendor data taken where they cannot be overheard.
  • Data handling — customer addresses, phone numbers, order exports and vendor KYC documents are not printed at home, not saved to personal devices or storage, and not shared in personal chat groups.
  • Equipment — company devices are issued and returned under the Asset Policy. Home internet, electricity and workspace costs are borne by the employee unless a specific allowance is set in the approved configuration; reimbursable items follow the Expense Policy.
  • Location — the approved city or state of work is recorded, and any change is notified in advance so that tax, payroll and coverage implications can be assessed. Working from outside India requires prior written approval.
  • Performance and communication — output is measured against written objectives, not hours online. Remote employees attend the agreed team rituals, keep work visible in the company's tracking tools, and are expected to travel to a company site for planned reviews, launches, peak-season operations and team sessions when asked, with reasonable notice.

Procedures

  1. The employee submits a request naming the arrangement sought, the proposed workspace and the working location.
  2. The reporting manager assesses role suitability and delivery history and recommends or declines.
  3. The function head approves, and the Security Owner confirms device and access requirements for elevated functions.
  4. People and Operations records the approval, the roster entry and any equipment issued.
  5. The arrangement is reviewed at {{review_frequency_default}}, and immediately if performance, availability or a security concern arises.
  6. Withdrawal or variation is communicated in writing with reasons and reasonable notice, except where a security or conduct issue requires immediate change.

Exceptions

One-off remote days for site-dependent roles may be approved by the function head where cover is arranged and dispatch or customer commitments are unaffected. Temporary remote work on medical, caregiving or compassionate grounds may be approved outside the eligibility rules, with the approval and its intended duration recorded in writing. Any exception that reduces a security control requires the exception process in the Information Security Policy.

Compliance

Managers confirm at {{review_frequency_default}} that each remote arrangement in their team is current, recorded and still appropriate. People and Operations maintains the register of approvals and locations, and reports coverage gaps to management. Nothing in this policy alters statutory entitlements, including leave under {{leave_entitlement}}.

Violations

Working remotely without approval, being persistently unreachable during core hours, misrepresenting working location or hours, or handling company data outside the required controls may lead to withdrawal of the arrangement and disciplinary action up to and including termination. Security breaches are additionally dealt with under the Information Security Policy.

Related Documents

  • Information Security Policy
  • Asset Policy
  • Expense Policy
  • Employee Code of Conduct

title: Expense Policy
html:
DRAFT — LEGAL REVIEW REQUIRED. This document is an operational or legal draft and must be reviewed and approved by authorized management and, where required, qualified legal counsel before becoming effective.

Purpose

PlantAtHome staff routinely spend money on the company's behalf — travelling to nurseries and vendor sites, buying packaging or consumables during a stockout, running paid campaigns, and subscribing to tools. This policy defines what the company will pay for, who must approve it, what proof is required, and how reimbursement is made, so that legitimate costs are settled promptly and every rupee spent is supported by a document that stands up to audit and to GST scrutiny.

Scope

This policy applies to all employees, interns and contract staff of Silvestrix Green LLP who incur business expenses, whether paid from personal funds, a company card, a petty cash float or a company account. It covers travel, field operations, vendor and nursery visits, tools and subscriptions, marketing spend, corporate gifting hospitality, and small operational purchases. It does not cover vendor payouts, courier and rider charges billed under partner agreements, or payroll items such as salary and statutory benefits.

Definitions

  • Business expense — a cost necessarily incurred to perform company work, that would not have been incurred otherwise.
  • Approver — the person authorised to sanction the expense under the Delegation of Authority Policy and {{approval_limit_expense}}.
  • Supporting document — an original tax invoice or receipt naming the supplier, date, amount and description; where GST input credit is available, an invoice bearing the company's registered name and GSTIN.
  • Expense Configuration — the approved schedule of per-category caps, submission windows, allowances and reimbursement cycles maintained by Finance.

Policy Statement

The company reimburses reasonable, necessary and properly evidenced business expenses. Approval is obtained before the money is spent wherever the spend is foreseeable; after-the-fact approval is reserved for genuine operational emergencies. No one approves their own expense, and no one approves an expense from which they personally benefit. Where an expense lacks a valid supporting document, or falls outside the approved configuration, it is not reimbursed.

Responsibilities

  • Claimant — obtains prior approval, collects a compliant invoice at the point of purchase, and submits the claim within the window in the Expense Configuration.
  • Approver — checks the business need, the amount against {{approval_limit_expense}}, and the completeness of evidence before approving.
  • Finance — verifies claims, maintains the Expense Configuration, books GST input credit where eligible, and releases reimbursement on the approved cycle.
  • Function heads — own their budget, review recurring spend such as subscriptions, and cancel what is no longer used.
  • Designated Partners — approve spend above the delegated limit and any new expense category.

Policy Requirements

CategoryTypical itemsEvidence requiredApproval
Intercity travelRail, bus or air travel and stay for vendor, nursery or partner visitsTicket and tax invoice; stay invoice in company namePrior approval by function head; above {{approval_limit_expense}} escalate to a Designated Partner
Local and field travelCab or auto fare for hub, vendor, courier or customer escalation visitsApp invoice or receipt with route and dateReporting manager, within the Expense Configuration cap
Operational purchasesPackaging, twine, soil, saucers or consumables bought locally to clear a dispatchTax invoice with GSTIN where available; photograph of goods receivedCity Operations Lead; must be logged against the order or hub
Software and subscriptionsTools, plugins, design and analytics servicesGST invoice in the company name; renewal terms notedFunction head, with Security Owner sign-off before any tool touches customer data
Marketing and gifting hospitalityCampaign spend, sampling, corporate client meetingsInvoice plus campaign or client referenceMarketing Lead; above {{approval_limit_expense}} escalate to a Designated Partner
  • Spend must be booked to the correct cost centre, city and, where relevant, the order or campaign it relates to.
  • Claims are submitted with legible supporting documents within the submission window set in the Expense Configuration; late claims require written justification and Finance acceptance.
  • Where a supplier is GST registered, an invoice bearing the company's registered name and GSTIN must be obtained at the time of purchase; a personal-name invoice forfeits input credit and may be rejected or reimbursed net of the credit lost.
  • Advances against travel or field operations are settled against actuals before a further advance is issued.
  • Reimbursement is released on the cycle stated in the Expense Configuration, through payroll or bank transfer to the employee's recorded account only.

Non-reimbursable

  • Personal purchases, family or guest costs on a business trip, and personal entertainment.
  • Traffic fines, parking penalties, late fees and interest arising from personal delay.
  • Alcohol, tobacco, and any payment to a government official or intermediary to secure or expedite an approval.
  • Home internet, electricity, furniture and routine commuting, unless a specific allowance is set in the approved configuration.
  • Plants, pots or company merchandise for personal use; staff purchases go through the employee purchase route at the approved rate.
  • Any expense already recovered from a vendor, customer or insurer.

Procedures

  1. Seek written approval before committing spend, stating purpose, category and estimated amount.
  2. Purchase from a GST-registered supplier where one is reasonably available, and collect a compliant invoice at the point of sale.
  3. Submit the claim with itemised lines, category, cost centre and attached documents within the approved submission window.
  4. The approver reviews business need and limit and approves or returns the claim with reasons.
  5. Finance verifies documents, queries anomalies, books eligible input credit and schedules payment on the approved cycle.
  6. Disputed or partially rejected lines are explained in writing to the claimant, who may escalate once to the Finance Lead.

Exceptions

Emergency spend to protect perishable stock, complete a customer delivery or restore a critical system may be incurred without prior approval, provided the approver is informed the same working day and the claim records the emergency. Any expense outside the approved categories, or above the delegated limit, requires written approval from a Designated Partner before payment.

Compliance

Finance samples approved claims at {{review_frequency_default}} for evidence quality, duplicate submissions and split claims used to stay under {{approval_limit_expense}}, and reports findings to management. Records are retained for the period required under applicable tax and company law. This policy does not create an entitlement to any allowance not stated in the Expense Configuration.

Violations

Inflated, duplicated or fabricated claims, altered invoices, personal spend presented as business spend, and deliberate splitting of an expense to avoid an approval limit are treated as misconduct. Consequences may include rejection and recovery of the amount, withdrawal of spending authority, disciplinary action up to and including termination, and referral for legal action where fraud is established. Approvers who knowingly pass a non-compliant claim are held equally accountable.

Related Documents

  • Remote Work Policy
  • Information Security Policy
  • Delegation of Authority Policy

title: Asset Policy
html:
DRAFT — LEGAL REVIEW REQUIRED. This document is an operational or legal draft and must be reviewed and approved by authorized management and, where required, qualified legal counsel before becoming effective.

Purpose

PlantAtHome issues laptops and phones to office teams, tablets, label printers, scanners and weighing scales to hubs, cameras and lighting to the catalogue studio, and crates, insulated bags and trolleys to field operations. This policy defines how those assets are assigned, recorded, used, secured, and returned, so that equipment is traceable, the data on it is protected, and losses are handled consistently rather than case by case.

Scope

This policy applies to all employees, interns, consultants and contract staff of Silvestrix Green LLP who are issued a company asset, and to any asset in company custody at an office, hub, warehouse or studio, or at a person's home under an approved remote arrangement. It covers physical assets and the digital assets registered in the company's name, including domains, cloud accounts, gateway and courier consoles, the WhatsApp Business number, code repositories and design files. Assets belonging to nursery vendors or delivery partners remain governed by their own agreements.

Definitions

  • Company asset — any item or account purchased, leased or registered by the company and made available for work.
  • Asset register — the maintained record of every asset, its identifier, value, custodian, location and status.
  • Custodian — the person to whom an asset is assigned and who is accountable for it until it is returned or reassigned.
  • Shared asset — equipment assigned to a site or team rather than an individual, with a named site custodian.

Policy Statement

Company assets are provided for company work and remain company property at all times. Every asset has a single accountable custodian recorded in the asset register, and no asset moves between people, sites or cities without that record being updated. Assets carrying customer, vendor or financial data are treated as extensions of PlantAtHome Systems and are subject in full to the Information Security Policy.

Responsibilities

  • Finance and Administration — maintains the asset register, records purchase value and depreciation, and reconciles the register against physical checks.
  • Function heads and City Operations Leads — approve assignments in their area and confirm site inventories at each check.
  • Security Owner — sets device security requirements, approves disposal or re-issue of any data-bearing asset, and controls custodianship of digital assets.
  • Custodians — use the asset properly, keep it secure, report loss or damage immediately, and return it when asked or on exit.
  • People and Operations — runs the exit clearance and confirms return before final settlement.

Policy Requirements

Asset classExamplesAssigned byRegister and physical check
ComputingLaptops, monitors, docks, external drivesFunction head{{review_frequency_default}}
Mobile and connectivityCompany phones, SIM cards, the number bound to the WhatsApp Business APIFunction head with Security Owner{{review_frequency_default}}
Hub and field equipmentTablets, label printers, barcode scanners, weighing scales, trolleys, crates, insulated bagsCity Operations Lead{{review_frequency_default}}
StudioCameras, lenses, lighting and backdrops for catalogue shootsContent Lead{{review_frequency_default}}
Digital assetsDomains, cloud and hosting accounts, payment and courier consoles, repositories, design filesDesignated Partner{{risk_review_frequency}}
  • Assignment — assets are issued only against an approved request and an acknowledgement signed by the custodian recording the asset identifier, condition and accessories. No asset is handed over informally between colleagues.
  • Register — the register records identifier, description, purchase value and date, custodian, site, condition and status. Every issue, transfer, repair, write-off and return updates it on the day it happens.
  • Acceptable use — assets are used for company work; incidental personal use of a laptop or phone is tolerated where it does not interfere with work, consume company data allowances unreasonably, or introduce risk. Assets must not be used for any unlawful purpose, for a competing business, or for personal trading. No company asset may be lent, sold, pledged, or modified, and no unapproved software may be installed.
  • Security — data-bearing assets must meet the encryption, screen lock, update and authentication requirements of the Information Security Policy, including {{password_min_length}}. Assets are not left visible in vehicles or unattended in public, and field equipment is stored inside the hub at the close of operations.
  • Maintenance — repairs are arranged through Administration only; unauthorised repairs, jailbreaking or unofficial servicing void the arrangement and may make the custodian liable.

Procedures

  1. Issue — the function head raises the request; Administration issues the asset, records it and takes the custodian's acknowledgement; the Security Owner confirms device controls before any data access is enabled.
  2. Transfer — a transfer is routed through Administration, with condition noted at handover and the register updated for both parties.
  3. Loss or theft — report to the reporting manager, Administration and the Security Owner immediately; remote wipe and credential revocation are triggered for data-bearing assets, and a police complaint is filed where the circumstances warrant it. The incident is also handled under the Information Security Policy if data may be exposed.
  4. Damage — report before continuing to use the asset. Fair wear and tear and genuine accidents during work are borne by the company; damage from negligence, misuse or use outside this policy may be recovered from the custodian at written-down value, in accordance with applicable law and after the custodian has been heard.
  5. Return on exit or role change — all assets, accessories, SIMs, access cards and keys are returned and inspected as part of exit clearance; data-bearing devices are wiped and re-imaged before re-issue. Digital asset custodianship, including domains and console ownership, is transferred to the incoming custodian and confirmed by the Security Owner. Final settlement is processed only after clearance is recorded.
  6. Disposal — write-off or disposal requires Finance approval, certified data destruction for data-bearing assets, and a register entry closing the asset.

Exceptions

Extended custody of an asset at a personal residence, use of a personal device for company work, or retention of an asset beyond an approved engagement requires written approval from the function head and, where data is involved, the Security Owner. Approvals are time-bound, recorded in the register, and lapse on expiry.

Compliance

Administration reconciles the physical inventory to the register on the cadence in the table above and reports variances, ageing assets and unreturned items to management. Digital asset custodianship is reviewed at {{risk_review_frequency}} so that no critical account depends on a single individual. This policy is reviewed at {{review_frequency_default}}.

Violations

Failure to return an asset, unauthorised sale, lending or modification, concealment of loss or damage, or use of a company asset for unlawful or competing activity is treated as misconduct and may result in recovery of value, disciplinary action up to and including termination, withholding of clearance, and legal action. Recovery from dues is applied only to the extent permitted by law and after due process.

  • Remote Work Policy
  • Expense Policy
  • Employee Onboarding and Offboarding SOP

title: Disaster Recovery Plan
html:
DRAFT — LEGAL REVIEW REQUIRED. This document is an operational or legal draft and must be reviewed and approved by authorized management and, where required, qualified legal counsel before becoming effective.

Purpose

This plan defines how PlantAtHome, a brand of Silvestrix Green LLP, restores order-taking, fulfilment and customer communication after an event that makes production systems unavailable or untrustworthy. It exists so that recovery is executed from a written sequence rather than improvised during an outage, and so that management can see plainly which recovery capabilities are implemented today and which are still targets.

Scope

This plan covers production systems operated or contracted by the company: the commerce API and its database, cache and queue workers; the customer storefront, admin console and mobile applications; the media object store and content delivery layer; DNS and TLS; and the integration surfaces to the payment gateway, courier and hyperlocal delivery partners, and the messaging gateway used for WhatsApp, email and SMS notifications. It also covers the source repositories, deployment pipelines and secrets stores required to rebuild those systems. Vendor-operated nursery systems are out of scope except at the interfaces through which vendors accept, dispatch and settle orders.

Definitions

  • Disaster — an incident that removes a critical system for longer than a normal operational fault, or that renders its data untrustworthy, and that cannot be resolved by routine troubleshooting.
  • Recovery Time Objective (RTO) — the maximum intended elapsed time between disaster declaration and restoration of a system to at least degraded service.
  • Recovery Point Objective (RPO) — the maximum intended data loss, expressed as the age of the last usable restore point.
  • Degraded mode — a defined reduced service state, such as accepting prepaid orders while courier booking is suspended, that preserves revenue and customer trust while full recovery proceeds.
  • Recovery Objectives Configuration — the approved register that holds the RTO and RPO value for each system tier.

Policy Statement

The company maintains a documented and periodically exercised disaster recovery capability for all Tier 1 and Tier 2 systems. RTO and RPO are stated as targets recorded in the currently approved Recovery Objectives Configuration; they are not asserted anywhere in this document as achieved figures. Where a recovery step is manual — including database restore, region change and DNS repointing — this plan says so rather than implying automated failover. No system is classified Tier 1 unless a restore of its data has actually been tested.

Responsibilities

RoleResponsibility
Recovery Lead (senior engineering owner on call)Declares a disaster, sequences recovery, authorises degraded mode and stand-down.
Infrastructure ownerExecutes restores, rebuilds compute, cache and queue workers, verifies data integrity.
Operations and support leadHolds and releases affected orders, manages customer and vendor messaging over the approved support channels.
Finance ownerReconciles payments, refunds and vendor settlements captured or missed during the outage window.
Management sponsorApproves out-of-plan spend and any external or regulatory communication.

Policy Requirements

Systems are classified into recovery tiers. Objective cells reference configuration rather than fixed figures.

TierSystemsRTO / RPO targetBackup regime
Tier 1 — revenue criticalCommerce API, primary database, payment callback handling, storefront checkoutPer the currently approved Recovery Objectives ConfigurationBackups at {{backup_frequency}}, held for {{backup_retention}}
Tier 2 — fulfilment criticalQueue workers, courier and hyperlocal adapters, admin console, notification gatewayPer the currently approved Recovery Objectives ConfigurationBackups at {{backup_frequency}}, held for {{backup_retention}}
Tier 3 — deferrableReporting, catalogue import tooling, marketing automation, internal dashboardsRestored after Tier 1 and Tier 2 are stableHeld for {{backup_retention}}

Restore rehearsals are performed at {{restore_test_frequency}} against a non-production environment, and a rehearsal that does not end in a verified, queryable dataset is recorded as a failure. Credentials, integration keys and infrastructure definitions required for a rebuild are stored outside the systems they recover.

Procedures

  1. Detect and classify. The on-call engineer confirms impact and classifies severity using {{incident_severity_model}}; if a critical system is lost or data integrity is in doubt, the Recovery Lead declares a disaster.
  2. Activate. Open a recovery log, assemble the named roles, and freeze all non-recovery deployments.
  3. Stabilise commerce. Place checkout or courier booking into degraded mode where that protects customers from taking orders the business cannot fulfil.
  4. Recover in tier order. Restore Tier 1 data from the most recent verified restore point, rebuild application and worker capacity, then reconnect Tier 2 integrations.
  5. Verify before cutover. Confirm order, payment and inventory record counts against the restore point, replay or reconcile payment and courier callbacks received during the gap, and only then return live traffic.
  6. Communicate. Issue internal updates at {{escalation_timeline}}, notify affected customers and vendors through the approved {{support_channels}}, and route any statement with legal or regulatory weight through the management sponsor.
  7. Stand down. The Recovery Lead closes the event, lifts the deployment freeze and hands open reconciliation items to Finance and Operations with named owners.

Exceptions

Deviation from the recovery sequence is permitted only where following it would extend the outage or risk further data loss, and requires the Recovery Lead's decision to be recorded in the recovery log with its reasoning. Systems that cannot meet their tier objective must be recorded as an accepted gap in the risk register and reviewed at {{risk_review_frequency}} rather than left as an implied capability.

Compliance

This plan is reviewed at {{review_frequency_default}} and after any disaster declaration or failed restore rehearsal. Evidence of compliance comprises restore rehearsal records, backup verification output, recovery logs and post-incident reviews. A post-incident review is completed for every declared disaster and covers root cause, timeline against the tier objectives, customer and vendor impact, and corrective actions with owners and due dates.

Violations

Failure to maintain backups for an in-scope system, to participate in a scheduled rehearsal, to declare a qualifying disaster, or to record recovery actions in the recovery log is treated as a control failure and handled under the company's disciplinary process. Deliberately bypassing recovery verification before returning a system to live customer traffic is a serious violation given its direct effect on orders and payments.

Related Documents

  • Incident Response Plan
  • Change Management Policy
  • Information Security Policy
  • Data Backup and Retention Policy

title: Incident Response Plan
html:
DRAFT — LEGAL REVIEW REQUIRED. This document is an operational or legal draft and must be reviewed and approved by authorized management and, where required, qualified legal counsel before becoming effective.

Purpose

This plan sets out how PlantAtHome detects, contains and resolves security and operational incidents affecting customer data, payments, fulfilment or the availability of its platforms. It gives every person in the company a single reporting path and gives responders a defined lifecycle, so that decisions about containment, customer notification and regulatory reporting are made deliberately and on record.

Scope

This plan applies to all employees, contractors, interns and third parties with access to company systems or data, and to all incidents involving the commerce API and database, the storefront, admin console and mobile applications, the payment gateway integration, courier and hyperlocal delivery integrations, the WhatsApp, email and SMS notification gateway, the media store, and any company or personal device used to access company systems. It covers confidentiality, integrity and availability incidents alike, including suspected compromise of an employee or vendor account, unauthorised exposure of customer contact or address data, fraudulent order or refund activity, and platform outages.

Definitions

  • Event — an observation that may or may not indicate a problem, such as an alert, a failed job or an unusual login.
  • Incident — an event confirmed to have adverse effect on the confidentiality, integrity or availability of systems or data, or on the company's ability to serve customers.
  • Personal data incident — an incident involving unauthorised access to, disclosure of, alteration of or loss of customer, vendor or employee personal data.
  • Incident Commander — the single accountable owner of an open incident, responsible for decisions and the incident record.
  • Containment — action taken to stop ongoing harm, which may precede full understanding of the cause.

Policy Statement

All suspected incidents are reported immediately, without fear of blame and without waiting for confirmation. Every incident receives a severity rating under {{incident_severity_model}}, a named Incident Commander and a written record. Containment of harm to customers takes precedence over preserving uptime, over completing an investigation and over protecting the company's presentation of events. No employee may conceal, delay or informally settle an incident involving personal data, payments or safety.

Responsibilities

RoleResponsibility
Any employee, contractor or vendorReport suspected incidents immediately through the designated reporting channel; preserve evidence and change nothing unnecessarily.
On-call engineerTriage the report, assign an initial severity, and escalate to an Incident Commander where the severity warrants it.
Incident CommanderOwn the lifecycle, authorise containment, maintain the incident record and declare resolution.
Security ownerLead investigation of malicious or unauthorised access, decide on credential rotation and forensic preservation.
Support and operations leadManage affected orders and refunds and issue customer-facing messages over the approved {{support_channels}}.
Management sponsor and legal counselApprove external statements and determine regulatory or data-protection notification obligations.

Policy Requirements

Severity is assigned from the following guidance and confirmed against the approved {{incident_severity_model}}, which is authoritative where the two differ.

SeverityTypical situationResponse expectation
CriticalConfirmed exposure or loss of personal or payment data; checkout or payment capture down; systemic incorrect charges or refundsImmediate Incident Commander, management sponsor and legal counsel engaged per {{escalation_timeline}}
HighSuspected unauthorised access to an admin, vendor or infrastructure account; fulfilment or notification pipeline broadly failing; significant fraud patternIncident Commander assigned and containment started per {{escalation_timeline}}
MediumSingle-account compromise contained at detection; partial feature failure with a workaround; isolated data-accuracy defectHandled by on-call within {{support_response_sla}}, escalated if scope grows
LowPolicy deviation with no data or service impact; suspicious event requiring confirmationLogged and reviewed at {{review_frequency_default}}

Severity is re-assessed as facts change; it is raised freely and lowered only by the Incident Commander with reasons recorded. Every incident record must retain the reporter, timeline, actions taken, systems and data categories involved, and the decision on customer notification.

Procedures

  1. Detection. Incidents surface from monitoring and alerting, support and vendor reports, payment or courier partner notices, or direct observation by staff.
  2. Reporting. The observer reports immediately through the designated channel with what was seen, when and on which system. Reporting is not delayed to gather more certainty.
  3. Assessment. The on-call engineer confirms whether an event is an incident, assigns severity, and names an Incident Commander for High and Critical.
  4. Containment. Stop ongoing harm first: revoke or rotate affected credentials and tokens, disable the compromised account or endpoint, suspend the affected integration or place checkout in a restricted state. Preserve logs and artefacts before destructive remediation.
  5. Investigation. Establish scope, entry point, dwell time and the categories of data and the customers, vendors or orders affected. Where personal data is involved, legal counsel is engaged to determine notification obligations, and any data subject request arising from the incident is answered within {{dsr_response_time}}.
  6. Resolution. Apply the fix through the normal change path where time allows, or as an emergency change with retrospective approval where it does not.
  7. Recovery. Restore full service, verify order, payment and inventory integrity across the incident window, reconcile refunds and vendor settlements, and confirm monitoring is clean before closing.
  8. Post-incident review. Conducted for every Critical and High incident and for any repeat Medium, producing root cause, timeline, customer impact and corrective actions with named owners and due dates.

Exceptions

Deviation from the lifecycle is permitted only to reduce active harm to customers or data, and must be recorded in the incident record with the deciding role. No exception may be granted to the reporting obligation, to the engagement of legal counsel for a personal data incident, or to the completion of a post-incident review for a Critical incident.

Compliance

Incident records, severity assignments, notification decisions and post-incident actions are the evidence of compliance with this plan. Open corrective actions are tracked to closure and reviewed at {{review_frequency_default}}; incident trends and unresolved root causes are reviewed at {{risk_review_frequency}}. This plan is exercised alongside the recovery rehearsals described in the Disaster Recovery Plan.

Violations

Failing to report a suspected incident, concealing or misrepresenting one, destroying evidence, or handling a personal data incident outside this plan is a serious violation and is addressed under the company's disciplinary process, up to termination, and may be referred to law enforcement where conduct is unlawful. Vendors and contractors who breach this plan may have access withdrawn and their agreement terminated.

Related Documents

  • Disaster Recovery Plan
  • Information Security Policy
  • Privacy Policy
  • Change Management Policy

title: Change Management Policy
html:
DRAFT — LEGAL REVIEW REQUIRED. This document is an operational or legal draft and must be reviewed and approved by authorized management and, where required, qualified legal counsel before becoming effective.

Purpose

This policy governs how changes reach PlantAtHome production systems. Because a single deployment can affect live checkout, pricing, inventory availability, courier booking and customer notifications, changes are made through a defined path with assessment, approval, staging verification, a rollback position and a record — not directly on production by whoever is closest to the problem.

Scope

This policy applies to all changes to production application code, database schema and production data corrections, configuration and feature flags, infrastructure and networking, third-party integration credentials and endpoints (payment gateway, courier and hyperlocal partners, messaging gateway), scheduled jobs and queue workers, and access permissions to production systems. It applies to employees, contractors and any third party with production access. Content and catalogue edits made through the admin console in the normal course of business are out of scope, except where they alter pricing rules, delivery serviceability or checkout gating, which are treated as changes under this policy.

Definitions

  • Change — any addition, modification or removal affecting an in-scope production system.
  • Standard change — a pre-approved, low-risk, repeatable change of a type recorded in the approved Standard Change Register.
  • Normal change — any change requiring assessment and approval before deployment.
  • Emergency change — a change required to restore service or stop active harm, deployed with abbreviated approval and reviewed afterwards.
  • Staging — the pre-production environment that mirrors production configuration and is the mandatory proving ground for changes.
  • Rollback position — the specific, tested means of returning to the prior state, including how any data written by the change is handled.

Policy Statement

Every change is deployed to staging and verified there before it is deployed to production. No change is applied directly to production without a corresponding change record, an identified approver and a stated rollback position. Where a change cannot be rolled back — most commonly a destructive schema or data migration — that fact is declared in the change request and the change requires elevated approval rather than an assumption that reversal is possible.

Responsibilities

RoleResponsibility
Requester (engineer or owner)Raises the change request, states risk, blast radius, test evidence and rollback position.
ReviewerIndependently reviews code and migrations; may not be the same person as the requester for normal and emergency changes.
ApproverApproves against the currently approved Change Approval Matrix and confirms staging verification is complete.
DeployerExecutes the deployment, watches it to a confirmed healthy state, and executes rollback if verification fails.
Operations and support leadFlags customer-visible impact and prepares messaging where the change alters ordering, delivery or notifications.

Policy Requirements

Changes are classified and handled as follows. Approval authority and any monetary limit are taken from the currently approved Change Approval Matrix.

ClassExamplesStaging requiredApproval
StandardRoutine dependency patching, content deployment, adding a monitoring alert, listed items in the Standard Change RegisterYesPre-approved by class; record only
Normal — low riskIsolated feature behind a flag, additive schema change, non-critical job changeYes, with functional verificationReviewer plus engineering owner
Normal — high riskCheckout, pricing, availability, payment or courier integration changes; destructive or irreversible migrations; credential or endpoint rotationYes, with functional and regression verificationEngineering owner plus management sponsor; spend within {{approval_limit_expense}}
EmergencyChange required to resolve a live incident or stop active customer or financial harmWhere time permits; otherwise stated as not stagedIncident Commander at deployment, formal approval retrospectively per {{escalation_timeline}}

Every production database migration must be run first on staging against a representative dataset. Feature flags are the preferred mechanism for high-risk behaviour so that reversal does not require a redeployment. Production credentials and access grants change only through this policy, never as an undocumented side effect of another change.

Procedures

  1. Raise the change request. Record what is changing, why, which systems and customer journeys it touches, its class, and the intended deployment window.
  2. Assess risk. Identify blast radius, data impact, integration dependencies and whether the change is reversible; state the rollback position explicitly, including how data written after deployment will be handled.
  3. Review and approve. Obtain independent review and the approval level set by the Change Approval Matrix for the change class.
  4. Deploy to staging and test. Verify the intended behaviour, run the automated test suite, and exercise the affected journeys — typically order placement, payment callback handling, availability gating, courier booking and notification dispatch where those are touched.
  5. Deploy to production. Deploy only after staging verification is recorded, prefer low-traffic windows for high-risk changes, and watch the deployment through to a confirmed healthy state rather than assuming a green pipeline means a live change.
  6. Verify or roll back. Confirm the change in production against the stated success criteria; if verification fails, execute the rollback position immediately and treat further attempts as a new change.
  7. Document. Close the change record with what was deployed, when, by whom, verification evidence and any deviation from plan.
  8. Post-implementation review. Required for high-risk and emergency changes and for any change that was rolled back, covering whether risk was correctly assessed and what should change in the process.

Exceptions

Bypassing staging is permitted only for an emergency change during an active incident, and only with the deviation and its reason recorded in the change record and reviewed afterwards. Any other exception requires written approval from the engineering owner and the management sponsor before deployment. Standing exemptions are not granted; an exception applies to one change only.

Compliance

Change records, review approvals, staging verification evidence and deployment logs constitute the evidence of compliance. Change records are sampled and reviewed at {{review_frequency_default}}, and change-related incidents and rollback rates are examined at {{risk_review_frequency}} to identify classes of change that need stronger controls. Records are retained for {{data_retention_period}} unless a longer period is required for audit or legal purposes.

Violations

Deploying to production without an approved change record, bypassing staging outside a declared emergency, applying undocumented manual edits to production data or configuration, or granting production access outside this policy is a control failure handled under the company's disciplinary process. Repeated or deliberate circumvention may result in withdrawal of production access, and for contractors and vendors, termination of engagement.

Related Documents

  • Incident Response Plan
  • Disaster Recovery Plan
  • Information Security Policy
  • Software Development Lifecycle Standard

title: API Usage Policy
html:
DRAFT — LEGAL REVIEW REQUIRED. This document is an operational or legal draft and must be reviewed and approved by authorized management and, where required, qualified legal counsel before becoming effective.

Purpose

This policy defines the conditions under which the application programming interfaces operated by Silvestrix Green LLP under the PlantAtHome brand may be accessed, and the controls that apply to the credentials used to access them. It exists to protect customer personal data, order and payment records, vendor catalogue and settlement data, and the availability of the commerce platform itself.

Scope

This policy applies to every PlantAtHome API surface, including the commerce and catalogue APIs, the modular services API namespace, the delivery and shipping microservices, and all webhook receivers that accept callbacks from courier, payment and messaging providers. It applies to every consumer of those interfaces: the storefront, the admin console, the mobile applications, approved nursery vendor systems, logistics partners, payment and messaging gateways, reporting and analytics tools, and any employee or contractor who calls an endpoint directly using a token or key.

Definitions

  • API credential — any key, token, secret or signing key that authenticates a caller to a PlantAtHome interface.
  • First-party client — an application built and operated by PlantAtHome (storefront, admin, mobile).
  • Integration partner — an approved vendor, courier, payment or messaging provider whose systems exchange data with ours.
  • Integration owner — the named PlantAtHome employee accountable for a specific credential and its use.
  • Rate limit — the ceiling on request volume for a credential, defined in the currently approved API Rate Limit Configuration.
  • Webhook callback — an inbound request from a partner reporting a state change, such as a shipment or payment event.

Policy Statement

API access is granted to a named integration for a stated business purpose, on least-privilege terms, and never to a person or a team as a general entitlement. Credentials remain the property of Silvestrix Green LLP, are non-transferable, and may be throttled, restricted or suspended at any time where PlantAtHome reasonably believes that continued access threatens platform stability, data confidentiality or the integrity of customer orders. All usage is logged and monitored.

Responsibilities

  • Engineering lead — issues, rotates and revokes credentials; maintains the API Rate Limit Configuration and the credential register.
  • Security owner — reviews scopes and access grants at the frequency set by {{review_frequency_default}}; approves exceptions jointly with the engineering lead.
  • Integration owner — keeps the purpose, scope and contact details of a credential current, and reports suspected compromise immediately.
  • Integration partners and vendors — protect issued credentials, call only the endpoints their scope permits, and notify PlantAtHome of compromise or of any change of the systems using the credential.
  • Support and operations — escalate suspected abuse rather than reissuing credentials directly.

Policy Requirements

Every credential must be authenticated, scoped, attributed to an owner, and rate limited. The controls that apply by credential class are set out below; all numeric limits are held in configuration and are not restated here.

Credential classAuthenticationRate limitPermitted data scopeRotation
First-party clientAuthenticated user session plus short-lived bearer tokenAs per the currently approved API Rate Limit ConfigurationData belonging to the authenticated user onlyOn expiry of the token lifetime in configuration
Vendor integration keyIssued key with source restrictionsAs per the currently approved API Rate Limit ConfigurationOwn catalogue, own inventory, own order lines and settlement recordsOn suspected compromise, offboarding, or the interval in the approved Credential Rotation Configuration
Logistics or payment callbackSigned request verified against the provider signing secretAs per the currently approved API Rate Limit ConfigurationWrite of shipment or payment state on referenced orders onlyOn provider secret rotation or suspected compromise
Reporting or analytics tokenIssued key, read-onlyAs per the currently approved API Rate Limit ConfigurationAggregated or masked data; no payment instrument dataPer the approved Credential Rotation Configuration
Administrative service tokenIssued key with multi-factor protected issuanceAs per the currently approved API Rate Limit ConfigurationAs defined by the granted role permissionsOn role change, offboarding or suspected compromise

Credentials must never be embedded in client-side code, mobile bundles, shared documents, chat messages or version control. Personal data returned by an endpoint may be used only for the stated purpose and retained no longer than {{data_retention_period}}. Callbacks that cannot be signature-verified are treated as untrusted triggers: the authenticated partner interface is the authority for the resulting state change.

Procedures

  1. Request — the integration owner submits the purpose, endpoints, data fields and expected volume for review.
  2. Issue — the engineering lead creates a scoped credential, records it in the credential register, and delivers it through an approved secret channel, never over email or chat.
  3. Monitor — request logs, error rates and volume against configured limits are reviewed continuously; anomalies are raised as incidents under the approved incident severity model {{incident_severity_model}}.
  4. Throttle or suspend — on abuse, credential leakage or platform risk, access is restricted immediately and the integration owner and partner contact are notified.
  5. Reinstate — access resumes only after the cause is remediated, the credential is rotated, and the engineering lead and security owner both approve.
  6. Decommission — credentials for ended integrations or departed staff are revoked as part of offboarding, not left dormant.

Exceptions

Exceptions, including temporary limit increases for catalogue migrations or seasonal load, must be requested in writing, justified, time-bound, and approved jointly by the engineering lead and the security owner. Approved exceptions are recorded in the exception register with an expiry date and are reviewed at {{review_frequency_default}}. An expired exception lapses automatically.

Compliance

Compliance is evidenced by the credential register, request and access logs, rate limit configuration history, and records of suspension and reinstatement decisions. Access to personal data through these interfaces is subject to PlantAtHome's data protection obligations, including responses to data subject requests within {{dsr_response_time}}. Nothing in this policy is a representation that any specific certification has been obtained.

Violations

Prohibited use includes sharing or reselling credentials, scraping or bulk-extracting catalogue, pricing or customer data beyond the granted scope, attempting to access another vendor's records, circumventing rate limits through multiple credentials, probing for vulnerabilities without written authorisation, and using order or contact data for unapproved marketing. Violations result in immediate suspension, escalation within {{escalation_timeline}}, contractual action for vendors and partners under the Vendor Agreement, disciplinary action for employees and contractors, and referral to authorities where the conduct may be unlawful.

Related Documents
