  • Data Protection and Privacy Policy
  • Vendor Agreement

title: Security Standards
html:
DRAFT — LEGAL REVIEW REQUIRED. This document is an operational or legal draft and must be reviewed and approved by authorized management and, where required, qualified legal counsel before becoming effective.

Purpose

These standards define the minimum technical security controls for the systems that run PlantAtHome: the commerce API and database, the admin console, the storefront, the mobile applications, the delivery and shipping services, the media store, and the third-party integrations for payments, courier booking and customer messaging. They translate our security intent into requirements an engineer can implement and an auditor can verify.

Scope

This document applies to all production and non-production environments operated by Silvestrix Green LLP for the PlantAtHome brand, to all code repositories and deployment pipelines, and to every employee, contractor and vendor engineer with access to them. It covers data in transit, data at rest, secrets, third-party dependencies, environment separation and periodic access review.

Definitions

  • Production — any environment holding real customer, vendor, order or payment data.
  • Staging — the pre-release environment used for verification before promotion to production.
  • Secret — any credential, key, token, signing key or connection string that grants access to a system or data.
  • Sensitive personal data — customer identity, contact, address and location data, and any payment-related identifiers.
  • Shared component — infrastructure deliberately used by more than one environment.

Policy Statement

Customer and vendor data is encrypted in transit and at rest, secrets live only in managed secret storage, dependencies are patched on a defined cadence, production is separated from every other environment, and access is granted on least privilege and re-verified on a schedule. Where a control cannot be met, the gap is recorded and time-bound rather than tolerated silently.

Responsibilities

  • Security owner — maintains these standards, runs access reviews at {{review_frequency_default}}, and owns the risk register reviewed at {{risk_review_frequency}}.
  • Engineering lead — implements the controls, owns the deployment pipeline and the secret store, and approves production access.
  • Engineers — follow the standards in day-to-day work and raise deviations rather than working around them.
  • Operations — monitor alerts and raise incidents under the approved severity model {{incident_severity_model}}.

Policy Requirements

Encryption

All external traffic to the storefront, admin console, mobile applications and public APIs is served over TLS only, using a protocol version and cipher set no weaker than the approved Encryption Configuration, with plaintext requests redirected and strict transport security enabled. Internal service-to-service traffic that leaves a private network is likewise encrypted. Data at rest is encrypted using industry-standard symmetric encryption for the primary database, its backups and snapshots, the object store holding product and customer-uploaded media, and any log store containing personal data.

Data classIn transitAt restKey custody
Customer identity, contact and addressTLS per approved Encryption ConfigurationEncrypted database and backup volumesManaged key service, access restricted to production role holders
Payment references and gateway tokensTLS per approved Encryption ConfigurationEncrypted at rest; card data never stored by PlantAtHomePayment gateway holds instrument data; we hold references only
Vendor settlement and commercial recordsTLS per approved Encryption ConfigurationEncrypted database and backup volumesManaged key service
Product and user-uploaded mediaTLS per approved Encryption ConfigurationServer-side encryption on the object storeManaged key service, bucket policy restricted to the application role
Application secretsRetrieved over encrypted channels onlyManaged secret store or encrypted configuration recordEngineering lead and security owner

Secrets management

Secrets are held in the managed secret store or in encrypted configuration records, injected at runtime, and never committed to version control, pasted into chat or tickets, embedded in mobile bundles, or written into client-side code. Repositories are scanned for secret patterns before merge. Any secret that reaches a place it should not have reached is treated as compromised and rotated, not merely deleted. Rotation follows the approved Credential Rotation Configuration and is mandatory on staff offboarding, vendor offboarding and suspected exposure. Workers and long-lived processes are restarted after a secret change so that no process continues on a revoked value.

Dependency and patch management

Application dependencies, base images and runtime versions are inventoried and monitored for published vulnerabilities. Findings are triaged against the approved severity model {{incident_severity_model}}; the highest severities are remediated on the emergency change path and the remainder in the routine maintenance cycle. Unmaintained or abandoned dependencies are scheduled for replacement rather than pinned indefinitely. No dependency is added without a review of its maintenance status and licence.

Environment separation

Production holds its own database, credentials, signing keys, gateway accounts and messaging credentials; no non-production system may hold a production secret. Non-production environments must be pointed at sandbox or test accounts for payments, courier booking and messaging, and code must gate destructive or live-partner actions on the environment setting rather than on hostname inspection. Production data may be copied into a lower environment only with prior approval and only after identifiers and contact details are masked. Where a component is genuinely shared between environments, such as a common media bucket, the sharing must be recorded in the risk register, its blast radius documented, and destructive operations against it blocked outside production.

Access review

Access to production systems, cloud accounts, repositories, the payment gateway and the messaging gateway is granted by named individual, never by shared login, and requires multi-factor authentication where the provider supports it. The security owner reconciles every grant against current roles at {{review_frequency_default}}, and immediately on any change of role or exit.

Procedures

  1. Changes reach production only through the reviewed pipeline; direct edits on servers are permitted only under a declared incident and are reverted into the repository afterwards.
  2. Certificate expiry, dependency advisories and failed access reviews raise tickets automatically with a named owner.
  3. Suspected compromise is raised as an incident, secrets are rotated first and investigated second, and follow-up actions are tracked to closure.
  4. New integrations are assessed for data flow, credential handling and environment separation before their first production call.

Exceptions

Any deviation requires written approval from the engineering lead and the security owner, a documented compensating control, and an expiry date. Exceptions are recorded in the risk register and reviewed at {{risk_review_frequency}}. An exception without a compensating control is not approved.

Compliance

Compliance is demonstrated through access review records, secret rotation records, dependency scan results, deployment history and incident records. These standards support our obligations regarding personal data and payment handling but are not, by themselves, a claim of certification against any external scheme.

Violations

Committing secrets to a repository, copying unmasked production data into a lower environment, disabling encryption or transport security, sharing production credentials, or bypassing the deployment pipeline outside a declared incident are treated as security violations. Consequences include immediate revocation of access, mandatory rotation, escalation within {{escalation_timeline}}, disciplinary action for employees and contractors, and contractual action for vendors.

Related Documents

  • API Usage Policy
  • Password Policy
  • Backup Policy
  • Incident Response Plan

title: Password Policy
html:
DRAFT — LEGAL REVIEW REQUIRED. This document is an operational or legal draft and must be reviewed and approved by authorized management and, where required, qualified legal counsel before becoming effective.

Purpose

This policy sets the rules for creating, storing, using, resetting and retiring the passwords that protect PlantAtHome systems and customer accounts. Weak or reused credentials are the most common route into an e-commerce platform, and a single compromised administrative login would expose customer addresses, order history, vendor settlement data and the ability to change prices and dispatch instructions.

Scope

This policy applies to all employees, contractors, vendor users and administrators who hold an account on any PlantAtHome system, including the admin console, the commerce API, the storefront and mobile customer accounts, the cloud provider console, code repositories, the payment gateway dashboard, the messaging gateway, courier partner portals and internal support tools. It also governs how the platform stores and verifies customer credentials.

Definitions

  • Password — any secret string used to authenticate a person, including passphrases.
  • Multi-factor authentication (MFA) — a second, independent authentication factor in addition to the password.
  • Privileged account — any account able to change roles, prices, orders, payouts, infrastructure or code.
  • Break-glass account — an emergency account used only when normal administrative access is unavailable.
  • Compromised credential — a password known or reasonably suspected to be in the possession of anyone other than its holder.

Policy Statement

Every account is personal and attributable. Passwords meet the minimum length {{password_min_length}}, are stored only in a form that cannot be reversed, are never shared or reused across systems, and are protected by a second factor wherever the system supports one. Privileged access carries stronger requirements than ordinary access, and a suspected compromise is acted on immediately rather than investigated first.

Responsibilities

  • Security owner — maintains this policy, runs credential reviews at {{review_frequency_default}} and rules on exceptions.
  • Engineering lead — enforces the requirements in code and platform configuration and manages the break-glass account.
  • People operations — triggers account creation on joining and revocation on exit, on the day the change takes effect.
  • Account holders — choose unique passwords, use the approved password manager, never share credentials, and report suspected compromise immediately.
  • Support team — verifies customer identity through the approved flow and never asks for, receives or reads back a password.

Policy Requirements

Passwords must meet the minimum length {{password_min_length}}, must not be a system default, must not reuse a password used on another service, and are screened against known-breached and trivially guessable values at the point of creation. Length and uniqueness are preferred over enforced character classes and routine expiry; passwords are changed on evidence of compromise, not on a calendar. Passwords are stored only as a salted hash produced by an approved slow, memory-hard algorithm such as bcrypt, and are never stored, logged, emailed, transmitted or displayed in a reversible form. Any system that can email a user their existing password is non-compliant and must be remediated or replaced.

Account typeMinimum lengthMFAStorageChange trigger
Customer storefront and mobile account{{password_min_length}}Offered where supported; one-time code over the approved messaging channel for verificationSalted hash, irreversibleSelf-service reset, or forced reset on suspected compromise
Vendor console user{{password_min_length}}Required where the provider supports itSalted hash, irreversibleOn compromise, role change or offboarding
Employee and contractor account{{password_min_length}}Required where the provider supports itSalted hash, irreversibleOn compromise, role change or exit
Privileged administrative account{{password_min_length}}, and longer where the approved Access Configuration requiresMandatory, no exemptionSalted hash, irreversible; secret held in the approved password managerOn compromise, role change, exit, or per the approved Credential Rotation Configuration
Cloud, gateway and repository root or owner account{{password_min_length}}, and longer where the approved Access Configuration requiresMandatory, hardware or authenticator factorSealed in the approved password manager with dual custodyOn any custodian change or suspected exposure

Shared logins are prohibited. Where a platform genuinely offers only one account, the credential is held in the approved password manager, access to it is logged, and it is rotated whenever a person with access leaves that role. Service and machine identities use API credentials rather than human passwords and are governed by the API Usage Policy.

Procedures

  1. Creation — accounts are issued individually on joining; the first login forces the account holder to set their own password, and no administrator retains knowledge of it.
  2. Reset — resets run through the self-service flow using a time-limited, single-use link or one-time code sent to the verified contact on record. Support staff may trigger a reset but never set, view or communicate a password. Identity is verified through the approved support verification flow before any reset is triggered on a customer's behalf.
  3. MFA enrolment — privileged users enrol a second factor before first privileged use; recovery codes are stored in the approved password manager, never in personal notes or email.
  4. Compromised credentials — the account holder or any observer reports the event immediately; the account is disabled or the password force-reset, active sessions and tokens are revoked, related credentials are rotated, and the event is raised as an incident under the approved severity model {{incident_severity_model}} and escalated within {{escalation_timeline}}. Where customer accounts are implicated, affected users are forced to reset and are notified.
  5. Offboarding — all accounts are disabled on the effective date, shared secrets the person could access are rotated, and the closure is recorded.
  6. Review — the security owner reconciles active accounts and MFA enrolment against current roles at {{review_frequency_default}}.

Exceptions

Exceptions require written approval from the security owner and the engineering lead, a compensating control such as source restriction or reduced privilege, and an expiry date recorded in the exception register. MFA on privileged and root accounts is not subject to exception. A legacy system that cannot meet these requirements is scheduled for remediation or replacement, and the gap is carried in the risk register until closed.

Compliance

Compliance is evidenced by platform password configuration, MFA enrolment records, access review records, reset and incident logs, and offboarding records. Support interactions are audited to confirm that passwords are never requested or disclosed.

Violations

Sharing a password, reusing a work password on a personal service, storing credentials in plaintext files, chat, spreadsheets or code, disabling MFA on a privileged account, or failing to report a suspected compromise are violations of this policy. Consequences include immediate suspension of access, mandatory rotation, disciplinary action for employees and contractors, and suspension or termination of access for vendor users under the Vendor Agreement.

Related Documents

  • Security Standards
  • API Usage Policy
  • Incident Response Plan
  • Employee Handbook

title: Backup Policy
html:
DRAFT — LEGAL REVIEW REQUIRED. This document is an operational or legal draft and must be reviewed and approved by authorized management and, where required, qualified legal counsel before becoming effective.

Purpose

This policy defines what PlantAtHome backs up, how often, for how long, how backups are protected, and how restoration is proven to work. Order, payment reference, vendor settlement and customer address data cannot be reconstructed from any other source, and product media represents substantial catalogue effort; the point of a backup programme is a tested restore, not a stored file.

Scope

This policy covers all production systems operated by Silvestrix Green LLP for the PlantAtHome brand: the primary commerce database, the object store holding product and customer-uploaded media, application configuration and secrets, delivery and shipping service data stores, search and reporting stores derived from primary data, and source code repositories. It applies to the engineering, operations and security roles that run and verify these backups.

Definitions

  • Backup — a copy of data held separately from the running system, from which the data can be restored.
  • Retention — the period a backup copy is kept before secure deletion.
  • Restore test — a rehearsed recovery of a backup into an isolated environment, verified against expected content.
  • Derived store — a system rebuildable from primary data, such as a search index or a cache.
  • Backup failure — any missed, incomplete, corrupt or unverifiable backup run.

Policy Statement

Every system holding data that cannot be regenerated is backed up on the approved schedule {{backup_frequency}}, retained for {{backup_retention}}, encrypted at rest and in transit, stored separately from the system it protects, restricted to named custodians, and proven by restore testing at {{restore_test_frequency}}. A backup that has never been restored is treated as unverified, not as protection.

Responsibilities

  • Engineering lead — owns backup configuration and coverage, and confirms that every new production data store is added to this policy before it goes live.
  • Operations — monitors backup jobs, raises failures as incidents and tracks them to closure.
  • Security owner — controls access to backup storage and keys, and reviews that access at {{review_frequency_default}}.
  • Restore test owner — plans and records restore tests at {{restore_test_frequency}} and reports the results to management.

Policy Requirements

Backup coverage by system is set out below. All frequency and retention values are held in configuration and referenced through the approved variables; they are not restated as fixed figures in this document.

SystemWhat is capturedFrequencyRetentionRestore testing
Primary commerce database (orders, customers, vendors, catalogue, settlements)Full snapshot plus transaction logs for point-in-time recovery{{backup_frequency}}{{backup_retention}}{{restore_test_frequency}}
Media object store (product and customer-uploaded images and documents)Object copies to a separate destination, with versioning or an equivalent immutability control{{backup_frequency}}{{backup_retention}}{{restore_test_frequency}}
Application configuration and secretsEncrypted export of configuration records and secret store contents{{backup_frequency}}{{backup_retention}}{{restore_test_frequency}}
Delivery and shipping service data storesSnapshot of partner order and shipment ledgers{{backup_frequency}}{{backup_retention}}{{restore_test_frequency}}
Source code and infrastructure definitionsMirror of repositories including branches and tags{{backup_frequency}}{{backup_retention}}{{restore_test_frequency}}
Derived stores (cache, search index, queues)Not backed up; rebuild procedure documented and tested insteadNot applicableNot applicableRebuild rehearsed at {{restore_test_frequency}}

Backups must be encrypted at rest with a managed key and transferred only over encrypted channels. Backup storage must be logically separate from the production account or bucket it protects, so that a compromise or accidental deletion in production cannot destroy the copies. Deletion of backup data must require elevated privileges and be logged. Personal data inside backups remains subject to {{data_retention_period}}; where a deletion request cannot be executed inside an immutable backup, the record is suppressed on restore and the reason documented. Backups may never be restored into a staging or development environment without the masking required by the Security Standards.

Procedures

  1. Run and verify — scheduled jobs run at {{backup_frequency}}; each run is verified for completion, size sanity and checksum integrity, and the result is recorded automatically.
  2. Alert — any failed, skipped or unverifiable run raises an alert to operations on the same schedule cycle, never silently.
  3. Restore testing — at {{restore_test_frequency}}, a backup is restored into an isolated environment and validated against agreed checks: recent orders present, media objects resolvable, referential integrity intact, and application boot successful. Results, elapsed restore time and any gaps are recorded.
  4. Real recovery — a production restore is authorised by the engineering lead, executed from the most recent verified backup, and recorded as an incident with a written timeline and post-incident review.
  5. Expiry — backups past {{backup_retention}} are securely deleted through the automated lifecycle rule; manual copies outside that lifecycle are prohibited.
  6. Change control — a new production data store is not released until its backup coverage and restore path are configured and this policy's table is updated.

Backup failure handling

A failed run is triaged under the approved severity model {{incident_severity_model}}. Operations re-runs the job, confirms the last known good copy, and identifies the exposure window created by the gap. Consecutive failures on the same system, or any failure affecting the primary commerce database, are escalated to the engineering lead within {{escalation_timeline}}. A system left without a verified backup is treated as an open risk in the risk register, reviewed at {{risk_review_frequency}}, until a successful verified run is recorded. A failed restore test is treated with the same seriousness as a failed backup.

Exceptions

Any system excluded from backup, retained for a shorter period, or exempted from restore testing requires written approval from the engineering lead and the security owner, a stated justification and rebuild path, an expiry date, and an entry in the exception register reviewed at {{review_frequency_default}}. The primary commerce database is not eligible for exception.

Compliance

Compliance is evidenced by backup job logs, integrity verification records, restore test reports, access review records for backup storage and keys, and incident records for failures and recoveries. These records also support our obligations to retain transactional and tax documentation, including invoices issued within {{gst_invoice_timeline}}, for the periods required by applicable law.

Violations

Disabling or reconfiguring a backup job without approval, storing backup copies on personal devices or unapproved storage, restoring production data into a non-production environment without masking and approval, sharing backup credentials or keys, or suppressing a backup failure rather than reporting it are violations of this policy. Consequences include withdrawal of infrastructure access, disciplinary action for employees and contractors, and contractual action for vendors and service providers.

Related Documents

  • Security Standards
  • Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery Plan
  • Incident Response Plan
  • Data Protection and Privacy Policy

title: Order Settlement SOP
html:
DRAFT — LEGAL REVIEW REQUIRED. This document is an operational or legal draft and must be reviewed and approved by authorized management and, where required, qualified legal counsel before becoming effective.

Purpose

This procedure defines how PlantAtHome, a brand of Silvestrix Green LLP, converts a customer payment into captured, ledger-posted and bank-matched money, and how the resulting balances become vendor payouts. It exists so that any order can be traced end to end — order value, gateway capture, gateway settlement, bank credit, ledger entry, vendor payable — without reconstructing history manually at period close.

Scope

Applies to all orders placed through the PlantAtHome website, mobile app and assisted or corporate channels, across live plants, gardening tools, pots and planters, seeds, fertilizers, accessories, FarmBox fresh produce and corporate gifting. Covers prepaid payments captured through Razorpay, cash collected on delivery by hyperlocal riders or courier partners, store credit adjustments, refunds, and settlement to approved nursery vendors for vendor-fulfilled lines. Excludes non-marketplace supplier invoices, payroll, and the approval of refunds themselves, which follow the Refund and Cancellation Policy.

Definitions

  • Authorisation — the gateway has reserved customer funds but has not moved them; the order is not yet paid.
  • Capture — the authorised amount is claimed and becomes receivable from the gateway.
  • Gateway settlement (payout) — a net credit from Razorpay to the company bank account aggregating captures less refunds, fees and taxes, identified by a payout reference and a bank UTR.
  • COD remittance — cash collected on delivery and remitted by the rider or courier partner under the applicable partner agreement.
  • Vendor group — the per-vendor split of an order used for fulfilment and settlement; one order may produce several vendor groups.
  • Settlement variance — any unexplained difference between expected and received amounts at capture, payout or bank level.
  • Unsettled receivable — money captured or collected but not yet matched to a bank credit.

Roles and Responsibilities

  • Finance Executive — runs the daily settlement cycle, performs matching, posts entries, maintains the exception register.
  • Finance Manager — reviews variances, approves ledger corrections and vendor statements within delegated limits.
  • Vendor Manager — validates vendor master data, commission terms and penalties, and handles vendor settlement queries.
  • Operations Manager — confirms delivery and COD collection status feeding settlement eligibility.
  • Engineering on-call — investigates capture, webhook and export failures.
  • Authorised signatory — releases payouts above delegated limits.

Prerequisites

  • Production (not test) gateway keys verified in the live environment, and the settlement bank account mapped at the gateway.
  • Chart of accounts and posting codes approved by the Finance Manager.
  • Vendor master complete: legal name, GSTIN, bank details, and commission terms recorded per {{commission_model}}.
  • Role-based access limiting settlement actions to finance roles, with segregation between preparer and approver.
  • Automated daily export of orders, payments, refunds and delivery status, plus access to gateway settlement and partner COD statements.

Trigger

The cycle runs each finance working day as defined in the currently approved Settlement Run Configuration, and additionally on: receipt of a gateway payout, receipt of a partner COD remittance statement, and period close.

Step-by-Step Procedure

  1. Extract all orders in a payment-relevant state and confirm every prepaid order carries a captured payment; list authorisations that remain uncaptured beyond the currently approved Capture Configuration window.
  2. Close the capture gap: capture or void each stale authorisation per that configuration, and confirm cancelled or failed payments have released reserved inventory.
  3. Post order-level entries using the matrix below; never post from a screenshot or an email, only from the system export.
  4. Ingest the gateway settlement report and record, per payout, gross captures, refunds, fees, tax on fees and adjustments.
  5. Match each payout to a bank credit by UTR and amount. Unmatched payouts and unexplained bank credits go straight to the exception register.
  6. Post gateway fees and the tax charged on them separately so input credit can be claimed under the GST Invoicing SOP.
  7. Reconcile partner COD statements against delivered COD orders; short, late or missing remittances are raised with the partner and tracked as unsettled receivable.
  8. Compute vendor settlement for delivered vendor lines that have passed the applicable return window, less commission per {{commission_model}}, less deductions per {{penalty_schedule}}, less statutory withholdings, on the cycle defined by {{vendor_settlement_cycle}}.
  9. Publish vendor statements showing every included order line and deduction; vendors may dispute within {{vendor_settlement_dispute_window}}.
  10. Obtain approval per {{approval_limit_expense}} and release payouts; record the bank reference against the statement.
  11. Roll forward every unresolved item in the exception register with owner and next action.
  12. At close, confirm unsettled receivable equals gateway balance plus COD in transit, and attach the evidence pack to the period file.
EventLedger effectSource of truthTiming
Prepaid captureGateway receivable debited, customer liability or revenue recognised per policyGateway capture recordSame settlement run
COD deliveryPartner receivable debitedDelivery confirmationSame settlement run
Payout receivedBank debited, gateway receivable clearedBank UTR plus payout reportAs per the currently approved Settlement Run Configuration
Gateway fees and taxExpense and input tax recognisedPayout reportWith the payout
RefundRevenue or liability reversedApproved refund record{{refund_processing_time}}
Vendor payableVendor liability raised net of commission and deductionsVendor group settlement run{{vendor_settlement_cycle}}

SLA

ActivityTarget
Capture completeness checkEvery run of the currently approved Settlement Run Configuration
Payout to bank matchingAs per the currently approved Settlement Run Configuration
Refund posting after approval{{refund_processing_time}}
Variance investigation and escalation{{escalation_timeline}}
Vendor statement publication{{vendor_settlement_cycle}}
Vendor dispute resolution{{vendor_settlement_dispute_window}}

Quality Checks

  • Every captured payment has exactly one ledger posting and every payout has exactly one bank match; duplicate UTRs are rejected.
  • No order sits in a paid state without a gateway capture reference, and no capture exists without an order.
  • Test-mode payment identifiers appearing in production data are treated as an incident, not a variance.
  • Vendor payable totals reconcile to the sum of settled vendor group lines less recorded deductions.
  • Refunds and chargebacks appear once, in one period, and never both reduce revenue and raise an expense.

Exceptions

Partial captures, orders edited after capture, payouts placed on hold by the gateway, short or delayed COD remittance, failed vendor bank transfers and duplicate settlements are not corrected silently. Each is logged with the order or payout reference, the amount, the cause and the corrective entry, and requires Finance Manager approval before posting. Chargebacks and disputed transactions are handed to the Payment Reconciliation SOP rather than adjusted here.

Escalation Process

Unresolved variances escalate on {{escalation_timeline}} from Finance Executive to Finance Manager, then to the Finance lead and an authorised signatory. Write-offs and compensating credits require approval within {{approval_limit_refund}} or {{approval_limit_expense}} as applicable. A suspected systemic failure — missing webhooks, mismatched environments, or payouts to the wrong account — is raised as an incident and graded under {{incident_severity_model}}, with settlement releases paused until the cause is known.

Records and Audit Trail

Retain per settlement run: the order and payment export, the gateway settlement report, the bank statement extract, the matching workpaper, the exception register, vendor statements and payout confirmations, and the approval record for every manual entry. Records are stored in the finance repository, are write-once once approved, and are retained for {{data_retention_period}}. Ledger corrections carry the preparer, approver, timestamp and reason. This procedure is reviewed at {{review_frequency_default}} or on any change to the gateway, bank arrangement or commission terms.

Related Documents

  • Payment Reconciliation SOP
  • GST Invoicing SOP
  • Refund and Cancellation Policy
  • Vendor Agreement

title: GST Invoicing SOP
html:
DRAFT — LEGAL REVIEW REQUIRED. This document is an operational or legal draft and must be reviewed and approved by authorized management and, where required, qualified legal counsel before becoming effective.

Purpose

This procedure sets out how PlantAtHome, a brand of Silvestrix Green LLP, raises tax documents for customer orders and vendor-fulfilled supplies under the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 and the rules made under it: what document is issued, when, with what classification, how corrections are made through credit and debit notes, and how the records are kept and produced on demand.

Scope

Covers every taxable and exempt outward supply billed through the PlantAtHome platform — live plants, gardening tools, pots and planters, seeds, fertilizers, accessories, FarmBox fresh produce and corporate gifting — for direct and vendor-fulfilled orders, in hyperlocal and pan-India courier lanes, on prepaid and cash on delivery terms. It includes shipping and handling charges billed to the customer, cancellations, returns and replacements. It excludes inward supplier invoices, the marketplace operator's periodic tax filings, and the accounting entries themselves, which follow the Order Settlement SOP.

Definitions

  • Tax invoice — the document issued for a taxable supply, carrying the statutory particulars including supplier and recipient details, HSN, taxable value, rate and tax amount.
  • Bill of supply — the document issued where the supply is exempt or the supplier is not permitted to charge tax on it.
  • Credit note — the document reducing the value or tax of a supply already invoiced, for example on return, cancellation after invoicing or a price correction downward.
  • E-invoice / IRN — an invoice reported to the Invoice Registration Portal that returns an Invoice Reference Number and signed QR code, applicable where the notified turnover conditions are met.
  • Place of supply — the state determining whether integrated tax or central and state tax applies, derived from the delivery address for goods.
  • HSN and Rate Master — the approved mapping of each SKU to its classification and rate, maintained in the catalogue.

Roles and Responsibilities

  • Finance Executive — monitors invoice generation, resolves failures, issues credit and debit notes.
  • Finance Manager — owns the HSN and Rate Master, approves classification changes and manual documents.
  • Catalogue team — records classification against every new SKU before it is published for sale.
  • Engineering — maintains invoice numbering, e-invoice integration and document storage.
  • Vendor Manager — ensures vendor GSTIN and registration status on file are current for vendor-fulfilled supplies.
  • Tax advisor — advises on applicability, classification disputes and filings.

Prerequisites

  • Active GST registration for each place of business, with a documented invoice series per registration that is continuous and unique for the financial year.
  • Every saleable SKU mapped in the HSN and Rate Master; a SKU without a mapping must not be sellable.
  • Customer GSTIN capture available at checkout for business and corporate gifting orders, validated for format before acceptance.
  • E-invoicing credentials configured where required under the currently approved E-Invoicing Applicability Configuration.
  • Document storage that is immutable after issue and searchable by order, invoice number and customer.

Trigger

An invoice is triggered by dispatch or delivery of an order or vendor group, whichever the currently approved Invoicing Configuration designates as the time of supply for that lane. A credit note is triggered by an approved cancellation after invoicing, an accepted return, a live plant claim settled in the customer's favour, or a confirmed billing error.

Step-by-Step Procedure

  1. On trigger, the system generates the document within {{gst_invoice_timeline}}, drawing supplier registration from the fulfilling location and place of supply from the delivery address.
  2. Select the document type using the matrix below. Do not issue a tax invoice for a supply mapped as exempt, and do not infer a rate from the category name — use only the HSN and Rate Master value.
  3. Where the order carries a validated customer GSTIN, issue as business-to-business with the recipient GSTIN and legal name; otherwise issue as business-to-consumer.
  4. Apply tax to shipping and handling in line with the treatment approved for the principal supply in that order.
  5. Where e-invoicing applies, report the document and obtain the IRN and QR code before it is shared with the customer; a document that fails reporting must not be sent until cleared or corrected.
  6. Deliver the document to the customer over the notification channels in use and attach it to the order record.
  7. For returns, cancellations after invoicing and settled live plant claims, raise a credit note referencing the original document number and date, for the returned lines only, and link it to the refund record before payment is released.
  8. For undercharges or corrections upward, raise a debit note against the original document with the reason recorded.
  9. Before each filing period closes, reconcile issued documents to the settlement records and confirm the series has no gaps, duplicates or cancelled-and-reused numbers.
  10. Escalate any classification doubt to the Finance Manager and tax advisor before further sales of that SKU.
SituationDocumentIssued
Taxable supply, consumerTax invoice, business-to-consumer{{gst_invoice_timeline}}
Taxable supply, GSTIN on orderTax invoice, business-to-business, with recipient GSTIN{{gst_invoice_timeline}}
Supply mapped exempt in the HSN and Rate MasterBill of supply{{gst_invoice_timeline}}
Return, cancellation after invoicing, settled claimCredit note against the original documentBefore refund release, per {{refund_processing_time}}
Undercharge or upward correctionDebit note against the original documentOn approval by the Finance Manager
Turnover conditions met per configurationAdditionally reported for IRN and QR codeBefore sharing with the customer

SLA

Invoice generation completes within {{gst_invoice_timeline}} of the trigger. Failed generations are worked the same working day. Credit notes are issued before the related refund is released and always within {{refund_processing_time}} of refund approval. Series continuity and document-to-settlement reconciliation are completed before each filing period closes. Classification queries are answered within {{support_response_sla}} internally.

Quality Checks

  • Invoice numbering is continuous per series with no gaps, reuse or manual overwrite.
  • Every dispatched order or vendor group has exactly one primary tax document; no order carries two.
  • Place of supply matches the delivery state on the order, and the tax head applied follows from it.
  • Each credit note references a real, unreversed original document and does not exceed its value.
  • Recipient GSTIN, where present, passes format validation and matches the recorded legal name.
  • No SKU is sellable without an HSN and Rate Master entry.

Exceptions

Manual documents are permitted only when automated generation is unavailable, and then only from the approved manual series with Finance Manager approval and same-day entry into the system once restored. Address or GSTIN corrections after issue are handled by credit note and fresh invoice, never by editing an issued document. E-invoice portal outages are logged with timestamps and the reporting is completed once service resumes; the outage record is retained as evidence.

Escalation Process

Generation failures escalate from Finance Executive to Engineering and the Finance Manager on {{escalation_timeline}}. Classification disagreements, applicability questions and any notice, audit query or portal rejection that cannot be cleared operationally are escalated to the Finance lead and the tax advisor immediately, with sales of the affected SKU suspended if a wrong rate may have been charged. A large-scale mis-issue is graded under {{incident_severity_model}}.

Records and Audit Trail

Retain issued invoices, bills of supply, credit and debit notes, IRN acknowledgements, the HSN and Rate Master with its change history, series registers, reconciliation workpapers and approvals for manual documents. Records are immutable after issue, stored against the order and in the finance repository, and retained for {{data_retention_period}} or the statutory retention period, whichever is longer. Every change to a rate mapping records who changed it, when and why. This procedure is reviewed at {{review_frequency_default}} and on any change in law, registration or platform behaviour.

title: Payment Reconciliation SOP
related_titles: Data Retention and Records Management Policy
html:
DRAFT — LEGAL REVIEW REQUIRED. This document is an operational or legal draft and must be reviewed and approved by authorized management and, where required, qualified legal counsel before becoming effective.

Purpose

This procedure defines the three-way reconciliation PlantAtHome, a brand of Silvestrix Green LLP, performs between its own order records, the payment gateway's records and the bank statement. Its object is to prove that every order marked paid was actually funded, that every rupee received belongs to a real order, and that failed, pending, refunded and disputed transactions are resolved rather than left to age.

Scope

Covers all customer money movements on the platform: prepaid captures through Razorpay, cash on delivery collected by hyperlocal riders and courier partners, refunds and partial refunds, store credit, chargebacks and disputes, and gateway fees and adjustments. Applies to every vertical and both fulfilment lanes, for direct and vendor-fulfilled orders. Excludes vendor payout computation and ledger posting, which are covered by the Order Settlement SOP, and refund eligibility decisions, which follow the Refund and Cancellation Policy.

Definitions

  • Three-way match — agreement between the order record, the gateway transaction and the bank credit or debit for the same money.
  • Successful payment — captured at the gateway and reflected as paid on the order.
  • Failed payment — declined or abandoned; no funds moved and no order obligation arises.
  • Pending payment — authorised but not captured, or a delayed instrument where the outcome is not yet known.
  • Chargeback — a payment reversed by the issuing bank on the cardholder's dispute, recovered from the merchant pending representment.
  • Exception — any item that fails the three-way match, in either direction.
  • Ageing — the elapsed time an exception has remained unresolved, used to drive escalation.

Roles and Responsibilities

  • Finance Executive — runs the reconciliation, classifies exceptions, chases owners, maintains the register.
  • Finance Manager — reviews ageing, approves write-offs and corrections within delegated limits, signs off each cycle.
  • Customer Support — supplies order context and contacts customers on stuck or duplicate payments.
  • Operations Manager — provides delivery proof and COD collection evidence for disputes.
  • Engineering on-call — investigates webhook loss, status drift between gateway and order, and duplicate transactions.
  • Finance lead — owns chargeback strategy and relations with the gateway and acquiring bank.

Prerequisites

  • Read access to gateway transaction, refund, dispute and settlement reports, and to the bank statement for the settlement account.
  • A daily automated export of orders with payment status, amount, currency, gateway reference and delivery status.
  • An exception register with owner, category, amount, ageing and resolution field.
  • Matching rules approved by the Finance Manager, including the tolerance defined in the currently approved Reconciliation Configuration.
  • Separation of duties: the person preparing the reconciliation cannot approve refunds or release payouts.

Trigger

The reconciliation runs on the cycle set in the currently approved Reconciliation Configuration, and additionally on receipt of a dispute or chargeback notification, on any gateway or webhook incident, and at period close before books are frozen.

Step-by-Step Procedure

  1. Pull the three sources for the period: order and payment export, gateway transaction and dispute reports, and the bank statement.
  2. Match automatically on gateway reference first, then on amount plus date within the approved tolerance. Never match on customer name or amount alone.
  3. Review successful payments: confirm each captured transaction has an order in a paid state and that the captured amount equals the order value less recorded discounts.
  4. Review failed payments: confirm no order was fulfilled against them and no inventory remains reserved; repeated failures for one customer are flagged to Support.
  5. Review pending payments: age them against the approved capture window, then capture, void, or refund per configuration. A pending payment must never be left to expire silently.
  6. Review refunds: each refund has an approval record, a linked credit note under the GST Invoicing SOP, one gateway refund entry and one deduction in a settlement report. Refunds not reflected at the gateway within {{refund_processing_time}} are escalated.
  7. Review chargebacks: log the dispute with its deadline the day it is received, assemble evidence — at minimum two independent proofs such as delivery confirmation and the delivery OTP or photograph — and submit representment before the network deadline. Never refund a transaction already under dispute.
  8. Classify every unmatched item using the exception matrix below and assign an owner the same working day.
  9. Post only approved corrections, then re-run the match to confirm the exception clears.
  10. Close the cycle with a signed summary: totals per source, matched value, open exceptions by ageing band, and the movement since the previous cycle.
ExceptionLikely causeOwnerResolution route
Order paid, no gateway recordStatus set incorrectly or manual overrideEngineeringCorrect order status; investigate override path
Gateway capture, no orderOrder creation failed after paymentSupport and EngineeringCreate or refund per {{refund_approval_sla}}
Duplicate capture, one orderCustomer retry or webhook replayFinanceRefund the duplicate within {{refund_processing_time}}
Refund at gateway, none on orderRefund raised outside processFinance ManagerInvestigate authorisation; correct records
Chargeback receivedCustomer dispute or fraudFinance leadRepresent with evidence before deadline
Bank credit, no payout recordAdjustment or non-order receiptFinanceIdentify source; do not release against it
COD short remittancePartner shortfall or lossOperationsRecover under the partner agreement

SLA

ItemTarget
Reconciliation cycleAs per the currently approved Reconciliation Configuration
Exception classification and owner assignmentSame working day as detection
Customer-affecting exception acknowledged{{support_response_sla}}
Customer-affecting exception resolved{{support_resolution_sla}}
Refund reflected at gateway{{refund_processing_time}}
Chargeback evidence submittedBefore the network deadline, never later
Ageing escalation{{escalation_timeline}}

Quality Checks

  • Matched value plus open exceptions equals total gateway value for the period, in each of the three sources.
  • No exception is closed without a stated cause and a supporting document reference.
  • No refund exists without an approval record, and no approval exists without a refund or a documented cancellation.
  • Duplicate gateway references never appear twice as matched.
  • Customers are never both refunded and charged back for the same transaction.
  • Ageing bands are recomputed each cycle; nothing is silently re-dated.

Exceptions

Amounts within the approved tolerance may be written off in aggregate with Finance Manager approval, provided the pattern is reviewed rather than repeatedly absorbed. Items older than the ageing threshold in the Reconciliation Configuration are provided for, but remain open until resolved or formally written off within {{approval_limit_expense}}. A suspected fraud, an unauthorised refund or evidence of internal misuse is removed from routine handling immediately and reported to the Finance lead and management.

Escalation Process

Open exceptions escalate on {{escalation_timeline}} from Finance Executive to Finance Manager, then to the Finance lead and management. Refund-related decisions require approval within {{approval_limit_refund}}. Gateway or bank-side failures — missing settlements, webhook loss, unexplained reversals — are raised with the provider the same day and graded under {{incident_severity_model}}; where customer money is affected, Support is briefed with agreed wording before customers are contacted.

Records and Audit Trail

Each cycle retains the three source extracts, the matching workpaper, the exception register snapshot, dispute evidence packs and submission confirmations, approvals for write-offs and corrections, and the signed cycle summary. Files are stored in the finance repository, are write-once after sign-off, and are retained for {{data_retention_period}}. Reconciliation exports must not contain full card numbers or other prohibited payment data; only masked identifiers and gateway references are stored. This procedure is reviewed at {{review_frequency_default}} and after any payment provider, bank or checkout change.

title: Internal Audit SOP
html:
DRAFT — LEGAL REVIEW REQUIRED. This document is an operational or legal draft and must be reviewed and approved by authorized management and, where required, qualified legal counsel before becoming effective.

Purpose

This SOP defines how PlantAtHome, a brand of Silvestrix Green LLP, plans, performs and closes internal audits of its e-commerce, fulfilment, vendor and finance operations. The objective is that control failures — a mispriced catalogue entry, an unissued GST invoice, a refund released without the required approval, a vendor dispatching outside agreed timelines — are found and corrected internally before they surface as a customer complaint, a vendor dispute or a regulatory query.

Scope

This SOP covers audits of: order capture, cancellation and refund handling; hyperlocal rider and pan-India courier fulfilment records; nursery vendor onboarding, order acceptance, dispatch and settlement; Razorpay payment capture and reconciliation; GST invoicing and tax registers; catalogue, pricing, city-availability and inventory accuracy; customer communications over WhatsApp Business API, email and SMS, including consent and opt-out records; and administrative access to the admin console, databases and media storage. It applies to employees and contractors, and to vendor records relating to PlantAtHome orders to the extent the executed vendor agreement permits inspection. Statutory audit and external assurance are outside this SOP; this SOP produces evidence that supports them.

Definitions

  • Audit Universe — the maintained list of auditable processes, systems and vendors, each carrying a risk rating derived under {{risk_scoring_model}}.
  • Engagement — a single audit with a defined scope, period under review, auditor and reporting date.
  • Control — a documented step, system rule or approval intended to prevent or detect a specific failure.
  • Evidence — a record that can be independently retrieved and identified, such as an order identifier, settlement reference, invoice number, message log entry or admin action log.
  • Sample — the set of records selected for testing under the method and size stated in the currently approved Internal Audit Configuration.
  • Finding — a tested control that did not operate as designed, stated with the control, the failure and the evidence.
  • Auditee — the process owner accountable for the area under review.
  • Corrective Action — the remediation raised against a finding and tracked to closure under the Corrective Action Process SOP.

Roles and Responsibilities

The Compliance Lead owns the audit plan and the audit universe, assigns auditors, approves severity ratings and signs the final report. The Auditor performs fieldwork and must be independent of the process audited; no person may audit work they perform, approve or manage. The Auditee provides access, confirms factual accuracy and proposes corrective actions with named owners. Functional Heads resolve disputes within their function and are accountable for their teams' overdue actions. Engineering provisions read-only data extracts and log access. The Designated Partners receive critical findings and approve any risk acceptance.

Prerequisites

  • An approved audit plan for the period, derived from the audit universe and the risk register.
  • Read-only access provisioned through role-based access control for the systems in scope, revoked at engagement close.
  • The current effective version of each policy, SOP and configuration governing the area under review.
  • The open corrective actions register and prior audit reports for the same area.
  • A restricted evidence workspace; personal data is extracted only where necessary and handled under the retention rules in the Data Retention and Privacy Policy.

Trigger

Planned engagements are scheduled at {{review_frequency_default}}, with high-risk areas reassessed at {{risk_review_frequency}}. Unplanned engagements are triggered by a material incident classified under {{incident_severity_model}}, a cluster of customer complaints on one theme, a vendor breaching {{vendor_return_rate_threshold}} or persistently missing {{vendor_quality_target}}, a regulatory or platform notice, a payment reconciliation break, or a request from the Designated Partners.

Step-by-Step Procedure

  1. Plan and scope. Define the process, period under review, systems, controls to be tested and the specific questions the engagement must answer. Record scope in the engagement record before fieldwork begins.
  2. Notify and open. Issue the engagement notice to the auditee and functional head and hold an opening discussion covering scope, access and timelines.
  3. Walk through. Map the process as actually performed against the documented SOP, and note where system behaviour and written procedure diverge.
  4. Select samples. Draw the sample using the method and size in the currently approved Internal Audit Configuration. Record the population, selection method and seed so the sample is reproducible.
  5. Gather evidence. Pull records directly from source systems rather than accepting prepared summaries. Save each item with its system identifier and retrieval date.
  6. Test. Test each control against its stated rule — for example, dispatch timestamps against {{vendor_dispatch_sla}}, delivery records against {{delivery_sla_hyperlocal}} or {{delivery_sla_courier}}, refund releases against {{refund_processing_time}} and {{approval_limit_refund}}, and invoice issuance against {{gst_invoice_timeline}}. Log every exception with its evidence reference.
  7. Validate facts. Share exceptions with the auditee for factual confirmation before rating them. Withdraw any exception shown to be an evidence-retrieval error.
  8. Classify severity. Rate each confirmed finding using the matrix below.
  9. Report and assign. Issue the draft report, obtain management responses, and raise a corrective action for every finding with a named owner and due date under the Corrective Action Process SOP.
  10. Follow up and close. Re-test the control after remediation; close the finding only on re-test evidence, never on assertion alone.
SeverityBasisNotificationRemediation timing
CriticalCustomer harm, statutory breach, fund loss or unauthorised data access, mapped through {{incident_severity_model}}Designated Partners, immediately on confirmationAs per the currently approved Internal Audit Configuration
HighControl absent or systematically bypassed across the sampleCompliance Lead and Functional HeadAs per the currently approved Internal Audit Configuration
MediumControl operates but fails on identifiable casesFunctional HeadAs per the currently approved Internal Audit Configuration
LowDocumentation, naming or record-keeping gap with no operational impactAuditeeAs per the currently approved Internal Audit Configuration

SLA

Engagement notice, draft report issuance, management response and final report dates follow the stage timings in the currently approved Internal Audit Configuration. Corrective action due dates are set by severity as shown above. Overdue actions are escalated per {{escalation_timeline}}. Critical findings are reported on confirmation and are not held for the report cycle.

Quality Checks

  • Independence is confirmed and recorded before fieldwork starts.
  • Every finding states the control, the failure mode and at least one retrievable evidence reference.
  • The sample is reproducible from the recorded population and method.
  • The auditee has confirmed factual accuracy, with any disagreement recorded rather than removed.
  • The Compliance Lead peer-reviews severity ratings for consistency across engagements.
  • Prior findings in the same area are re-tested rather than assumed closed.

Exceptions

If access is denied or records are unavailable, the auditor records a scope limitation in the report instead of omitting the area. If a vendor declines inspection permitted under its agreement, the matter is referred to the vendor relationship owner and may attract {{penalty_schedule}}. If an active incident is found mid-engagement, fieldwork on that item pauses and the matter transfers to incident response; the audit resumes once the incident is contained. Risk acceptance in place of remediation requires written approval from the Designated Partners and an entry in the risk register.

Escalation Process

Factual disputes escalate to the Functional Head. Severity disputes are decided by the Compliance Lead with the dissent recorded in the report. Overdue or repeatedly reopened corrective actions escalate per {{escalation_timeline}}. Critical findings, suspected fraud and any interference with evidence bypass the auditee and go directly to the Designated Partners.

Records and Audit Trail

Each engagement retains the scope note, sampling record, evidence set, exception log, auditee responses, final report and re-test evidence in the compliance module, linked to the corresponding corrective actions and risk register entries. Records are retained for {{data_retention_period}}, access is restricted to the compliance function and the Designated Partners, edits are versioned rather than overwritten, and the store is covered by the platform backup schedule at {{backup_frequency}}.

Related Documents

  • Risk Management Policy
  • Vendor Agreement
  • Data Retention and Privacy Policy
  • Information Security Policy

title: Corrective Action Process SOP
html:
DRAFT — LEGAL REVIEW REQUIRED. This document is an operational or legal draft and must be reviewed and approved by authorized management and, where required, qualified legal counsel before becoming effective.

Purpose

This SOP defines the single lifecycle PlantAtHome uses to take any confirmed control failure from discovery to verified closure: Finding, Assignment, Root Cause Analysis, Corrective Action, Verification, Closure. It exists so that a failure found once — a refund released outside approval limits, a vendor consistently missing dispatch timelines, a notification sent to a customer who had opted out — is fixed at its cause and does not reappear in the next audit cycle.

Scope

Every corrective action arising from an internal audit finding, an incident review, a repeated customer complaint pattern, a vendor performance breach, a payment or GST reconciliation break, a security or access review exception, or a regulatory or platform notice is tracked under this SOP. It covers actions owned by PlantAtHome teams and actions owned by nursery vendors where the finding relates to their fulfilment of PlantAtHome orders. Routine defect fixes with no control failure behind them are handled through normal engineering and operations workflows and are not tracked here.

Definitions

  • Corrective Action Record (CAR) — the tracked item created for one finding, holding owner, due date, status, root cause, action, evidence and links.
  • Root Cause — the condition which, if removed, would have prevented the failure; not the person who performed the step.
  • Containment — the immediate measure that stops ongoing harm while the root cause is still being established.
  • Corrective Action — the durable change to a control, system, configuration or procedure.
  • Verification — independent re-testing that the changed control now operates as intended.
  • Risk Register and Compliance Register — the system registers holding, respectively, rated risks and standing obligations; each CAR links to at least one entry in one of them.

Roles and Responsibilities

The Compliance Lead owns this process, raises CARs from findings, maintains the register and approves closure. The Action Owner is a named individual, never a team, accountable for analysis, remediation and evidence. The Verifier is independent of the Action Owner and re-tests the control. Functional Heads resolve resourcing conflicts and answer for overdue actions in their function. The Vendor Relationship Owner holds vendor-owned actions and applies {{penalty_schedule}} where warranted. The Designated Partners approve risk acceptance and closure without full remediation.

Prerequisites

  • A confirmed finding with its evidence reference and severity already assigned under the Internal Audit SOP or the applicable incident review.
  • Access to the corrective actions register in the compliance module.
  • The relevant risk register entry, or grounds to create one, and the compliance obligation the finding touches.
  • Access to the system, configuration or document that must change, or an identified owner who has it.

Trigger

A CAR is opened when a finding is confirmed and rated; when an incident review closes with a preventive commitment; when a vendor breaches {{vendor_return_rate_threshold}} or misses {{vendor_quality_target}}; when reconciliation, access review or complaint analysis identifies a control gap; or when a prior CAR is reopened because the failure recurred.

Step-by-Step Procedure

  1. Raise the finding. Create the CAR with the control, the failure, the evidence reference, the severity, and links to the risk register and compliance register entries. A CAR without a link to at least one register entry is not accepted.
  2. Contain. Where customers, funds or data are exposed, apply and record an immediate containment measure before analysis begins.
  3. Assign. The Compliance Lead names one Action Owner and sets the due date from severity, using the timing in the currently approved Corrective Action Configuration. Assignment is acknowledged by the owner in the register.
  4. Analyse the root cause. The owner establishes why the control failed, using the evidence and system logs, and records the causal chain. Analysis that ends at human error must continue to the missing check, unclear procedure or absent system constraint behind it.
  5. Define and implement the corrective action. State the change, the system or document affected, and how recurrence is prevented. Prefer an enforced system control or configuration change over a reminder or a training note; where only a procedural change is possible, record why.
  6. Verify. The Verifier re-tests the control on records created after the change and records the result. Verification failure returns the CAR to analysis with the reason logged.
  7. Close. The Compliance Lead closes the CAR on verification evidence, updates the linked risk register entry score under {{risk_scoring_model}}, and notes any residual risk.
StageStatusOwnerEvidence required to exitTiming
FindingOpenCompliance LeadConfirmed finding, severity, register linksOn confirmation
AssignmentAssignedCompliance LeadNamed owner and acknowledged due dateAs per the currently approved Corrective Action Configuration
Root Cause AnalysisIn AnalysisAction OwnerRecorded causal chain with supporting recordsAs per the currently approved Corrective Action Configuration
Corrective ActionIn ProgressAction OwnerChange implemented, with reference to the commit, configuration or document versionBy the severity-based due date
VerificationIn VerificationVerifierRe-test on post-change recordsAs per the currently approved Corrective Action Configuration
ClosureClosed or Closed — Risk AcceptedCompliance LeadVerification result and updated register entryOn verification

SLA

Due dates are derived from finding severity using the stage timings in the currently approved Corrective Action Configuration; critical findings are contained on confirmation rather than on the stage clock. A CAR past its due date is marked Overdue automatically and escalates per {{escalation_timeline}}. Register health is reviewed at {{review_frequency_default}}, and linked risks are re-scored at {{risk_review_frequency}}.

Quality Checks

  • Every CAR names one accountable individual and carries at least one risk or compliance register link.
  • The recorded root cause explains the failure without naming individual blame as the cause.
  • The corrective action is traceable to a specific system, configuration or document change.
  • Verification is performed by someone other than the Action Owner, on records created after the change.
  • Repeat findings in the same control are flagged and the earlier CAR is reviewed for premature closure.
  • No CAR is closed on assertion or on a training session alone.

Exceptions

Where remediation is not feasible or is disproportionate to the exposure, the Designated Partners may record a risk acceptance; the CAR closes as Closed — Risk Accepted, the risk register entry is updated with the residual rating and a review date, and the item is revisited at {{risk_review_frequency}}. Where the fix depends on a third party — a courier, payment gateway or messaging provider — the CAR remains open with an interim compensating control recorded. Vendor-owned actions not completed within the assigned window are handled under the vendor agreement and may attract {{penalty_schedule}}.

Escalation Process

Overdue CARs escalate first to the Functional Head, then per {{escalation_timeline}} to the Compliance Lead and the Designated Partners. Disputes over ownership are decided by the Compliance Lead. A CAR reopened after closure is escalated on reopening, since the original verification did not hold. Critical-severity CARs are reported to the Designated Partners at every stage transition.

Records and Audit Trail

The corrective actions register holds, for each CAR, the originating finding and evidence, owner, due date, status history with timestamps, root cause, implemented change, verification result, closure approval and links to the risk and compliance registers. Status changes are versioned rather than overwritten. Records are retained for {{data_retention_period}} and are produced as evidence in subsequent internal audits and external reviews.

Related Documents

  • Internal Audit SOP
  • Risk Management Policy
  • Incident Response SOP
  • Vendor Performance Management SOP
  • Data Retention and Privacy Policy

title: Compliance Review Framework
html:
DRAFT — LEGAL REVIEW REQUIRED. This document is an operational or legal draft and must be reviewed and approved by authorized management and, where required, qualified legal counsel before becoming effective.

Purpose

This framework defines how Silvestrix Green LLP, operating the PlantAtHome brand, identifies the regulatory obligations that apply to its e-commerce operations, assigns an accountable owner to each, and reviews each one on a documented cadence against real evidence. It exists so that compliance is a scheduled activity with an audit trail, rather than a reaction to a customer complaint or a departmental notice.

Scope

This framework covers every PlantAtHome business line — live plants, gardening tools, pots and planters, seeds, fertilizers, accessories, FarmBox fresh produce and corporate gifting — and every function that touches them: catalog and merchandising, storefront and mobile app, customer support, order fulfilment whether direct or by an approved nursery vendor, hyperlocal rider and pan-India courier delivery, payment processing, customer messaging over WhatsApp Business API, email and SMS, finance, human resources and engineering. It binds employees and contractors. Approved vendors are bound only to the extent obligations are passed through by their vendor agreement; this framework does not by itself create obligations on a vendor.

Definitions

  • Compliance Area — a grouping of related legal or contractual obligations reviewed as one unit under one accountable owner.
  • Control Owner — the named role accountable for the area, for producing evidence and for closing findings. Accountability is not delegable to a vendor or an external consultant.
  • Evidence — a dated artefact produced by normal operations (an invoice sample, an export of the refund register, a capture of a live listing, a vendor licence copy) showing whether a control actually worked in the period reviewed.
  • Configuration — the approved register of operational values (windows, turnaround times, thresholds, approval limits) that policy references instead of restating.
  • Finding — a recorded gap between the obligation and the evidence, carrying a severity, an owner and a target closure date.

Policy Statement

Every compliance area listed here has one named owner, a stated regulatory or contractual basis, a review cadence and a defined evidence expectation. Reviews test evidence drawn from live systems, not descriptions of intended process. Findings are recorded whether or not they are resolved during the review. Where an obligation depends on an operational value — a return window, a refund turnaround, a settlement cycle — the review tests actual performance against the currently approved Configuration.

This framework describes an internal control activity. It does not assert that PlantAtHome is in full compliance with any statute, and it does not substitute for advice from qualified counsel or a registered tax practitioner.

Responsibilities

  • Designated Partners, Silvestrix Green LLP — approve this framework and any exception; receive the open-findings summary each cycle.
  • Compliance Coordinator — maintains the compliance register, schedules reviews, collects evidence, records findings and tracks remediation. A coordination role that does not absorb the Control Owner's accountability.
  • Control Owners — as named in the table below.
  • Engineering Lead — provides system extracts and access records; implements configuration or code changes arising from findings.
  • All staff — report suspected non-compliance to the Compliance Coordinator without waiting for the next scheduled review.

Policy Requirements

The areas below are mandatory. Cadence is {{review_frequency_default}} unless the risk register rates the area elevated, in which case it moves to {{risk_review_frequency}}. No area may be marked reviewed without at least one dated evidence artefact attached.

Compliance AreaPrimary ReferenceControl OwnerCadenceEvidence Expected
Consumer protection and marketplace disclosuresConsumer Protection Act, 2019; Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020Head of Customer Experience{{review_frequency_default}}Listing sample showing seller identity, country of origin, total price and grievance officer details; grievance log tested against {{support_response_sla}} and {{support_resolution_sla}}

Evidence is retained for {{data_retention_period}}. Where an area depends on a third party — payment aggregator, courier partner, messaging provider — the review also confirms that the contract and platform policy currently in force are the versions operations are actually running against.

Procedures

  1. Schedule. The Compliance Coordinator opens the review in the register before its due date and confirms the obligation text is current against the regulatory change log.
  2. Collect. The Control Owner supplies the listed evidence for the period, exported from live systems.
  3. Test. Sampling covers both directly fulfilled and vendor-fulfilled orders, and both hyperlocal and courier delivery lanes, wherever the area touches fulfilment.
  4. Record. Each gap is logged as a finding with severity, owner and target date, including gaps fixed during the review.
  5. Remediate. Changes to an operational value are made in the Configuration, never by editing policy prose.
  6. Sign off. Control Owner and Compliance Coordinator sign the review; unresolved high-severity findings escalate to a Designated Partner within {{escalation_timeline}}.
  7. Retain. Evidence, findings and sign-off are filed together so a third party can reconstruct the review without asking the reviewer.

Exceptions

A review may be deferred, or an evidence expectation reduced, only with written approval from a Designated Partner recorded in the register with a reason and a fixed expiry. An exception may not be open-ended, may not be granted retrospectively to close a finding, and may not be granted for an obligation carrying a statutory deadline such as tax filing, invoice issue, data-subject response or grievance response. Vendor-specific relief is handled under the vendor agreement, not here.

Compliance

Adherence to this framework is itself reviewed at {{review_frequency_default}}. The Compliance Coordinator reports reviews due, completed and overdue, plus open findings by severity and age, to the Designated Partners, naming overdue reviews and expired exceptions by owner. The register and its evidence may be produced to statutory auditors, retained counsel or platform partners on request.

Violations

Failure to complete an assigned review, to produce evidence, or to close an accepted finding by its target date is a performance matter under the applicable HR process and is escalated to the Designated Partners. Falsifying or backdating evidence, or marking a review complete without testing, is treated as serious misconduct. Where a vendor's conduct causes the breach, the vendor agreement's performance terms and {{penalty_schedule}} apply.
