title: Regulatory Change Management
html:
DRAFT — LEGAL REVIEW REQUIRED. This document is an operational or legal draft and must be reviewed and approved by authorized management and, where required, qualified legal counsel before becoming effective.

Purpose

This policy defines how PlantAtHome, a brand of Silvestrix Green LLP, learns that a law, rule, regulator direction, platform policy or partner contract term has changed; decides whether the change affects the business; and gets the change into documents, configuration and systems before it takes effect. It exists because most of the obligations PlantAtHome operates under are amended by notification rather than by announcement, and a change nobody noticed is indistinguishable from a change nobody made.

Scope

Applies to changes affecting any PlantAtHome business line — live plants, gardening tools, pots and planters, seeds, fertilizers, accessories, FarmBox fresh produce and corporate gifting — across consumer protection and e-commerce rules, GST and tax administration, Legal Metrology declarations, food safety, agri-input licensing, personal data protection, payment processing, commercial communication, employment, and the terms of courier, hyperlocal delivery, payment and messaging partners. It applies to all employees and contractors, and to vendor-facing requirements that PlantAtHome must pass down through vendor agreements.

Definitions

  • Regulatory Change — any amendment, new rule, circular, clarification, court or regulator direction, or partner policy revision that alters an obligation PlantAtHome already carries or creates a new one.
  • Source — a named, checkable publication or channel from which changes are read.
  • Impact Assessment — the written analysis of what a change requires: which obligations move, which documents and Configuration values change, which system work is needed, and by when.
  • Effective Date — the date from which the changed obligation binds, which may precede the date PlantAtHome learned of it.
  • Change Owner — the person accountable for delivering the assessed changes by the effective date.

Policy Statement

Monitoring under this policy is a manual process. Named people read named sources on a schedule and record what they found. PlantAtHome does not operate an automated regulatory feed, alerting service, or subscription that guarantees notification of a change, and nothing in this policy should be read as automated detection. The controls that make manual monitoring reliable are therefore the schedule, the named owner, and the requirement to log a dated check even when nothing changed — an absent log entry means the check did not happen, not that nothing was published.

Every identified change is assessed, assigned and verified. A change is not closed because a document was edited; it is closed when the behaviour in the live systems and the operational Configuration match the new obligation, and the evidence of that is on file.

Responsibilities

  • Designated Partners — approve material changes, approve engaging external counsel, and decide when a change requires suspending a product line, a delivery lane or a payment method.
  • Compliance Coordinator — owns the change log, confirms each scheduled source check happened, drives triage, and tracks each change to verified closure.
  • Source Owners — as named in the table below; perform the check and log the result.
  • Change Owners — deliver the assessed document, configuration and system changes by the effective date.
  • Engineering Lead — implements system and Configuration changes and confirms the deployed behaviour.
  • Vendor Manager — passes vendor-affecting changes into vendor communications and, where needed, agreement amendments.

Policy Requirements

Each source below is checked manually on the stated cadence, and every check is logged with the date, the person and the outcome, including a nil outcome.

SourceWhat It CoversSource OwnerCheck Cadence
Gazette of India and Ministry of Consumer Affairs notificationsConsumer protection, e-commerce rules, marketplace disclosure dutiesCompliance Coordinator{{review_frequency_default}}
CBIC notifications, circulars and GST portal advisoriesRates, HSN classification, invoicing and e-invoicing, return formatsFinance Controller{{review_frequency_default}}
Legal Metrology department circulars and state notificationsPre-packaged commodity declarations for pots, seeds, fertilizers, FarmBoxHead of Catalog{{review_frequency_default}}
MeitY notifications and rules issued under the data protection statuteNotice and consent, breach reporting, data principal rightsData Protection Point of Contact{{review_frequency_default}}
FSSAI orders and licensing advisoriesFarmBox fresh produce handling, labelling and licensingFarmBox Category Lead{{review_frequency_default}}
Seed, fertilizer and insecticide licensing notificationsAgri-input listing eligibility and restricted itemsHead of Catalog{{risk_review_frequency}}
Payment aggregator directions and Razorpay policy or integration noticesPayment collection, refunds, settlement, data handlingFinance Controller{{review_frequency_default}}
Commercial communication regulations and WhatsApp Business Messaging PolicyConsent, template categories, opt-out handling across {{support_channels}}Growth Lead{{review_frequency_default}}
Courier and hyperlocal partner terms and API changelogsProhibited items, liability, labelling, delivery attempt handlingHead of Logistics{{review_frequency_default}}
Retained counsel and statutory auditor advisoriesCross-cutting changes and interpretation of ambiguous notificationsCompliance Coordinator{{review_frequency_default}}

Triage severity, assessment turnaround and escalation thresholds follow the currently approved Regulatory Change Configuration; unresolved items escalate to a Designated Partner within {{escalation_timeline}}. Change records are retained for {{data_retention_period}}.

Procedures

  1. Monitor. The Source Owner reads the source and logs the check, attaching the notification text or a stable reference to it.
  2. Identify. The Compliance Coordinator triages each item as not applicable, informational, or actionable, with a one-line reason. Not-applicable items stay in the log; they are the record of why nothing was done.
  3. Assess impact. The assessment names the affected obligations, the documents needing amendment, the Configuration values needing change, the storefront, admin or vendor-facing system work required, the vendor or customer communication needed, the effective date, and whether counsel must be engaged.
  4. Assign. A Designated Partner or the Compliance Coordinator names a Change Owner and a target date set against the effective date, not against convenience.
  5. Update documents. Policies, standards and templates are amended and re-approved. Operational figures move in the Configuration; policy text continues to reference them.
  6. Implement. System, catalog, invoicing, messaging or vendor-agreement changes are made and released. Where a change cannot be delivered by the effective date, the affected listing, lane or method is restricted until it can be.
  7. Verify. The Compliance Coordinator confirms in the live system that the new behaviour is present — a re-issued invoice, an amended listing, a changed consent flow — and files the evidence against the change record.
  8. Document. The record is closed with the source, assessment, decisions, owner, dates and verification evidence attached, and feeds the next cycle of the Compliance Review Framework.

Exceptions

A scheduled source check may be skipped, or an implementation target extended, only with written approval from a Designated Partner recorded against the change with a reason and a fixed expiry. No exception may push implementation past a statutory effective date; where the date cannot be met, the correct response is to restrict the affected activity and record that decision, not to grant an exception.

Compliance

At {{review_frequency_default}} the Compliance Coordinator reports to the Designated Partners: source checks due versus logged, open changes by severity and age, changes approaching or past their effective date, and changes closed without verification evidence. Because monitoring is manual, a missing check log is itself reported as a control failure.

Violations

Failing to perform or log an assigned source check, closing a change without verification, or implementing a change without updating the affected documents is a performance matter under the applicable HR process and is escalated to the Designated Partners. Recording a check that was not performed is treated as serious misconduct. Where a vendor fails to adopt a passed-down regulatory requirement by its effective date, the vendor agreement's performance terms and {{penalty_schedule}} apply, and listings may be suspended pending compliance.

title: Live Plant Inspection Checklist SOP
related_titles: Live Plant Packaging and Dispatch Standard
Order Fulfilment and Vendor Dispatch SOP
html:
DRAFT — LEGAL REVIEW REQUIRED. This document is an operational or legal draft and must be reviewed and approved by authorized management and, where required, qualified legal counsel before becoming effective.

Purpose

To define the mandatory pre-dispatch inspection every live plant must pass before PlantAtHome (Silvestrix Green LLP) or an approved nursery vendor hands it to a hyperlocal rider or a courier partner. The inspection establishes a dated, photographed record of plant condition at the moment custody changes, so that later damage, wilt or mortality claims can be assessed against evidence rather than assertion.

Scope

Applies to every live plant line item — single plants, buy-with-pot combinations, plant components of bundles and corporate gifting lots — dispatched from a PlantAtHome fulfilment point or from a vendor nursery, on both the hyperlocal and pan-India courier lanes. Non-living SKUs (pots and planters, tools, seeds, fertilizers, accessories) are covered by the general packing check and are out of scope. FarmBox fresh produce follows its own perishables procedure.

Definitions

  • Inspector — the trained fulfilment associate or vendor staff member who performs and signs the checklist. The Inspector may not be the person who packed the item where staffing allows separation.
  • PASS — the check meets the standard in the currently approved Live Plant Grading Configuration.
  • FAIL — the check is below standard; the plant cannot be dispatched against this order.
  • CONDITIONAL — a cosmetic or recoverable deviation that does not affect plant viability and may be released only under an authorised override.
  • Authorised Override — a documented release of a CONDITIONAL item by a role holding that authority under the approval matrix.
  • Evidence Pack — the checklist record plus photographs attached to the order line and shipment.

Roles and Responsibilities

  • Packer (own or vendor) — stages the plant, completes remediation on returned items, re-presents for inspection.
  • Inspector — runs every check, records outcomes honestly, captures photographs, marks the overall outcome.
  • Dispatch Supervisor — reviews CONDITIONAL items, grants or refuses overrides, releases the lot to the rider or courier.
  • Category / Quality Lead — owns the grading configuration, audits samples, rules on disputed FAILs.
  • Vendor Operations — tracks vendor-level failure trends and applies the agreed consequence framework.
  • Customer Support — retrieves the Evidence Pack when a claim is raised.

Prerequisites

  • Order line allocated to a vendor or fulfilment group and picked to the inspection bay.
  • Device logged into the admin or vendor app with camera access, so photographs attach to the order line rather than a personal gallery.
  • Current Live Plant Grading Configuration visible at the bay, with the reference images for each check.
  • Approved packaging materials, sleeves, moisture barrier and care card in stock.
  • A physically separated Hold Bay for FAIL and pending-CONDITIONAL items.

Trigger

Inspection is triggered when a live plant line item reaches packing stage inside the vendor dispatch window, and again on any of the following: re-presentation after remediation of a failed check, re-listing of a plant returned on a delivery attempt, or a plant held past its planned dispatch date in a staging area.

Step-by-Step Procedure

  1. Scan the order line and confirm the SKU, variant and quantity match the pick.
  2. Stage the plant in the inspection bay in adequate light; remove sleeves so foliage and stem are fully visible.
  3. Work the checks below in order. Record PASS, FAIL or CONDITIONAL for each — never leave a row blank, and never back-fill after dispatch.
  4. Photograph the whole plant, the root zone or drainage holes, and any defect that drove a CONDITIONAL or FAIL.
  5. Apply the overall outcome rule: any FAIL makes the line FAIL; one or more CONDITIONAL with no FAIL makes the line CONDITIONAL; all PASS makes the line PASS.
  6. Route the outcome — PASS proceeds to sealing; CONDITIONAL goes to the Dispatch Supervisor for override or refusal; FAIL goes to the Hold Bay and the line is re-allocated or the customer is offered a substitution or cancellation.
  7. Seal, apply the shipping label and orientation marking, and hand over to the rider or courier only after the outcome is saved.
  8. Save the Evidence Pack against the order and shipment before the handover scan is closed.
CheckWhat good looks likeOutcome
Healthy foliageColour, turgidity and leaf count within the grading configuration for the SKU; no widespread yellowing, browning, scorch or leaf drop; trimmed tips acceptable within the configured tolerancePASS / FAIL / CONDITIONAL
Healthy rootsFirm, light-coloured roots holding the root ball; no mush, sour smell or heavy circling beyond the configured tolerance; plant sits stable when lifted by the stem basePASS / FAIL / CONDITIONAL
Soil / media conditionMedia level, texture and volume as specified for the pot size; no compaction, crusting, algae or weed growth; media retained by the collarPASS / FAIL / CONDITIONAL
MoistureMoisture band as per the currently approved Live Plant Grading Configuration for the SKU and dispatch lane; not waterlogged, no free water in the sleeve, not bone dryPASS / FAIL / CONDITIONAL
PestsNo live insects, webbing, egg masses, scale, honeydew or ant activity on leaf faces, undersides, stem joints or media surfacePASS / FAIL
DiseaseNo leaf spot, mildew, rot, canker or unexplained collapse; no lesion spread since the last inspection of the batchPASS / FAIL
Structural integrityStem, primary branches, graft union and pot intact; no cracks, chips or wobble; stake and tie secure; plant self-supporting for the lane it will travelPASS / FAIL / CONDITIONAL
LabellingCorrect SKU and variant tag, botanical and common name, care card present and legible, order label matching the shipment recordPASS / FAIL / CONDITIONAL
PackagingMedia secured against spill, foliage sleeved without crushing, pot immobilised, orientation and fragile marking applied to the standard for the assigned lanePASS / FAIL / CONDITIONAL

Override path. Only a Dispatch Supervisor or a higher role named in the approval matrix may release a CONDITIONAL line. Pest and disease checks are never overridable. The override record must capture the check name, the reason for release, the mitigation applied, the supporting photograph and the identity of the approver; an override without all five is invalid and the line reverts to Hold.

SLA

ActivityTarget
Inspection completed after pickingWithin {{vendor_dispatch_sla}}
Supervisor decision on a CONDITIONAL lineAs per the currently approved Dispatch Escalation Configuration
Re-allocation or customer contact after a FAIL{{support_response_sla}}
Handover to rider or courier after PASSWithin the window that preserves {{delivery_sla_hyperlocal}} or {{delivery_sla_courier}} for the assigned lane

Quality Checks

The Category / Quality Lead re-inspects a sample of dispatched lines at {{review_frequency_default}} and compares findings against the recorded outcomes. Divergence between recorded and audited outcomes is treated as an inspection integrity issue, not a plant issue. Vendor-level dispatch quality is measured against {{vendor_quality_target}}, and live plant claim volume against {{vendor_return_rate_threshold}}; sustained breach triggers {{penalty_schedule}} under the vendor agreement.

Exceptions

  • SKUs sold deliberately bare-root, as plugs, as bulbs or in seasonal dormancy are graded against their own configuration rows; foliage and moisture checks are marked not applicable rather than FAIL.
  • Corporate gifting lots are inspected per unit but recorded per lot, with a defect log naming each affected unit.
  • Where a customer has accepted a disclosed cosmetic defect at the time of order, the corresponding check may be recorded CONDITIONAL with the acceptance referenced; viability checks still apply in full.
  • No exception permits dispatch of a plant failing the pest or disease check.

Escalation Process

  1. Inspector to Dispatch Supervisor for any CONDITIONAL line or a disputed FAIL.
  2. Dispatch Supervisor to Category / Quality Lead where a defect pattern spans a batch, or where the grading configuration does not describe the observed condition.
  3. Category / Quality Lead to Vendor Operations where a vendor's failures are systemic rather than incidental.
  4. Unresolved matters follow {{escalation_timeline}}. Any suspected falsification of an inspection record is escalated immediately to management and does not wait on the tiers above.

Records and Audit Trail

Each inspection produces an Evidence Pack — per-check outcomes, photographs, Inspector identity, timestamp, and any override with its approver and reason — stored against the order line and shipment, and retained for {{data_retention_period}}. The pack is the primary evidence when a customer raises a live plant claim within {{live_plant_claim_window}} or submits replacement evidence within {{replacement_evidence_window}}, and is disclosed to the vendor when a claim is charged back. Records are append-only; a correction is logged as a new entry citing the original, never as an edit.

Related Documents

  • Live Plant Packaging and Dispatch Standard
  • Returns, Replacement and Refund Policy
  • Vendor Quality and Performance Agreement
  • Order Fulfilment and Vendor Dispatch SOP

title: Refund Approval Policy
html:
DRAFT — LEGAL REVIEW REQUIRED. This document is an operational or legal draft and must be reviewed and approved by authorized management and, where required, qualified legal counsel before becoming effective.

Purpose

This policy defines who may approve a customer refund at PlantAtHome, a brand of Silvestrix Green LLP, what evidence must exist before that approval, and how fast a decision must be reached. It exists so that money leaves the business only on a named, documented and authorised decision, and so a customer receives the same answer whichever agent, city or nursery vendor is involved.

Scope

All refunds against customer orders on the PlantAtHome website and apps, across every category: live plants, gardening tools, pots and planters, seeds, fertilizers, accessories, FarmBox fresh produce and corporate gifting. It covers prepaid Razorpay reversals, refunds of prepaid amounts on cancelled COD-adjacent orders, store credit, partial and shipping-only refunds, and goodwill refunds initiated by PlantAtHome after a service failure. It applies equally to directly fulfilled and vendor-fulfilled orders, and to hyperlocal rider and pan-India courier deliveries. Cancellations raised inside {{cancellation_window}} where no payment has been captured are handled under the Order Cancellation Policy and enter this policy only once funds have been captured.

Definitions

  • Refund Band — a value range that determines the minimum approval level, held in the Refund Approval Configuration and driven by {{approval_limit_refund}}.
  • Evidence Pack — the record set attached to the refund request in the admin system before a decision is taken.
  • Goodwill Refund — a refund granted where no policy entitlement exists, for service recovery.
  • Vendor-Recoverable Refund — a refund whose cost is chargeable to a nursery vendor under the Vendor Agreement.
  • Refund Instrument — the destination of the money: original payment method, bank or UPI credit, or store credit.

Policy Statement

PlantAtHome refunds a customer when the claim is valid under the Returns and Refunds Policy, or when PlantAtHome has failed the customer. Every refund carries a named approver, a reason code and an evidence pack. Approval authority is banded by refund value and is configuration-driven, never hardcoded into tooling or improvised in chat. No person approves a refund they themselves raised, and no person approves a refund on an order in which they hold a personal or vendor interest. Refunds are issued to the original payment instrument by default; store credit may be offered but is never imposed where the customer is entitled to money back.

Responsibilities

  • Support Agent — collects the evidence pack, applies the correct reason code, decides within the routine band.
  • Support Lead — reviews supervised-band requests and all disputed or repeat-claim cases.
  • Finance — validates payment capture and settlement status, releases the payout, and books vendor recovery.
  • Vendor Operations — confirms fault attribution for vendor-fulfilled lines.
  • Head of Operations and the Designated Partner — approve high-value, bulk and corporate gifting refunds and own the configuration values.

Policy Requirements

BandRefund value rangeRequired approval levelEscalation or second checkDecision SLA
Band 1 — routineUp to the Band 1 ceiling in {{approval_limit_refund}}Support AgentAuto-routes to Support Lead if the evidence pack is incomplete{{refund_approval_sla}}
Band 2 — supervisedAbove Band 1, up to the Band 2 ceiling in {{approval_limit_refund}}Support LeadFinance verification before payout release{{refund_approval_sla}}
Band 3 — financeAbove Band 2, up to the Band 3 ceiling in {{approval_limit_refund}}Finance ManagerHead of Operations countersigns vendor-recoverable claimsas per the currently approved Refund Approval Configuration
Band 4 — partnerAbove the Band 3 ceiling in {{approval_limit_refund}}; all bulk and corporate gifting refundsDesignated Partner, Silvestrix Green LLPFinance prepares the file; no delegation permittedas per the currently approved Refund Approval Configuration

Minimum evidence by claim type: damaged or dead-on-arrival plant — dated photographs of the plant and of the outer packaging, raised inside {{live_plant_claim_window}}; wrong or missing item — unboxing evidence plus the picking record; non-delivery — carrier or rider status and the delivery attempt trail against {{delivery_attempts}}; quality complaint after establishment — customer account of care plus photographs, assessed against the plant care guidance issued at dispatch. Return-linked refunds require a return request inside {{return_request_window}} and a scan or rider acknowledgement of the returned goods, except where the item is non-returnable for hygiene or perishability reasons. Approved refunds are released within {{refund_processing_time}}.

Procedures

  1. The customer raises a claim through any of {{support_channels}}; the agent creates the refund request against the order and its specific lines.
  2. The agent attaches the evidence pack, selects a reason code and fault owner (PlantAtHome, vendor, carrier or customer), and the system computes the refundable value including or excluding shipping.
  3. The system assigns the band from the configuration and routes the request to the lowest sufficient approver.
  4. The approver decides within the applicable SLA, recording either approval or a written reason for rejection.
  5. Finance confirms that payment was captured and not already reversed, then triggers the refund to the refund instrument.
  6. Vendor-recoverable amounts are posted to the vendor ledger for netting in the next settlement cycle.
  7. The customer is notified over WhatsApp, email or SMS with the approved amount, instrument and expected credit timeline.

Exceptions

Refunds outside the stated claim windows, refunds exceeding the value paid, refunds to an instrument other than the original, and refunds on orders flagged for suspected abuse require Finance Manager approval with a written justification. Repeat claimants identified by the fraud review may be moved to evidence-first handling. Court orders, consumer forum directions and regulator instructions are executed on legal advice and recorded as exceptions.

Compliance

Every refund decision, band assignment and configuration change is written to the audit log described in the Financial Audit Log Policy. Finance samples approved refunds at {{review_frequency_default}} to test band adherence, evidence quality and fault attribution. The policy is intended to support PlantAtHome's obligations under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019 and the Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020; it does not replace legal advice on any individual dispute.

Violations

Approving outside band, approving one's own request, sharing approver credentials, issuing a refund without an evidence pack, or splitting a refund into smaller amounts to stay inside a lower band are treated as control breaches. They are investigated by Finance with Human Resources and may lead to withdrawal of approval rights, disciplinary action and recovery of loss. Deliberate collusion with a customer or vendor is treated as fraud and may be reported to law enforcement.

Related Documents

  • Returns and Refunds Policy
  • Order Cancellation Policy
  • Vendor Settlement Policy — Finance View
  • Commission Calculation Policy
  • Financial Audit Log Policy
  • Customer Support Escalation SOP

title: Vendor Settlement Controls
html:
DRAFT — LEGAL REVIEW REQUIRED. This document is an operational or legal draft and must be reviewed and approved by authorized management and, where required, qualified legal counsel before becoming effective.

Purpose

This policy sets out how PlantAtHome Finance computes, verifies, approves and pays amounts due to approved nursery and supply vendors, and how vendors challenge a figure they believe is wrong. It is the Finance-side companion to the commercial terms in the Vendor Agreement, written so that a settlement can be reproduced line by line from system records months later.

Scope

All vendors fulfilling customer orders for Silvestrix Green LLP under the PlantAtHome brand: live plant nurseries, pot and planter suppliers, tool and accessory sellers, seed and fertilizer suppliers, FarmBox produce suppliers and corporate gifting fulfilment partners. It covers vendor-shipped courier lines and vendor-handover lines collected by hyperlocal riders. It does not cover employee reimbursements, marketing spend or non-inventory procurement, which follow the Procurement and Expense Approval Policy.

Definitions

  • Settlement Cycle — the recurring period on which payables are cut off, computed and paid, defined by {{vendor_settlement_cycle}}.
  • Eligible Line — an order line that has been delivered, has passed its claim window, and is not under hold or dispute.
  • Settlement Statement — the itemised statement issued to the vendor showing gross value, every deduction and the net payable.
  • Hold — a block preventing payout of otherwise eligible value, applied for compliance, quality or recovery reasons.
  • Recovery — value charged back to a vendor for refunds, replacements or penalties attributable to that vendor.

Policy Statement

Vendors are paid on the published cycle, for delivered and claim-cleared value only, net of contractually defined deductions, against a statement the vendor can reconcile independently. Finance does not pay on an undelivered order, does not pay twice on the same line, and does not adjust a settlement outside the ledger. Every deduction traces to a policy, a configuration value or a documented incident. Vendor bank and GST details are changed only through the verified change procedure, never on the basis of an email or message alone.

Responsibilities

  • Finance Executive — runs the cycle, reconciles gateway and courier data, prepares statements.
  • Finance Manager — reviews holds and recoveries, approves the payout file, owns tax deduction correctness.
  • Vendor Operations — validates fault attribution, quality penalties and performance-linked deductions.
  • Head of Operations — approves exceptional releases, write-offs and out-of-cycle payments.
  • Vendor — maintains accurate bank, PAN and GST records, issues tax invoices, raises disputes inside the dispute window.

Policy Requirements

ComponentEffect on net payableSource of truthGoverning reference
Gross value of eligible delivered linesAddOrder and delivery records in the admin systemEligibility rules below
Platform commissionDeductCommission engine output{{commission_model}}, per the Commission Calculation Policy
Shipping and rider cost recovery where borne by PlantAtHome for a vendor-caused re-dispatchDeductCourier and rider invoicesas per the currently approved Vendor Settlement Configuration
Customer refunds and replacements attributed to the vendorDeductRefund ledgerRefund Approval Policy
Quality, dispatch and cancellation penaltiesDeductVendor performance records{{penalty_schedule}}, {{vendor_dispatch_sla}}, {{vendor_acceptance_sla}}
Statutory tax deductions and collectionsDeductTax computation on the settlement runIncome-tax Act, 1961 and Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017
Prior-cycle corrections and upheld dispute creditsAdd or deductVendor ledger adjustmentsDispute outcome record

A line becomes eligible only after delivery is confirmed and the applicable customer claim window has closed: {{return_request_window}} for goods generally and {{live_plant_claim_window}} for live plants and FarmBox produce. Value is held, not forfeited, where vendor KYC is incomplete, where bank or GST details fail verification, where the Vendor Agreement is unsigned, where the vendor's return rate exceeds {{vendor_return_rate_threshold}}, or where an open investigation covers the line. Negative net payable carries forward to the next cycle and is recovered from future value before any cash demand is made.

Procedures

  1. Finance closes the cycle per {{vendor_settlement_cycle}} and freezes the eligible line set.
  2. Razorpay settlement data, COD remittances and courier invoices are reconciled against order records; unmatched items are parked, not netted arbitrarily.
  3. The commission engine and the vendor ledger produce deductions; Vendor Operations confirms attributed refunds and penalties.
  4. Finance applies statutory deductions and generates the settlement statement and payout file.
  5. The Finance Manager approves the file; payment is released to the verified vendor bank account only.
  6. Statements are published to the vendor console and notified by email and WhatsApp with the cycle reference.
  7. Vendor tax invoices and PlantAtHome commission invoices are exchanged in line with {{gst_invoice_timeline}}.

Exceptions

Out-of-cycle or advance payments, release of held value before the underlying issue closes, waiver of a penalty, and settlement to an account newly added require Finance Manager approval, and Head of Operations approval where the amount exceeds {{approval_limit_expense}}. Vendors under exit or termination are settled only after open claims, in-transit returns and outstanding recoveries are closed.

Compliance

Disputes must be raised on the specific statement line within {{vendor_settlement_dispute_window}}; Finance acknowledges, investigates and responds within the period set in the approved Vendor Settlement Configuration, and unresolved disputes escalate per {{escalation_timeline}}. Statements, payout files, approvals, invoices and dispute outcomes are retained for {{data_retention_period}} and logged per the Financial Audit Log Policy. Finance reviews holds, ageing payables and unmatched reconciliation items at {{review_frequency_default}}.

Violations

Releasing a payout without approval, altering a settlement outside the ledger, changing vendor bank details without verification, or suppressing a valid recovery are control breaches. They are investigated by Finance with Human Resources and may lead to removal of system access, disciplinary action and recovery of loss. Vendor-side misconduct, including invoicing for undelivered goods, is handled under the Vendor Agreement and may lead to suspension, forfeiture of held value and legal action.

title: Commission Calculation Policy
html:
DRAFT — LEGAL REVIEW REQUIRED. This document is an operational or legal draft and must be reviewed and approved by authorized management and, where required, qualified legal counsel before becoming effective.

Purpose

This policy defines how PlantAtHome calculates the commission it earns on vendor-fulfilled sales: which models exist, how the commission base is built, how discounts, returns and taxes affect it, and who may change a rate. It exists so that a vendor, an auditor and Finance can all arrive at the same number from the same order record.

Scope

All commission earned by Silvestrix Green LLP on orders fulfilled by approved vendors across live plants, gardening tools, pots and planters, seeds, fertilizers, accessories, FarmBox fresh produce and corporate gifting. It applies to hyperlocal and courier fulfilment alike. Commission on directly owned inventory does not arise and is out of scope; margin on owned stock is governed by the Pricing and Discount Approval Policy.

Definitions

  • Commission Base — the value on which the commission rate or rule is applied, after the adjustments set out below.
  • Platform-Funded Discount — a reduction to the customer price borne by PlantAtHome.
  • Vendor-Funded Discount — a reduction agreed with and borne by the vendor.
  • Rate Card — the approved set of commission rules by model, category and vendor, held in the Commission Configuration.
  • Reversal — commission withdrawn when the underlying sale is cancelled, returned or refunded.

Policy Statement

Commission is earned on completed sales, computed from the configured rate card only, and reversed in full whenever the sale is undone. Rates are configuration-driven and versioned; the rate in force at the moment of order placement governs that order, so a later rate change never re-prices historic settlements. Commission is calculated on the taxable value of goods, never on the tax collected, and never on amounts PlantAtHome itself funded as a discount. No rate is applied to a vendor who has not been shown that rate in writing.

Responsibilities

  • Category Management — proposes category and vendor-specific rates with commercial justification.
  • Finance Manager — validates the economics, approves the rate card and owns tax treatment.
  • Head of Operations — approves vendor-specific deviations from the category default.
  • Engineering — implements the configured models without hardcoded rates and preserves rate versioning.
  • Finance Executive — reconciles engine output to settlements each cycle and raises variances.

Policy Requirements

ModelHow it computesTypical useConfigured by
PercentageRate applied to the commission baseGeneral catalogue lines with stable unit economics{{commission_model}}, percentage rule in the Commission Configuration
Fixed feeFlat amount per eligible line or per shipmentLow-value, high-volume items such as seeds and small accessoriesas per the currently approved Commission Configuration
Category-basedRate resolved from the product category, with the nearest configured ancestor applying where a leaf has no ruleDifferentiated handling for live plants, pots, tools and fertilizersCategory rate card in the Commission Configuration
Vendor-specificVendor override that takes precedence over the category rule for that vendor onlyNegotiated terms, exclusive supply, corporate gifting partnersVendor record, approved per {{commission_model}}

Resolution order is strict: vendor-specific override, then category rule, then the platform default; a fixed fee and a percentage combine only where the rate card explicitly defines both for the same line.

Worked example using placeholders

StepComputation
Price charged to the customer for the line, inclusive of taxP
Remove the tax component T at the applicable HSN rateTaxable value V = P minus T
Add back any platform-funded discount Dp, which does not reduce the baseV plus Dp
Deduct any vendor-funded discount Dv, which does reduce the baseCommission Base B = V plus Dp minus Dv
Apply the resolved ruleCommission C = B multiplied by the rate resolved from {{commission_model}}, or the configured fixed fee
Add tax on the commission serviceC plus GST on C, invoiced by PlantAtHome to the vendor
Carry to settlementC and its tax are deducted per the Vendor Settlement Policy — Finance View

Procedures

  1. Category Management submits a rate proposal with volume, return rate and margin impact.
  2. Finance models the effect on contribution and confirms tax treatment; the Finance Manager approves, and the Head of Operations approves vendor-specific overrides.
  3. The approved rate is entered in the Commission Configuration with an effective-from timestamp; the prior version is retained.
  4. Vendors are notified in writing before an increased rate takes effect, with the notice period stated in the Vendor Agreement.
  5. The commission engine stamps the resolved rule and computed commission onto each order line at placement.
  6. On cancellation, return or refund, commission is reversed in proportion to the value undone; a partial refund reverses commission on the refunded portion only, and shipping-only refunds do not affect commission.
  7. Finance reconciles engine output against settlement statements every cycle and investigates any line where the stamped rule differs from the current rate card.

Exceptions

Zero-commission or promotional-rate periods, launch waivers for new vendors, and bespoke corporate gifting arrangements require Finance Manager approval and a written vendor communication, and are entered as time-bounded configuration rather than manual adjustments. Retrospective rate changes are not permitted; a correction to a past cycle is processed as a documented ledger adjustment, not by editing history.

Compliance

Rate card versions, approvals, per-line resolved rules and reversals are logged per the Financial Audit Log Policy. Finance samples commission computations at {{review_frequency_default}} and tests discount, return and tax treatment against this policy. Commission invoices are raised in line with {{gst_invoice_timeline}} and retained for {{data_retention_period}} under the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017.

Violations

Applying an unapproved rate, editing commission on a settled line, disabling a reversal, or offering a vendor terms outside the rate card without approval are control breaches. They are investigated by Finance with Human Resources and may lead to withdrawal of configuration access, disciplinary action and recovery of loss. Undisclosed personal benefit connected to a vendor rate is treated as fraud.

Related Documents

  • Vendor Settlement Policy — Finance View
  • Refund Approval Policy
  • Pricing and Discount Approval Policy
  • GST Invoicing and Tax Compliance Policy
  • Vendor Onboarding and KYC Policy
  • Financial Audit Log Policy

title: Financial Audit Log Policy
html:
DRAFT — LEGAL REVIEW REQUIRED. This document is an operational or legal draft and must be reviewed and approved by authorized management and, where required, qualified legal counsel before becoming effective.

Purpose

This policy defines what PlantAtHome records when money, money-affecting configuration, or financial authority changes; how those records are protected from alteration; who may read them; how long they are kept; and how often they are reviewed. Without a trustworthy log, no refund band, settlement or commission rate in the other financial policies can be proven after the fact.

Scope

All systems of Silvestrix Green LLP that create, change or release financial value under the PlantAtHome brand: the admin and operations console, the storefront and mobile apps, the order and settlement services, the Razorpay integration, courier and rider integrations, and any operational script or console command that writes to production data. It covers employee, contractor and vendor-console actions, and automated actions taken by scheduled jobs and integrations.

Definitions

  • Financial Audit Event — any recorded action that changes an amount, an approval state, a payout destination, or a rule that determines an amount.
  • Actor — the authenticated human, service account or scheduled job that performed the action.
  • Append-Only — a store to which records may be added but not updated or deleted through application paths.
  • Compensating Entry — a new record that corrects an earlier one without erasing it.
  • Privileged Action — a change made outside normal application workflow, such as a direct database write or an operational command.

Policy Statement

Every financial audit event is logged at the moment it occurs, with enough context to reconstruct who did what, to which record, from what value to what value, and on whose authority. Logs are append-only: corrections are made by compensating entry, never by rewriting history. If an action cannot be logged, it should not proceed. Access to financial logs is read-only, role-based and itself logged. Logs are treated as business records, not as debugging output, and are not deleted to reclaim storage.

Responsibilities

  • Engineering — instruments financial paths, enforces append-only storage at the database grant level, and prevents log-writing from being bypassed by scripts.
  • Finance Manager — defines which events are financially material and reviews the log for control breaches.
  • Security and IT — owns access control, backup, restore testing and tamper detection.
  • Head of Operations — approves privileged production actions before they are taken.
  • All staff and vendors — act under their own credentials only.

Policy Requirements

Event classExamplesMinimum fields capturedRetentionReview cadence
Money movementRefund release, vendor payout, gateway reversal, COD remittance matchActor, order or vendor reference, amount, instrument, approval reference, timestamp, result{{data_retention_period}}{{review_frequency_default}}
Approval decisionsRefund band approvals, settlement file approval, expense approvalsActor, band or limit applied, decision, reason code, evidence reference{{data_retention_period}}{{review_frequency_default}}
Rule and configuration changesCommission rate card, refund bands under {{approval_limit_refund}}, penalty schedule, shipping thresholdsActor, prior value, new value, effective-from, approver{{data_retention_period}}as per the currently approved Audit Review Configuration
Payout destination changesVendor bank account, UPI handle, GST or PAN recordActor, prior and new masked identifiers, verification evidence, approver{{data_retention_period}}Every change, reviewed before the next payout
Authority changesRole, permission and designation changes affecting financial approvalActor, subject user, prior and new role, approver{{data_retention_period}}{{review_frequency_default}}
Privileged actionsDirect database writes, operational commands, credential or key rotationActor, command or statement summary, ticket or approval reference, before and after state{{data_retention_period}}Reviewed at {{risk_review_frequency}}
Invoice and tax recordsInvoice generation, cancellation, credit notesActor, document number, order or settlement reference, amount, tax breakup{{data_retention_period}}{{review_frequency_default}}

Logs must never contain full card numbers, card verification values, banking credentials, passwords, API secrets or full authentication tokens; account identifiers are masked. Personal data inside logs is limited to what is needed to identify the actor and the affected order or vendor.

Procedures

  1. Application writes the audit event in the same transaction as the financial change, so a successful change cannot exist without its record.
  2. The database role used by the application holds insert and select rights on audit tables; update and delete rights are not granted to it.
  3. Logs are shipped to a separate retained store and included in the platform backup cycle at {{backup_frequency}}, kept for {{backup_retention}}, with restores tested at {{restore_test_frequency}}.
  4. Finance and Security run the scheduled review, examining out-of-band approvals, repeated refunds to the same customer or account, payout destination changes, and privileged actions without an approval reference.
  5. Suspected tampering, gaps in the record, or missing coverage on a financial path is raised as a security incident and classified under {{incident_severity_model}}.
  6. Read access is granted by role on the least-privilege basis in the Access Control Policy, authenticated with credentials meeting {{password_min_length}} and multi-factor authentication, and reviewed at {{review_frequency_default}}.

Exceptions

Emergency production intervention where logging is unavailable requires Head of Operations approval, must be recorded manually within the same working day, and is reviewed as an incident. Export of financial logs outside the platform requires Finance Manager approval, is limited to the fields needed, and is itself logged. Legal hold overrides deletion: records under investigation, dispute or regulatory request are preserved past their normal retention until the hold is lifted.

Compliance

This policy is designed to support PlantAtHome's record-keeping obligations under the Companies Act, 2013, the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017, the Information Technology Act, 2000, and the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023. It records an intended control standard and is not a certification of compliance; gaps found in review are tracked to closure with named owners. Requests from data principals are handled per the Data Retention and Privacy Policy within {{dsr_response_time}}, subject to statutory retention of financial records.

Violations

Disabling or bypassing audit logging, editing or deleting log records, sharing credentials, acting under another person's account, or performing a privileged production change without approval are serious breaches. They are investigated by Security with Finance and Human Resources and may lead to immediate withdrawal of access, disciplinary action up to termination, and referral to law enforcement where financial loss or concealment is involved.

Related Documents

  • Refund Approval Policy
  • Vendor Settlement Policy — Finance View
  • Commission Calculation Policy
  • Information Security Policy
  • Access Control Policy
  • Data Retention and Privacy Policy

title: Risk Management Framework
related_titles: Fraud Prevention and Payment Dispute Policy
html:
DRAFT — LEGAL REVIEW REQUIRED. This document is an operational or legal draft and must be reviewed and approved by authorized management and, where required, qualified legal counsel before becoming effective.

Purpose

This framework gives PlantAtHome, a brand of Silvestrix Green LLP, one consistent method for identifying, scoring, owning, mitigating and monitoring the risks that can interrupt trade in perishable living inventory, break a delivery promise, expose customer money or personal data, or damage the brand. It exists so risk decisions are made deliberately, by a named person, and recorded — rather than absorbed silently by whichever team notices the problem first.

Scope

This framework applies across all verticals — live plants, gardening tools, pots and planters, seeds, fertilizers, accessories, FarmBox fresh produce and corporate gifting — and to both fulfilment lanes: direct fulfilment and fulfilment by approved nursery vendors, delivered hyperlocally by rider or pan-India by courier. It binds every employee, contractor and intern, and every vendor to the extent set out in their agreement. It covers the storefront, admin console, mobile applications, the Razorpay payment stack, the WhatsApp Business API, email and SMS notification channels, and all third-party logistics integrations.

Definitions

  • Risk — an uncertain event that, if it occurred, would damage customers, revenue, living stock, data, or the brand.
  • Inherent and residual risk — exposure before controls, and exposure remaining after the controls actually in place today.
  • Risk owner — the single named individual accountable for a risk, its controls and its contingency. Ownership is never assigned to a team name alone.
  • Risk register — the maintained record of identified risks, scores, owners, treatments and review dates.
  • Key risk indicator (KRI) — an operational metric watched as an early warning that a risk is materialising.
  • Approved Risk Configuration — the current management-approved set of risk categories, scoring bands, appetite thresholds and escalation triggers held in the system of record. Categories and thresholds are configurable and are deliberately not fixed in this document.

Policy Statement

PlantAtHome manages risk as a normal part of running the business, not as an annual paperwork exercise. Every material risk must carry a named owner, a score produced by {{risk_scoring_model}}, a mitigation that reduces likelihood or impact, and a contingency for the case where mitigation fails. Risks are reviewed per {{risk_review_frequency}}, and the wider framework per {{review_frequency_default}}. Risk is accepted only knowingly, in writing, and by someone with the authority to accept it.

Responsibilities

  • Designated Partners — set risk appetite, approve the Approved Risk Configuration, and authorise acceptance of risks scored above appetite.
  • Function heads (risk owners) — maintain their register entries, run mitigations, report KRI breaches without waiting for a review cycle.
  • Operations and Logistics — own plant handling, dispatch, rider and courier performance risks.
  • Technology — own platform availability, data security and integration failure risks.
  • Finance — own payment, chargeback, fraud, GST and vendor settlement risks.
  • Vendor Management — owns vendor capability, quality and concentration risks.
  • All personnel — report emerging risks and near-misses to the relevant owner; concealment is itself a reportable event.

Policy Requirements

Each register entry must record the category, description, cause, owner, inherent and residual scores under {{risk_scoring_model}}, controls in place, contingency reference, KRI, and next review date. The default categories below are the starting set; they and their thresholds may be amended in the Approved Risk Configuration without reissuing this policy.

Default risk categoryStanding ownerPrimary indicator monitoredEscalation trigger
Plant mortality and shrinkageNursery OperationsDead-on-arrival and mortality claims raised within {{live_plant_claim_window}}Threshold in Approved Risk Configuration
Weather disruptionLogisticsDispatch holds and breaches of {{delivery_sla_hyperlocal}}Per Approved Risk Configuration
Courier failureLogisticsFailed attempts against {{delivery_attempts}} and {{delivery_sla_courier}}Per Approved Risk Configuration
FraudFinanceFlagged orders, refund abuse patternsAny case above {{approval_limit_refund}}
Data breachTechnologySecurity alerts, unauthorised access eventsPer {{incident_severity_model}}
Inventory mismatchCatalogue OperationsStock variance and oversell eventsPer Approved Risk Configuration
Payment disputesFinanceChargebacks and settlement mismatchesPer Approved Risk Configuration
Vendor failureVendor Management{{vendor_acceptance_sla}}, {{vendor_dispatch_sla}}, {{vendor_return_rate_threshold}}{{penalty_schedule}}
Regulatory changeDesignated PartnersStatutory and platform rule changesOn notification
Technology failureTechnologyAvailability and integration error ratesPer {{incident_severity_model}}
ReputationMarketing and SupportComplaint volume against {{support_resolution_sla}}Per Approved Risk Configuration

Procedures

Risks are identified from order exception queues, vendor performance reports, courier failure data, chargeback notices, security monitoring, stock variance reports, support escalations and post-incident reviews. Each identified risk is scored under {{risk_scoring_model}} and assigned an owner. Treatment is selected from reduce, transfer, avoid or accept, and recorded with the control that delivers it. Contingency planning is mandatory for any risk whose materialisation would stop customer orders being fulfilled; the contingency must name the fallback process and the person who activates it. Owners monitor KRIs continuously and escalate breaches per {{escalation_timeline}}. Registers are reviewed per {{risk_review_frequency}}, and any risk that materialises is re-scored using what the incident revealed.

Exceptions

Operating outside an approved threshold requires written acceptance by a Designated Partner, must be time-bound with a defined expiry, and must state the compensating control in force meanwhile. Expenditure to mitigate a risk follows {{approval_limit_expense}}. No exception may waive a statutory obligation, and none may be granted retrospectively to cover an unreported incident.

Compliance

This framework supports obligations under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019 and the e-commerce rules made under it, the Legal Metrology (Packaged Commodities) Rules, the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023, the Information Technology Act, 2000 and applicable GST law. Card data is handled by Razorpay as the payment processor; PlantAtHome does not store card credentials, and no claim of independent payment-card certification is made. Register completeness and review timeliness are themselves audited per {{review_frequency_default}}.

Violations

Failing to record a known material risk, accepting risk without authority, breaching a threshold without escalation, or concealing an incident or near-miss will be treated as a disciplinary matter proportionate to the harm caused, and may lead to termination where the conduct is deliberate. Vendor breaches are handled under the vendor agreement and {{penalty_schedule}}, up to suspension or delisting.

Related Documents

  • Business Continuity Plan
  • Contingency Procedures
  • Information Security Policy
  • Vendor Onboarding and Management Policy
  • Fraud Prevention and Payment Dispute Policy
  • Customer Support and Escalation Policy

title: Business Continuity Plan
html:
DRAFT — LEGAL REVIEW REQUIRED. This document is an operational or legal draft and must be reviewed and approved by authorized management and, where required, qualified legal counsel before becoming effective.

Purpose

This plan sets out how PlantAtHome keeps taking, fulfilling and settling orders when something material breaks — the platform, the payment rail, the delivery network, the weather, a major vendor, or the security of our data. It is written as a scalable framework rather than a fixed script, because the business runs on a small team and continuity work must be proportionate to the disruption actually faced.

Scope

This plan covers all trading verticals and both fulfilment lanes (direct and approved nursery vendor), the hyperlocal rider and pan-India courier networks, the storefront, admin console and mobile applications, the Razorpay payment integration, the WhatsApp Business API, email and SMS notification channels, and the physical handling of live inventory. It covers disruption from the point of detection to formal stand-down and recovery.

Definitions

  • Disruption — any event that prevents normal order capture, fulfilment, communication or settlement.
  • Interim trading mode — a deliberately reduced way of operating that keeps customer commitments alive while normal systems are unavailable.
  • Incident Commander — the person who declares a disruption, directs response and calls stand-down.
  • Perishable exposure — orders containing live plants or FarmBox produce, which degrade while a disruption continues and therefore take priority over non-perishable stock.
  • Recovery objectives — the target time to restore a service and the tolerable data loss, as set in the Approved Continuity Configuration.

Policy Statement

PlantAtHome will maintain a proportionate, tested capability to continue serving customers through disruption, and will be honest internally and externally about the limits of that capability. Continuity is treated as an operational obligation to customers holding paid orders and to vendors holding stock on our behalf, not as a documentation exercise.

An honest statement of current maturity: backup and restore practices, monitoring, and manual fallback procedures exist and are in use. Full disaster-recovery capability is still being built. Formally agreed recovery time and recovery point objectives, standby infrastructure able to take over automatically, and independently exercised failover for every integration are not yet in place. Until they are, continuity for several scenarios depends on manual handling by a small team, and this plan states that plainly rather than implying a resilience the business does not yet have.

Responsibilities

  • Designated Partners — approve this plan and the Approved Continuity Configuration, authorise spend during a disruption within {{approval_limit_expense}}, and approve any external statement.
  • Incident Commander — declares severity per {{incident_severity_model}}, runs the response, maintains the log, calls stand-down.
  • Technology — restores platform and integrations, protects data, verifies backups per {{backup_frequency}} with retention per {{backup_retention}} and restore testing per {{restore_test_frequency}}.
  • Operations and Logistics — protects living stock, re-sequences dispatch, arranges alternative delivery routing.
  • Finance — reconciles payments taken during degraded operation and manages vendor settlement continuity per {{vendor_settlement_cycle}}.
  • Support — handles customer contact within {{support_response_sla}} across {{support_channels}} using approved holding messages.

Policy Requirements

Every scenario below must have a named owner, a workable interim trading mode, and defined criteria for returning to normal. Where a scenario currently has no automated fallback, the manual fallback must be documented and known to the people expected to run it.

ScenarioImmediate priorityInterim trading modeReturn criteria
Technology outagePreserve paid orders and data integrityManual order capture and dispatch per Contingency ProceduresService restored and backlog reconciled
Payment failurePrevent double charges and orphaned paymentsHold order confirmation; reconcile against processor records before dispatchProcessor confirms stability; ledger matches
Major logistics disruptionPerishable exposure firstRe-route between hyperlocal and courier lanes; proactive re-scheduling within {{delivery_sla_courier}} expectationsNetwork capacity restored
Extreme weatherProtect living stock and rider safetyPause dispatch of perishables; notify affected customers before the promised window lapsesConditions safe per Operations assessment
Vendor disruptionRe-source open ordersReassign to alternate approved vendor or direct fulfilment within {{vendor_acceptance_sla}}Vendor recovers or orders reassigned
Data incidentContain, preserve evidence, assess personal data exposureRestrict affected systems; continue trading only where safeContainment confirmed and notifications assessed

Procedures

Detection may come from monitoring, a support surge, a vendor or courier notification, a payment processor status change, or an employee report. The Incident Commander confirms the scenario, assigns severity per {{incident_severity_model}}, and activates the relevant interim trading mode. Perishable exposure is triaged first: live plants and FarmBox orders already picked or in transit are protected before non-perishable stock. Customer communication uses approved holding messages over {{support_channels}}, states what is known, and never promises a restoration time that has not been confirmed. All actions, decisions and timings are logged as they happen. Stand-down, recovery reconciliation and post-incident review are executed under Contingency Procedures.

Exceptions

During a declared disruption, the Incident Commander may suspend non-essential process steps to keep customer commitments alive, provided financial controls, statutory obligations and personal data protections are maintained. Any such suspension is logged and reviewed at stand-down. Deviations affecting refunds beyond {{approval_limit_refund}} or spend beyond {{approval_limit_expense}} require Designated Partner approval.

Compliance

Response to a data incident must satisfy the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 and the Information Technology Act, 2000, including notification obligations assessed within the statutory timelines and data subject handling per {{dsr_response_time}}. Customer commitments during disruption remain governed by the Consumer Protection Act, 2019 and its e-commerce rules. Tax documentation remains due per {{gst_invoice_timeline}} even where invoicing is performed manually. This plan is reviewed per {{review_frequency_default}} and after every declared disruption.

Violations

Trading through a known disruption without declaring it, bypassing payment reconciliation, dispatching perishable orders known to be undeliverable, or delaying notification of a suspected data incident are serious breaches and will be handled as disciplinary matters. Vendor failures to follow agreed continuity obligations are addressed under {{penalty_schedule}}.

Related Documents

  • Risk Management Framework
  • Contingency Procedures
  • Information Security Policy
  • Backup and Data Recovery Standard
  • Delivery and Shipping Policy
  • Customer Support and Escalation Policy

title: Contingency Procedures
html:
DRAFT — LEGAL REVIEW REQUIRED. This document is an operational or legal draft and must be reviewed and approved by authorized management and, where required, qualified legal counsel before becoming effective.

Purpose

These procedures tell the person on shift exactly what to do when the Business Continuity Plan is activated: who declares a disruption, who is told and in what order, how orders are taken and fulfilled without the platform, and how the business is returned to normal operation afterwards. It is written to be usable under pressure by whoever is available, not only by the people who wrote it.

Scope

These procedures apply to every declared disruption affecting order capture, fulfilment, payment, delivery or customer communication, across all verticals and both fulfilment lanes. They apply to employees, contractors and any approved nursery vendor asked to operate in fallback mode on our behalf.

Definitions

  • Activation — the formal decision to leave normal operation and run a contingency mode.
  • Communication tree — the fixed order in which people are contacted so no one waits for permission to escalate.
  • Manual order record — the offline record of an order taken while systems are unavailable, containing everything needed to reconstruct it later.
  • Stand-down — the formal decision that contingency mode has ended and normal process resumes.
  • Reconciliation backlog — manual records, payments and stock movements awaiting entry into the platform after stand-down.

Policy Statement

Contingency operation is a controlled state with a start, a defined way of working, and an end. Nobody improvises alone: activation is declared, actions are logged, and the business does not drift back to normal without an explicit stand-down and a reconciliation that proves nothing was lost. Customer money, live stock and personal data are protected ahead of throughput.

Responsibilities

  • First responder — anyone who detects the problem; obliged to alert the Incident Commander immediately, whatever the hour.
  • Incident Commander — declares activation and severity, directs response, owns the log, calls stand-down.
  • Operations lead — runs manual fulfilment, protects perishable stock, controls dispatch sequencing.
  • Technology lead — diagnoses and restores, preserves evidence in security incidents, confirms data integrity before reconciliation.
  • Finance lead — controls payment handling, verifies every manual order against processor records.
  • Support lead — issues approved customer messaging and holds the line on what may and may not be promised.

Policy Requirements

Activation levels follow {{incident_severity_model}}; escalation between levels follows {{escalation_timeline}}. The following table is the working reference on shift.

LevelTypical triggerDeclared byWho is told
WatchDegraded service or single failing integration, orders still flowingFunction lead on shiftIncident Commander and affected function
ActivatedOrder capture, payment, dispatch or notification unavailableIncident CommanderAll function leads, Support briefed with holding message
CriticalSuspected data incident, payment integrity in doubt, or multi-day fulfilment stoppageIncident Commander with a Designated PartnerDesignated Partners, all leads, affected vendors

The communication tree runs first responder to Incident Commander, then to function leads in parallel, then to Designated Partners at Critical, then outward to vendors and customers. If the Incident Commander cannot be reached within {{escalation_timeline}}, the first responder contacts a Designated Partner directly. Customers are told only what is confirmed, within {{support_response_sla}} across {{support_channels}}.

Procedures

Activation. Confirm the failure is real and not local to one device. Declare the level, timestamp it, open the incident log, and name who is doing what.

Temporary manual order handling. Capture every order on a manual order record containing customer name and contact, delivery address with landmark, items and quantities, quoted price, payment status and reference, promised window, and the name of the person who took it. Do not take card details by phone or message under any circumstances; direct customers to an approved payment link or record the order as unpaid pending confirmation. Verify stock by physical or vendor confirmation before committing, since availability cannot be trusted while the platform is down. Prioritise dispatch of live plants and FarmBox produce over non-perishable items. Confirm each order to the customer over an approved channel so they hold a written record. Vendors operating in fallback are given orders by an approved channel only, with acceptance confirmed back in writing.

Stand-down. The Incident Commander confirms the underlying failure is resolved and stable, then declares stand-down with a timestamp and notifies everyone on the communication tree.

Recovery. Enter the reconciliation backlog into the platform in the order the records were created, matching each payment against processor records before any dispatch or refund is finalised. Correct stock positions against physical counts. Re-check every promised delivery window and re-communicate where a promise can no longer be met, applying the standard refund route where the customer chooses to cancel, processed within {{refund_processing_time}}. Confirm tax documentation is issued per {{gst_invoice_timeline}} for orders invoiced manually. Hold a post-incident review that produces named actions with owners and feeds the risk register per {{risk_review_frequency}}.

Exceptions

The Incident Commander may vary these steps where following them would cause greater harm, for example halting all dispatch rather than sequencing it. Variations are logged with the reason. Refunds or goodwill beyond {{approval_limit_refund}} and spend beyond {{approval_limit_expense}} still require Designated Partner approval, and no exception permits taking card details manually or delaying assessment of a suspected data incident.

Compliance

Manual operation does not suspend statutory duties. Consumer obligations under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019 continue to apply to orders taken offline; personal data written on manual records is protected under the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023, must be stored securely during the incident, entered into the platform at reconciliation, and destroyed once entered rather than retained beyond {{data_retention_period}}. Incident logs are retained as evidence of response.

Violations

Operating in fallback without declaring activation, taking payment card details manually, dispatching against unverified stock, discarding manual records before reconciliation, or resuming normal operation without stand-down are serious breaches and will be treated as disciplinary matters. Vendor non-compliance is handled under {{penalty_schedule}}.

Related Documents
