  • Risk Management Framework
  • Customer Support and Escalation Policy
  • Delivery and Shipping Policy
  • Returns, Refunds and Cancellation Policy
  • Information Security Policy

title: Product Data Standards
html:
DRAFT — LEGAL REVIEW REQUIRED. This document is an operational or legal draft and must be reviewed and approved by authorized management and, where required, qualified legal counsel before becoming effective.

Purpose

PlantAtHome sells living products that a customer cannot inspect before purchase. The product record is therefore the customer's only representation of what will arrive, and it also drives city availability, delivery routing, care messaging and post-delivery claim handling. This standard defines the attributes every plant product record must carry, where that data must live, and the completeness rules that must be satisfied before a product may be listed for sale.

Scope

This standard applies to every live plant SKU published on the PlantAtHome website, mobile app and any syndicated feed, whether created by the PlantAtHome merchandising team in the master catalogue or proposed by an approved nursery vendor. It applies to gifting bundles and FarmBox listings to the extent they include a live plant. Non-plant categories — tools, pots and planters, seeds, fertilizers and accessories — are governed by their own required-field sets in the product database but are subject to the same completeness gate and the same review discipline.

Definitions

  • Product record — the structured entry for a SKU in the PlantAtHome product database, including its attributes, media and availability mapping.
  • Structured attribute — a typed, validated field stored against the product record, as distinct from free-text description copy.
  • Controlled list — the permitted set of values for an attribute, maintained in the product database and not in this document.
  • Completeness gate — the automated and human check that must pass before a record may move from draft to live.
  • Attribute owner — the named role accountable for the accuracy of a given attribute.

Policy Statement

Plant product data belongs in the structured product database, not in policy text, marketing copy, images or vendor correspondence. This document names the attributes that are mandatory and the rules that govern them; the permitted values, field types and validation logic are held in the product database and its configuration, which is the single source of truth. A product record may not be listed for sale until every mandatory attribute is populated with a valid value and the record has passed catalogue review. Description copy may elaborate on structured data but must never substitute for it or contradict it.

Responsibilities

  • Merchandising / catalogue team — owns the master catalogue, the controlled lists and the taxonomy; performs catalogue review and periodic audits.
  • Approved vendors — supply complete and accurate data for products they propose, and notify PlantAtHome when a supplied product changes in size, pot, sourcing or appearance.
  • Horticulture reviewer — verifies botanical identification, care attributes, pet safety and toxicity content.
  • Technology team — maintains field validation, the completeness gate and audit reporting.
  • Customer support — reports data defects surfaced by customer contacts back to the catalogue team.

Policy Requirements

Every live plant product record must carry the following attributes as structured fields.

AttributeRequirementValidation
Botanical nameMandatory; genus and species at minimum, with cultivar where applicableVerified against the approved horticultural reference set; no waiver permitted
Common nameMandatory; customer-facing display nameMust not imply a species other than the botanical name
CategoryMandatory; one primary category plus applicable verticalControlled list from the published taxonomy
Plant sizeMandatory; height and spread band as suppliedControlled list; must match dispatch reality
Pot sizeMandatory; nursery or decorative pot as shippedControlled list; must match the packed item
Sunlight requirementMandatoryControlled list
Water requirementMandatoryControlled list
Care levelMandatoryControlled list
Pet safetyMandatory; explicit safe or not safeUnverified status blocks listing; no waiver permitted
Toxicity informationMandatory wherever pet safety is not safeHorticulture reviewer sign-off; no waiver permitted
Climate suitabilityMandatory; mapped to serviceable cities and zonesControlled list; drives availability
Expected appearanceMandatory; states natural variation and seasonal stateReviewed against current supply
ImagesMandatory; media set as per the currently approved Catalogue Media ConfigurationGoverned by the Product Image Accuracy Standard

Procedures

  1. A record is created in draft state, by merchandising or by an approved vendor through the vendor catalogue interface.
  2. The completeness gate runs automatically; records missing a mandatory attribute or holding an invalid value cannot be submitted for review.
  3. Catalogue review checks values against supply reality, with horticulture sign-off on identification, pet safety and toxicity.
  4. An approved record is published; a rejected record returns to the originator with the failing attributes named.
  5. Any change to size, pot, sourcing vendor or appearance requires the record to be updated before further dispatch, and re-review where a mandatory attribute changes.
  6. Catalogue audits sample live records at {{review_frequency_default}}, and immediately following any customer claim attributed to a data defect.

Exceptions

A temporary waiver of a non-critical attribute may be granted only by the catalogue owner, must record the reason, the named approver and an expiry date, and must be visible in the record's audit trail. No waiver is available for botanical name, pet safety, toxicity information or the mandatory media set. A record whose waiver expires unresolved is delisted automatically.

Compliance

Compliance is measured by completeness-gate pass rate, audit findings and the volume of customer claims traced to inaccurate product data. Vendor-originated data defects are recorded against the vendor's quality record and assessed against {{vendor_quality_target}}. Records that fail audit are delisted until corrected.

Violations

Bypassing the completeness gate, publishing unverified pet safety or toxicity data, or knowingly listing attributes that do not match the item supplied are treated as serious breaches. Internal breaches are handled under PlantAtHome's disciplinary process. Vendor breaches attract the remedies set out in {{penalty_schedule}}, up to suspension of listings and termination under the Vendor Code of Conduct, without prejudice to obligations under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019 and applicable e-commerce rules.

Related Documents

  • Live Plant Quality Standards
  • Product Image Accuracy Standard
  • Vendor Onboarding and Approval Policy
  • Vendor Code of Conduct

title: Live Plant Quality Standards
html:
DRAFT — LEGAL REVIEW REQUIRED. This document is an operational or legal draft and must be reviewed and approved by authorized management and, where required, qualified legal counsel before becoming effective.

Purpose

A live plant continues to change after it is picked. This standard defines the pre-dispatch quality checks every live plant must pass, the outcomes a checker may record, and the controls that prevent a failed plant from reaching a customer. It exists to reduce dead-on-arrival claims, replacement cost and the reputational damage of sending a customer a plant that a trained eye would have rejected.

Scope

This standard applies to every live plant dispatched under the PlantAtHome brand, whether packed at a PlantAtHome facility or at an approved nursery vendor's premises, and whether moving by hyperlocal rider or pan-India courier. It covers plants sold individually, in bundles, as gifting items and as part of FarmBox orders. It applies to replacement and re-dispatch units on the same terms as first dispatch.

Definitions

  • Quality check — the physical inspection of a specific unit against the nine checkpoints in this standard, performed after picking and before packing is sealed.
  • Checker — the trained person performing the inspection; at a vendor site, the vendor's nominated quality contact.
  • PASS — every checkpoint met; the unit may proceed to dispatch.
  • FAIL — one or more checkpoints not met; the unit must not proceed to dispatch.
  • CONDITIONAL — the unit is dispatchable only after a named remedial action is completed and re-checked.
  • Override — an authorised decision to dispatch a unit that did not record a clean PASS.

Policy Statement

No live plant is dispatched without a recorded quality check outcome against the unit being shipped. A FAIL outcome blocks dispatch. A CONDITIONAL outcome blocks dispatch until the remedial action is completed and a fresh outcome is recorded. Quality is judged on the plant in hand, not on the catalogue photograph or on a batch inspection performed earlier in the day.

Responsibilities

  • Checker — performs the inspection honestly, records the outcome and the failing checkpoints, and segregates failed units.
  • Vendor — ensures every dispatching site has a trained nominated checker and that failed units are withdrawn from the order rather than substituted silently.
  • Operations manager — is the only role that may authorise an override, and owns the resulting audit record.
  • Quality lead — reviews outcome data, override frequency and downstream claims, and retrains or suspends checkers where the data does not reconcile.
  • Customer support — links every live-plant claim back to the recorded outcome for that unit.

Policy Requirements

Each unit is assessed against all nine checkpoints. Any checkpoint marked as failing produces a FAIL for the unit unless the table permits a CONDITIONAL route.

CheckpointWhat is assessedPermitted outcomes
Healthy foliageColour, turgidity, absence of significant browning, yellowing, scorch or mechanical damagePASS or FAIL
Healthy rootsRoot colour and firmness, absence of rot or severe pot-binding, root ball intactPASS or FAIL
Soil conditionMedium appropriate to the species, level as per the currently approved Potting Media Configuration, free of contaminationPASS or CONDITIONAL (top-up and re-check)
MoistureMoisture appropriate to the species and to the dispatch lane, neither waterlogged nor desiccatedPASS or CONDITIONAL (adjust and re-check)
Pest-freeNo live pests, eggs or webbing on foliage, stem, medium surface or pot exteriorPASS or FAIL
Disease-freeNo fungal, bacterial or viral symptoms; no spreading lesionsPASS or FAIL
Structural integrityStem and branch soundness, pot intact and not cracked, plant stable in its potPASS or CONDITIONAL (repot and re-check)
Correct labellingSpecies, size and pot size match the ordered SKU and the product recordPASS or FAIL
Secure packagingPacked to the approved method for the species, size and dispatch lane; root ball secured; ventilation as requiredPASS or CONDITIONAL (repack and re-check)

A unit recording FAIL must be physically segregated from dispatch-ready stock and the order line held, substituted with a passing unit of the same SKU, or cancelled and refunded under the applicable refund policy. Backdating, editing or reusing a prior outcome record for a different unit is prohibited.

Procedures

  1. Pick the unit against the order line and take it to the check station.
  2. Assess all nine checkpoints and record the outcome against the order line and the unit, naming any failing checkpoint.
  3. On CONDITIONAL, complete the named remedial action, then record a fresh outcome; a unit may not be dispatched on a CONDITIONAL record alone.
  4. On FAIL, segregate the unit, flag the order line, and either substitute a passing unit within {{vendor_dispatch_sla}} or escalate to operations for hold or cancellation.
  5. Seal packaging only after a PASS is recorded, and attach the dispatch documentation.
  6. Quality lead reviews outcome and override data at {{review_frequency_default}} against claim volumes and {{vendor_return_rate_threshold}}.

Exceptions

An override of a FAIL is permitted only where the operations manager judges the defect cosmetic and immaterial to plant health. Every override must record the authorising person by name, the specific checkpoint overridden, the reason, and the customer-facing disclosure made where the appearance differs from the listing. Overrides are written to an immutable audit trail and reported at {{review_frequency_default}}. No override is available for pest, disease or root failures, or for incorrect labelling.

Compliance

Compliance is measured by check coverage against dispatched units, override rate, and the correlation between recorded outcomes and downstream claims raised within {{live_plant_claim_window}}. Vendor performance is assessed against {{vendor_quality_target}} and {{vendor_return_rate_threshold}}. Persistent gaps trigger retraining, mandatory pre-dispatch photography or suspension of self-checking at that site.

Violations

Dispatching a FAIL unit without an authorised override, recording an outcome for a unit that was not inspected, or concealing a substitution are treated as serious breaches. Employees are handled under the disciplinary process. Vendors are subject to {{penalty_schedule}}, recovery of replacement and return-leg costs, suspension of order allocation and termination under the Vendor Code of Conduct.

Related Documents

  • Product Data Standards
  • Product Image Accuracy Standard
  • Vendor Code of Conduct
  • Vendor Onboarding and Approval Policy

title: Customer Ticket Handling SOP
related_titles: Customer Grievance Redressal and Escalation Policy
html:
DRAFT — LEGAL REVIEW REQUIRED. This document is an operational or legal draft and must be reviewed and approved by authorized management and, where required, qualified legal counsel before becoming effective.

Purpose

This procedure defines how PlantAtHome (Silvestrix Green LLP) receives, triages, investigates, resolves and closes customer support tickets so that every contact is traceable to an owner, an order and a resolution. It exists to make support outcomes consistent across live plants, gardening tools, pots and planters, seeds, fertilizers, accessories, FarmBox produce and corporate gifting, whether the order was fulfilled directly or by an approved nursery vendor.

Scope

Applies to all customer contacts received on the approved support channels listed in {{support_channels}}, including WhatsApp Business API, email, SMS reply, in-app and web contact forms, and calls logged by the support team. It covers pre-purchase queries, delivery issues on both the hyperlocal rider lane and the pan-India courier lane, product condition complaints, payment and Razorpay reconciliation queries, and requests routed to refund, replacement or return workflows. Vendor-side disputes are in scope only up to the point of handoff to vendor operations.

Definitions

Ticket: a single tracked customer issue holding ticket ID, priority, category, subcategory, customer identity, related order, owner, applicable SLA, status, resolution notes, customer satisfaction score and escalation history.

Category and subcategory: the configured classification pair (for example Delivery / Not Delivered, Product / Plant Damaged in Transit, Payments / Refund Not Received) used for routing and reporting.

Priority: one of LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH or URGENT. Priority values, their routing rules and their SLA mapping are configurable and are applied as per the currently approved Support SLA Configuration.

Owner: the named support agent accountable for the ticket until closure, regardless of how many teams contribute.

Roles and Responsibilities

  • Support Agent: acknowledges, triages, investigates, communicates, and records resolution notes and the satisfaction outcome.
  • Support Lead: monitors the queue and breach risk, reassigns ownership, approves priority overrides, and owns first-level escalations.
  • Operations and Fulfilment: verifies dispatch, rider or courier status, and reattempt feasibility.
  • Vendor Management: handles tickets traced to an approved nursery vendor's packing, dispatch or quality performance.
  • Finance: executes approved refunds through the original payment instrument and confirms settlement references.
  • Head of Customer Experience: owns this SOP, the configuration values it references, and final escalation authority.

Prerequisites

  • Agent has an active support desk account with role-based access to the order record, shipment tracking and customer contact history.
  • Category, subcategory, priority and SLA configuration is current and published.
  • Approved WhatsApp message templates and email templates are live for acknowledgement, update and closure messages.
  • Refund, replacement and return decision authority is defined and current, including {{approval_limit_refund}}.

Trigger

A ticket is created automatically when a customer message arrives on any approved channel, when a delivery exception is raised by the fulfilment system, or manually by an agent logging a call or an internally detected issue affecting a customer order.

Step-by-Step Procedure

  1. Capture. Create or confirm the ticket record. Populate ticket ID, customer, related order, channel of origin and the customer's stated issue in their own words.
  2. Verify identity and order linkage. Match the requester against the registered contact on the order before disclosing any order, address or payment detail. Where no order exists, classify as a pre-purchase or general query.
  3. Triage. Assign category, subcategory and priority using the currently approved Support Priority Configuration. Perishable and live-plant condition issues, failed or misdelivered hyperlocal deliveries, payment debited without order creation, and any safety or legal allegation are triaged upward.
  4. Assign ownership. Route to the queue mapped to the category and set a named owner. Unowned tickets are not permitted in any status other than newly created.
  5. Acknowledge. Send the approved acknowledgement message confirming ticket ID and next update commitment.
  6. Investigate against the order record. Review order status, line items, vendor allocation, dispatch and rider or courier scan history, prior tickets on the same order, and any evidence the customer supplied. Request photographic evidence where the category requires it, within {{replacement_evidence_window}}.
  7. Select a resolution path. Information-only closure; redelivery or reattempt within {{delivery_attempts}}; replacement under the Product Replacement Policy; return initiation under the Returns and Cancellation Policy within {{return_request_window}}; refund under the Customer Refund Policy; or goodwill adjustment within delegated authority. Live-plant condition claims follow {{live_plant_claim_window}}.
  8. Obtain approvals. Where the remedy exceeds the agent's authority, route for approval and record the approver and decision in the ticket.
  9. Execute and confirm. Trigger the downstream action, capture the reference identifier (replacement order, return pickup, refund reference) in resolution notes, and inform the customer.
  10. Close with a satisfaction check. Confirm the customer agrees the issue is resolved, set status to Resolved, dispatch the satisfaction survey, and record the returned customer satisfaction score against the ticket.

SLA

First response and resolution targets are driven by ticket priority as configured. Timers start at ticket creation, pause only while the ticket is in a documented Awaiting Customer status, and resume on customer reply.

PriorityFirst response targetResolution target
URGENT{{support_response_sla}}{{support_resolution_sla}}
HIGH{{support_response_sla}}{{support_resolution_sla}}
MEDIUM{{support_response_sla}}{{support_resolution_sla}}
LOW{{support_response_sla}}{{support_resolution_sla}}

Quality Checks

  • Every ticket has a category, subcategory, priority, named owner and, where applicable, a linked order before it leaves triage.
  • Resolution notes state what was found, what was done and the downstream reference, not merely "resolved".
  • Reopened tickets and tickets with a low satisfaction score are sampled and reviewed by the Support Lead at {{review_frequency_default}}.
  • No commitment is made to a customer on timelines, amounts or outcomes beyond what the published policies and current configuration permit.

Exceptions

Corporate gifting and bulk FarmBox accounts may be handled under an account-specific service arrangement, which overrides default routing but not the record-keeping requirements of this SOP. Tickets alleging regulatory breach, data-protection violation, personal injury, or arriving as a legal notice or consumer forum communication are not resolved by the support team; they are logged, priority-flagged and handed to management and legal immediately. Fraud-indicative or abusive contacts may be placed on a restricted-handling flag by the Support Lead.

Escalation Process

A ticket escalates when the response or resolution target is at risk of breach, when the customer requests escalation, when the remedy exceeds delegated authority, or when the same order generates a repeat complaint. Escalation moves through Support Agent, Support Lead, Head of Customer Experience and then management, following {{escalation_timeline}}. Each escalation appends an entry to the ticket's escalation history recording the reason, the recipient and the timestamp; ownership transfers explicitly and is never left implied.

Records and Audit Trail

The support desk retains the full ticket record including all customer correspondence, internal notes, status transitions, approvals, escalation history and the satisfaction score, held for {{data_retention_period}}. Refund and replacement actions must be reconcilable to the order and payment records. Customer personal data is accessed only for handling the ticket, and data subject requests arising within a ticket are routed to the privacy owner and answered within {{dsr_response_time}}.

Related Documents

  • Customer Refund Policy
  • Product Replacement Policy
  • Returns and Cancellation Policy
  • Customer Grievance Redressal and Escalation Policy

title: Customer Support Policy
related_titles: Live Plant Replacement and Claims Policy
html:
DRAFT — LEGAL REVIEW REQUIRED. This document is an operational or legal draft and must be reviewed and approved by authorized management and, where required, qualified legal counsel before becoming effective.

Purpose

This policy defines how PlantAtHome, a brand of Silvestrix Green LLP, receives, handles, records and closes customer contacts, and what a customer may expect once they reach us. It exists so that a question about a wilted plant, a delayed hyperlocal rider, a Razorpay charge or a corporate gifting order is handled to the same standard regardless of the channel used, and regardless of whether the order was fulfilled directly or by an approved nursery vendor.

Scope

This policy covers all pre-purchase, in-order and post-delivery contacts across every vertical we sell — live plants, gardening tools, pots and planters, seeds, fertilizers, accessories, FarmBox fresh produce and corporate gifting — for both hyperlocal same-day delivery in serviceable cities and pan-India courier delivery elsewhere. It binds employees, contractors, temporary staff and any vendor personnel who speak to a customer on PlantAtHome's behalf. Commercial disputes between PlantAtHome and a vendor are outside this policy and follow the vendor agreement.

Definitions

  • Contact — any inbound customer message, call or form submission received on an enabled channel.
  • Ticket — the single record in the admin support system that carries a contact, its order linkage, all correspondence and its outcome.
  • First response — the first substantive human reply that acknowledges the issue and states the next step. Automated acknowledgements do not count.
  • Resolution — the point at which the agreed remedy has been actioned (refund approved, replacement dispatched, delivery rebooked, information supplied) and communicated to the customer.
  • Enabled channel — a channel listed as active in {{support_channels}}.
  • Vendor-fulfilled order — an order or line item shipped by an approved nursery vendor rather than from our own stock.

Policy Statement

Every contact is logged, owned by a named agent and closed with a stated outcome. Support commitments are published as {{support_response_sla}} for first response and {{support_resolution_sla}} for resolution, measured on enabled channels only. Agents resolve within the published customer policies; where a case falls outside them, it is escalated rather than settled informally. We do not promise a customer an outcome we cannot deliver, and we do not close a ticket without telling the customer why.

Responsibilities

  • Support agent — owns the ticket end to end: verification, correct classification, accurate record-keeping, customer communication and closure.
  • Support lead — queue health, breach watch against {{support_response_sla}} and {{support_resolution_sla}}, quality sampling and coaching.
  • Vendor operations — pursues vendor-fulfilled cases against {{vendor_acceptance_sla}} and {{vendor_dispatch_sla}} and supplies the vendor's response back to the ticket.
  • Delivery operations — rider and courier exceptions, reattempts within {{delivery_attempts}}, and address or serviceability corrections.
  • Finance — refund execution within {{refund_processing_time}} and approvals beyond {{approval_limit_refund}}.
  • Grievance officer — statutory grievance handling and the final internal review point.

Policy Requirements

ChannelAuthorised useFirst responseResolution
WhatsApp Business APITwo-way support, order status, evidence collection (photographs of plants and packaging){{support_response_sla}}{{support_resolution_sla}}
EmailTwo-way support, invoices and GST documents, corporate gifting and bulk queries, written grievances{{support_response_sla}}{{support_resolution_sla}}
SMSOutbound transactional notification only; inbound replies are not monitored and customers are directed to an enabled two-way channelNot applicableNot applicable

Channels not listed in {{support_channels}} — including personal phone numbers or personal accounts of staff and vendor personnel — are not authorised support channels and any contact received on them must be brought into a ticket. Outbound WhatsApp messages sent outside the platform's customer service window must use an approved message template. Identity must be verified against the order record before any order detail, address or payment information is disclosed or changed. Remedies must be quoted from the governing policy, using the current configured values for {{return_request_window}}, {{live_plant_claim_window}}, {{cancellation_window}} and {{replacement_evidence_window}}, never from memory or goodwill.

Accessibility. Support is offered in English and Hindi at minimum; where an agent fluent in the customer's preferred language is unavailable, the case is handed to one who is rather than refused. Customers who cannot use WhatsApp must be served on another enabled channel, and an agent may capture a customer's account of the issue on their behalf where the customer cannot write it themselves.

Quality monitoring and satisfaction. A sample of closed tickets per agent is reviewed against the approved quality rubric at {{review_frequency_default}}, covering accuracy of the remedy, tone, verification and record quality. Recordings and transcripts are used for coaching and dispute resolution only. A satisfaction survey is sent after resolution; scores are reported with SLA attainment and reopen rate, and repeated dissatisfaction on a vendor's orders is assessed against {{vendor_quality_target}} and {{vendor_return_rate_threshold}}.

Procedures

  1. Log the contact as a ticket on receipt and link it to the order, customer and, where relevant, the vendor and shipment.
  2. Verify identity, then classify the issue (delivery, plant condition, product, payment, cancellation, account or data request) and set priority under {{incident_severity_model}}.
  3. Acknowledge within {{support_response_sla}}, stating what will happen next and by when.
  4. Collect the evidence the governing policy requires — for live plant claims, photographs within {{live_plant_claim_window}} — and record it on the ticket.
  5. Action the remedy within your authority; refunds above {{approval_limit_refund}} go to the approver, and approval is given within {{refund_approval_sla}} with payment within {{refund_processing_time}}.
  6. For vendor-fulfilled orders, raise the case to vendor operations and continue to own the customer communication yourself.
  7. Escalate on the triggers in the Customer Support Escalation Matrix rather than letting a ticket age silently.
  8. Close with the outcome, the reason and the reference number stated to the customer, then trigger the satisfaction survey.

Exceptions

Corporate gifting and bulk contracts may carry contractually agreed service terms that override the standard commitments; those terms must be recorded on the account before they are honoured. Commitments are suspended for the duration of a documented force majeure event — flood, civic disruption, courier network failure — with proactive customer notification. Cases showing indicators of fraud or claim abuse are moved to review and remedies are withheld pending that review. Abusive, threatening or discriminatory conduct toward staff or riders permits an agent to end the interaction after one clear warning and continue in writing only; the account may be restricted on management approval. Every exception is recorded on the ticket with the approver's name.

Compliance

This policy supports our obligations under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019 and the Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020, including publication of grievance contact details and a nominated grievance officer, and under the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 for personal data handled in tickets. Tax documents are issued in line with {{gst_invoice_timeline}}. Ticket records and attachments are retained for {{data_retention_period}}; customer data-rights requests are routed to the privacy owner and answered within {{dsr_response_time}}. SLA attainment, reopen rate, escalation volume and satisfaction scores are reported to management at {{review_frequency_default}}.

Violations

Failure to log a contact, disclosure of customer information without verification, promising a remedy outside approved policy, altering or deleting ticket evidence, or moving a customer conversation to an unauthorised personal channel are treated as policy violations and handled under the applicable disciplinary process. Vendor personnel who breach these requirements are addressed through the vendor agreement, including remedies under {{penalty_schedule}} and, for repeated breach, suspension of order allocation.

Related Documents

  • Customer Support Escalation Matrix
  • Returns and Refunds Policy
  • Live Plant Replacement and Claims Policy
  • Order Cancellation Policy
  • Delivery and Shipping Policy
  • Customer Data Privacy Policy
  • Vendor Partner Agreement

title: Customer Support Escalation Matrix
related_titles: Live Plant Replacement and Claims Policy
html:
DRAFT — LEGAL REVIEW REQUIRED. This document is an operational or legal draft and must be reviewed and approved by authorized management and, where required, qualified legal counsel before becoming effective.

Purpose

This matrix sets the single escalation path for PlantAtHome customer cases: who owns a case at each level, what forces it upward, what information must travel with it, and what closing it requires. It removes the two failures escalation usually suffers — a case that ages in a queue because nobody had authority to decide it, and a case handed up as a one-line complaint that the next owner has to investigate from scratch.

Scope

Applies to every customer case raised on an enabled channel under the Customer Support Policy, for directly fulfilled and vendor-fulfilled orders, hyperlocal and pan-India courier deliveries, across all verticals including FarmBox fresh produce and corporate gifting. It applies equally to cases a customer explicitly escalates and to cases the system escalates automatically. It does not govern platform outages or security incidents, which follow {{incident_severity_model}} in parallel.

Definitions

  • Escalation — transfer of decision ownership to a higher level, with the ticket remaining the single record of the case.
  • Trigger — a defined condition that requires escalation whether or not the customer asks for it.
  • Handover pack — the fixed set of facts that must accompany a case upward.
  • Owner — the named individual accountable at the current level; a role name alone is not an owner.
  • Grievance — a case a customer formally escalates in writing for statutory redressal.

Policy Statement

Escalation is a routing decision, not a punishment and not an admission. A case moves up when the current level lacks the authority, information or remedy to close it within {{escalation_timeline}}, and it moves with a complete handover pack. Customer communication is never suspended by an escalation: the customer is told the case has moved, who now owns it and when they will next hear from us. Ownership never returns downward silently.

Responsibilities

  • Level 1 — Support agent — resolve within published policy, or escalate with a complete pack before the trigger threshold is reached.
  • Level 2 — Support lead — decisions within delegated authority, cross-queue coordination and breach recovery.
  • Level 3 — Functional owner — vendor operations, delivery operations, finance or engineering, depending on where the fault sits.
  • Level 4 — Head of customer experience — cases requiring exception approval, reputational judgement or spend above delegated limits.
  • Level 5 — Grievance officer and designated partner, Silvestrix Green LLP — statutory grievances, legal notices and regulatory correspondence.

Policy Requirements

LevelTrigger conditionsOwnerTimingInformation that must pass upClosure requirement
L1All new contacts; anything resolvable within published customer policy and within {{approval_limit_refund}}Support agentFirst response within {{support_response_sla}}; resolution within {{support_resolution_sla}}Not applicable — case originates hereRemedy actioned, outcome and reason stated to the customer, survey triggered
L2{{support_resolution_sla}} at risk or breached; customer dissatisfied with the L1 outcome; remedy outside {{return_request_window}}, {{live_plant_claim_window}} or {{cancellation_window}}; second contact on the same orderSupport leadAccepted and customer updated within {{escalation_timeline}}Order and ticket reference, issue classification, evidence collected, remedy already offered and refused, exact ask of the customerDecision recorded with the policy clause or approved exception relied on
L3Fault sits outside support: vendor missed {{vendor_acceptance_sla}} or {{vendor_dispatch_sla}}; delivery failed after {{delivery_attempts}}; refund not credited within {{refund_processing_time}}; suspected payment or platform defectVendor operations, delivery operations, finance or engineering ownerAccepted and root-cause position returned within {{escalation_timeline}}L2 pack plus vendor or courier identifiers, shipment and rider or AWB references, payment reference, and the confirmed factual positionRoot cause stated, corrective action logged, ticket updated with the outcome for the customer
L4Exception beyond {{approval_limit_refund}} or {{approval_limit_expense}}; repeat failure on the same customer or vendor; corporate gifting or bulk account at risk; public or media exposureHead of customer experienceAccepted and disposition set within {{escalation_timeline}}Full case history, commercial value at stake, precedent risk, options with recommendationWritten approval or refusal of the exception, and any policy or configuration change raised for review
L5Written grievance, consumer forum or regulator correspondence, legal notice, or allegation of data misuse or personal harmGrievance officer, with designated partnerAcknowledged and progressed within {{escalation_timeline}} and applicable statutory timelinesComplete chronology, all customer correspondence, evidence set, internal decisions and their approversFormal written reply issued, record retained for {{data_retention_period}}

A case may skip levels when the trigger clearly belongs higher — a legal notice goes directly to L5, a suspected platform-wide payment failure directly to L3. Skipping is recorded on the ticket with the reason. Cases are never escalated by forwarding a message thread alone; an escalation without its handover pack is returned to the sender, and the clock continues to run against the original level.

Procedures

  1. Confirm the trigger and the level it maps to before escalating; if none applies but the case is stuck, escalate to L2 and say why.
  2. Assemble the handover pack on the ticket itself, not in a separate message.
  3. Assign the ticket to a named owner at the receiving level and record the escalation time.
  4. Tell the customer the case has been escalated, who owns it and when they will next hear from us.
  5. The receiving owner accepts or reassigns within {{escalation_timeline}}; unaccepted escalations are auto-raised to the next level.
  6. On resolution, the resolving level records the decision and the clause or approval relied on, then hands communication back to the original agent for closure unless the customer has been told otherwise.
  7. Close with outcome, reason and reference stated to the customer; a case is not closed by the customer going silent.

Exceptions

During a declared force majeure or a mass delivery disruption, affected cases may be handled as a single grouped escalation at L3 with one owner and a common customer communication, rather than individually, provided each ticket carries the group reference. Corporate gifting accounts with contracted service terms escalate directly to the named account owner at L3. Cases involving alleged staff or rider misconduct bypass L2 and go to L4 immediately. Every exception to this matrix is recorded on the ticket with the approving owner named.

Compliance

Escalation records support our obligations under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019 and the Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020 for grievance acknowledgement and redressal, and under the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 where personal data is involved. Escalation volume by level and trigger, acceptance timeliness against {{escalation_timeline}}, and repeat-escalation rate are reported to management at {{review_frequency_default}}, and escalation causes attributable to vendors are assessed against {{vendor_quality_target}} and {{vendor_return_rate_threshold}}.

Violations

Holding a case past its trigger, escalating without a handover pack, reassigning a case downward without informing the customer, closing an escalated ticket without a recorded decision, or approving a remedy above delegated authority are policy violations handled under the applicable disciplinary process. Vendor-side failures to respond to an L3 escalation are addressed under the vendor agreement, including {{penalty_schedule}} and suspension of order allocation for repeated breach.
